tools.name: animation_physics
tools.description: Author animation and physics assets: Animation Blueprints, blend spaces, montages, Control Rig/IK, skeletons, sockets, physics assets, cloth, ragdolls, and vehicles.

actorName.description: A placed actor: a prop simulates on its root when that is a physics body, else on its first static mesh; a skeletal mesh actor gets a Physics Asset for its mesh.

additive.description: Make the poses additive against pose 0, as facial and corrective poses are (default false).

additiveAnimType.description: NoAdditive (default) plays the clip as a full pose. LocalSpaceAdditive keeps only its difference from the base pose and adds that on top of whatever plays under it (a Sequencer section on another row, Apply Additive in an Animation Blueprint). MeshSpaceAdditive adds rotations in mesh space, for aim offsets; Sequencer cannot play it.

animations.description: Animation asset paths to play in this state; one Sequence Player is created per entry and the first drives the state Result pose. Without it the state is created empty and the character holds its reference pose.

artifacts.description: Canonical /Game asset paths to delete during cleanup.

assetPath.description: Animation Sequence asset path, e.g. /Game/Anims/A_Run (a montage or blend space is refused: analyze the sequences it plays).

assets.description: Canonical /Game animation asset paths to retarget.

assignToMesh.description: Make the skeletal mesh use the new asset and save the mesh too (default false).

autoMap.description: Map every unmapped chain: exact name matches first, then the closest names (default false).

automaticRule.description: Fire the transition when the source state's sequence player reaches the end of its animation instead of testing a condition. Left alone when omitted.

axis.description: Axis to change: X or Horizontal (default), Y or Vertical.

basePoseAnimation.description: Animation sequence to take the additive base pose from.

basePoseFrame.description: Frame used as the additive base pose.

basePoseType.description: What the additive difference is taken from (default RefPose): RefPose = the skeleton reference pose, AnimScaled = basePoseAnimation frame by frame, AnimFrame = one frame (basePoseFrame) of basePoseAnimation.

bidirectional.description: Whether the transition also applies from toState back to fromState. Left alone when omitted.

blendOption.description: Blend curve; left as it is when omitted.

blueprintPath.description: Animation Blueprint whose AnimGraph is edited.

bodyForAll.description: Create a body for every bone regardless of size.

bodyType.description: Shape added to the bone's body: Capsule (default), Sphere or Box; any other name is refused.

boneName.description: Shorthand for one layer filtering this bone and its children; ignored when layerSetup is sent.

boneTracks.description: Bone tracks to key: [{ boneName, frames: [{ frame, rotationDelta?: {pitch,yaw,roll}, rotation?: {pitch,yaw,roll}|{x,y,z,w}, location?: {x,y,z}, scale?: {x,y,z} }] }]. frame runs 0 to numFrames inclusive. Only the poses that matter need keys: frames between two keys of a channel are blended (rotation slerped), frames before its first key or after its last hold that key. Channels left out keep the reference pose of that bone, so a rotation-only track poses without collapsing the skeleton. Prefer rotationDelta, which bends the bone relative to its rest orientation; plain rotation replaces the local rotation outright and needs the rest orientation to already be known. Calling it again with the name of an existing clip re-keys that clip from empty (its additive settings are kept).

center.description: Physics body centre offset relative to its bone as [x, y, z].

clothAssetName.description: Name of a clothing asset already registered on the mesh.

clothAssetPath.description: Clothing asset to load and register before binding.

clothOp.description:
Which bind cloth to skeletal mesh variant to run; omit for 'bind'.
bind: Bind a cloth asset to a skeletal mesh.
assign: Assign a cloth asset to a skeletal mesh section.

conditionComparison.description: How conditionVariable is tested: greater (default), less, greater_equal, less_equal for a numeric variable; true or false for a bool.

conditionValue.description: Right-hand value for a numeric conditionComparison (default 0). Ignored for true/false.

conditionVariable.description: Animation Blueprint variable the transition rule tests, e.g. Speed or bFalling. Without it the rule graph is left unconnected, which reads as false forever and the state machine never leaves its entry state.

connectToOutput.description: Wire the blend node into the AnimGraph output pose (default true).

constraintName.description: Name of the created physics constraint.

contactHeight.description: cm above a foot's lowest point that still counts as planted (default 5).

controlType.description: add_control: the value the control drives (default transform).

createIfMissing.description: Create the curve when the sequence does not have it (default true).

crossfadeDuration.description: Transition blend duration in seconds. blendTime is accepted as an alias.

density.description: Density in g/cm3, which sets mass from volume (water is 1).

direction.description: positive_to_negative (default: the positive side is copied onto the negative side) or negative_to_positive.

dropRenderOnlyMorphs.description: The edit rebuilds the mesh from its source data, which deletes morph targets that exist only in render data (made by create_morph_target or set_morph_target_deltas). Without true, a mesh that has any is refused with RENDER_ONLY_MORPHS naming them and nothing changes (default false).

edit.description: The edit to make (each step of steps names its own).

element.description:
Which remove skeleton element variant to run.
bone: Remove boneName from a skeleton, with its children when removeChildren is true; otherwise its children move up to its parent and keep their place in the reference pose. A virtual bone is BONE_NOT_FOUND (delete_virtual_bone removes it). The only root a skeleton has is refused (CANNOT_REMOVE_ROOT); a second root is removed like any bone. One undo step (the reply's undo block says so), saved unless save is false; the reply gives boneCount.
socket: Remove a socket from a skeleton or skeletal mesh.
physics_body: Remove a physics body from a Physics Asset.

enableRootMotion.description: Move the character by the motion of the root bone instead of playing in place (default true).

endFrame.description: Last frame of the notify state range.

engine.description: Engine settings: maxRPM, maxTorque, gears (forward gear count).

feet.description: Foot bones to check (default every bone whose name holds foot but not ik, e.g. foot_l and foot_r).

forceRootLock.description: Whether root motion is force-locked to the reference pose.

friction.description: Kinetic friction, 0 (ice) to 1 and above (rubber); the engine default is 0.7.

frictionCombineMode.description: How this surface and the one it touches combine their friction: Min lets the slipperier (or deader) one win, Max the grippier (or bouncier) one; Average when not set.

from.description: connect, disconnect: the output pin, Node.Pin as get_control_rig lists it; execution runs from the event's execute pin to each unit's (ExecutePin in UE 5.8).

geomType.description: Body shape for every bone: Capsule (default; Sphyl too), Box, Sphere, TaperedCapsule (cloth only), SingleConvexHull or MultiConvexHull; any other name is refused and nothing is created.

global.description: add_bone, add_null: location, rotation and scale are in rig space, not relative to the parent.

gridDivisions.description: Number of grid divisions on the axis.

groupName.description: Slot group a new slot joins on the skeleton (default DefaultGroup). Montages in one group interrupt each other; a slot already on the skeleton keeps its group.

info.description:
Which get skeleton info variant to run; omit for 'skeleton'.
skeleton: Count what a skeleton holds (skeletonPath, or a skeletal mesh's skeleton): boneCount, virtualBoneCount and socketCount. The names come from info=bones, info=sockets and info=virtual_bones.
bones: List every bone of a skeleton (skeletonPath, or a skeletal mesh's skeleton) in hierarchy order, parents before children: name, index, parentIndex (-1 for the root), parentName and reference-pose location relative to the parent. These are the exact names layer filters, sockets, IK chains and physics bodies take.
sockets: List sockets of a skeleton.
virtual_bones: List the virtual bones declared on a skeleton.
bone_transform: Read the reference-pose transform and parent of a bone.
morph_targets: List the morph targets declared on a Skeletal Mesh.
physics_asset: Read the bodies and constraints declared by a Physics Asset.
physics_bodies: List physics bodies of a PhysicsAsset.

interpolationTime.description: Input smoothing time in seconds for every axis (0 turns smoothing off).

interpolationType.description: Input smoothing type for every axis; it only acts while interpolationTime is above 0.

kind.description:
Which create animation asset variant to run; omit for 'asset'.
asset: Create an empty Animation Sequence (assetType sequence, the default) or Montage on skeletonPath, named name in path (default /Game/Animations, made if missing), and save it. A montage starts with the DefaultSlot track and no animation. An asset of that class already at the path is reused (existingAsset); another class there is ASSET_TYPE_MISMATCH. For a sequence with a length and frame rate use kind sequence; for a montage from an animation, kind montage.
sequence: Create an Animation Sequence asset.
montage: Create a montage asset, optionally from a sequence.
blend_space: Create a 2D Blend Space for skeletonPath (required) as name in path (default /Game/Animations) and save it: horizontal axis horizontalAxisName (Direction, -180 to 180 by default), vertical verticalAxisName (Speed, 0 to 600), 4 grid divisions each; add_blend_sample places animations on it. A blend space already there is kept as it is and answered with existingAsset and the axes it has (set_axis_settings changes them); another asset there is ASSET_TYPE_MISMATCH. The reply gives assetPath and saved.
blend_space_1d: Create a 1D Blend Space for skeletonPath (required) as name in path (default /Game/Animations) and save it: one axis, axisName (Speed by default) from axisMin to axisMax (0 to 600), 4 grid divisions. A blend space already there is kept as it is and answered with existingAsset and the axis it has (set_axis_settings changes it); another asset there is ASSET_TYPE_MISMATCH. The reply gives assetPath and saved.
blend_space_2d: Create a 2D Blend Space, as kind=blend_space does: skeletonPath required, horizontal axis Direction -180 to 180 and vertical Speed 0 to 600 unless given, saved; one already there is kept and answered with existingAsset and its axes.
aim_offset: Create an Aim Offset for skeletonPath (required) as name in path (default /Game/Animations) and save it, with the axes aim offsets use: Yaw -180 to 180 and Pitch -90 to 90, 4 grid divisions each (set_axis_settings changes them). Its samples are additive rotation-offset (mesh space) poses, added with add_aim_offset_sample. A taken name is refused. The reply gives assetPath and saved.
pose_library: Create a Pose Asset from an animation sequence, one pose per key frame, on the sequence's skeleton; PoseByName and PoseBlender nodes play its poses.
procedural: Create a procedural anim asset.

layerSetup.description: One entry per blend pose, in pin order: [{ branchFilters: [{ boneName, blendDepth }] }]. A filter takes boneName and every bone under it from that blend pose over the base pose: blendDepth 0 (default) at full weight at once, N ramps the weight up over N bones down the chain (the named bone gets 1/N), and a negative depth on a bone under an earlier filter takes that branch back out (-1 removes it). Every bone must be on the Animation Blueprint's skeleton (BONE_NOT_FOUND).

length.description: Capsule length between the end caps (default 20).

limit.description: Most units to list (default 50, up to 500); matched counts them all.

limits.description: Angular limits. Only the axes named change; an angle without a motion makes that axis Limited.

oneOf.description: Bone location relative to its parent; left out, the bone keeps its own at this frame.
World or relative location as [x, y, z].
add_bone, add_null, add_control: location [x, y, z] in cm (a control's offset), relative to the parent unless global.

location.description: Bone location relative to its parent; left out, the bone keeps its own at this frame.

mass.description: Body mass in kg, above 0: sets the body's mass override (without one its mass comes from density and volume).

maxSamples.description: Frames sampled, spread evenly with the first and last always in (default 300, at most 2000; a shorter clip samples every frame).

minBoneSize.description: Bones shorter than this (cm, editor default 20) get no body unless bodyForAll.

modularRig.description: Create a Modular Rig (UE 5.5+; older engines report modularRig false).

morphTargets.description: Names to import (default all the source mesh has in its source data).

name.description: Asset name (alternative to outputPath).

node.description: One node's name: only that node, with every struct member pin by its full path.

nodeId.description: The node GUID; an alternative to nodeName.

notifyClass.description: AnimNotify (or AnimNotifyState) class name; prefixed with AnimNotify_/AnimNotifyState_ automatically when missing.

outputPath.description: Canonical /Game path for the SkeletalMesh this writes.

overwrite.description: Overwrite an existing asset with the same name.

parent.description: add_bone, add_null, add_control: the parent element's name (a bone, null or control); omitted, the top of the hierarchy.

parentClass.description: AnimInstance subclass the Blueprint derives from (default AnimInstance): a native class name or an Animation Blueprint path.

path.description: Canonical /Game output path for the created asset.

physicsAssetName.description: Name of the generated Physics Asset.

pin.description: set_pin: the pin, Node.Pin; a struct member has its own pin (SetTransform.Item.Name, SetTransform.Transform.Translation.X).

playRate.description: Speed (default 1; 2 plays it twice as fast).

poseNames.description: Distinct names for the poses in frame order; frames without a name keep the engine default name.

position.description: add_unit: graph position [x, y] (default right of the last node).

positionX.description: Graph X position of the new node (default 0).

positionY.description: Graph Y position of the new node (default 0).

priorityOrder.description: Evaluation order when several transitions out of one state can fire on the same frame; the lowest wins.

propertyName.description: The property: a member of the node's settings struct (Alpha, PlayRate, bLoopAnimation, Sequence) or of the graph node (NodeComment), with dots for a nested one (Node.PlayRate). On an asset player the asset property (Sequence, BlendSpace) is written through the node's own setter and read back, and fails when the node did not take it; any other property is written by reflection and its stored value read back.

query.description: Words to match in the unit's name, display name, category or keywords (spaces ignored), e.g. two bone, aim, set transform.

ragdoll.description:
Which setup ragdoll variant to run; omit for 'setup'.
setup: Enable runtime ragdoll physics on a skeletal actor; requires an assigned PhysicsAsset and an editor build.
activate: Switch ragdoll simulation on/off at runtime on a skeletal actor via the distinct native ragdoll=activate action (editor build).

relativeLocation.description: Socket location relative to its attach bone as [x, y, z].

relativeRotation.description: Socket rotation relative to its attach bone as [pitch, yaw, roll].

relativeScale.description: Socket scale relative to its attach bone as [x, y, z].

removeChildren.description: Whether child bones are removed with the target bone.

restitutionCombineMode.description: How this surface and the one it touches combine their bounce: Min lets the slipperier (or deader) one win, Max the grippier (or bouncier) one; Average when not set.

retargeterPath.description: An existing IK Retargeter to bake through. Omit to auto-build one by characterizing both skeletons and mapping their chains.

rootBoneName.description: Root bone name for the created skeleton.

rootMotionRootLock.description: The pose the root is locked to: RefPose (default), AnimFirstFrame or Zero, in any case; another value reads as RefPose.

oneOf.description: Bone rotation relative to its parent as [pitch, yaw, roll]; left out, the bone keeps its own at this frame.
Box or capsule rotation relative to the bone as [pitch, yaw, roll].
Rotation as [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees.
add_bone, add_null, add_control: rotation [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees.

rotation.description: Bone rotation relative to its parent as [pitch, yaw, roll]; left out, the bone keeps its own at this frame.

sampleValue.description: Sample position: a number on a 1D blend space, or {x, y} (or [x, y]) on a 2D one.

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

oneOf.description: Uniform scale factor, or non-uniform scale as [x, y, z].
Bone scale as [x, y, z]; left out, the bone keeps its own at this frame.
add_bone, add_null, add_control: scale [x, y, z] (default 1).

scale.description: Bone scale as [x, y, z]; left out, the bone keeps its own at this frame.

simulatePhysics.description: true: the body simulates whenever the mesh simulates physics (PhysicsType Default, as in a ragdoll); false: it follows the animation (Kinematic).

skeletalMeshPath.description: A skeletal mesh whose skeleton to read, instead of skeletonPath.

slotName.description: Name of the montage slot (default DefaultSlot).

socketOp.description:
Which configure socket variant to run; omit for 'configure'.
configure: Change an existing socket of a skeleton (skeletonPath; a skeletal mesh path uses its skeleton): attachBoneName moves it to another bone, and relativeLocation, relativeRotation and relativeScale replace only the parts given. A missing socket is SOCKET_NOT_FOUND, an unknown bone BONE_NOT_FOUND, and a call naming nothing to change is refused. The skeleton is saved unless save is false (saved).
add: Put a socket named socketName on attachBoneName of a skeleton (skeletonPath; a skeletal mesh path uses its skeleton), at relativeLocation, relativeRotation and relativeScale (default zero, zero and one). A bone the skeleton lacks is BONE_NOT_FOUND and a name already taken SOCKET_EXISTS. The skeleton is saved unless save is false (saved).
create: Put a socket named socketName on attachBoneName of a skeleton (skeletonPath; a skeletal mesh path uses its skeleton), at relativeLocation, relativeRotation and relativeScale (default zero, zero and one). A bone the skeleton lacks is BONE_NOT_FOUND and a name already taken SOCKET_EXISTS. The skeleton is saved unless save is false (saved).
modify: Change an existing socket of a skeleton (skeletonPath; a skeletal mesh path uses its skeleton): attachBoneName moves it to another bone, and relativeLocation, relativeRotation and relativeScale replace only the parts given. A missing socket is SOCKET_NOT_FOUND, an unknown bone BONE_NOT_FOUND, and a call naming nothing to change is refused. The skeleton is saved unless save is false (saved).

sourceAnimationPath.description: AnimSequence whose key frames become the poses; its skeleton is used.

sourceChain.description: Source IK Rig chain that drives it; empty or None clears the mapping.

sourceMesh.description: SkeletalMesh giving the source proportions. Defaults to the skeleton preview mesh, then any mesh in the project built on it.

sourceMeshPath.description: Skeletal mesh that owns the morph targets (its LOD 0 source data).

sourceSkeletalMesh.description: An already-skinned mesh on the same skeleton to copy weights from, such as the body the garment is worn over. Beats computing weights fresh wherever the garment hugs the body. Falls back to smooth binding when omitted.

startFrame.description: First frame of the notify state range.

stateMachineName.description: Target state machine name inside the Animation Blueprint.

staticFriction.description: Friction at rest, before a body starts to slide.

staticMeshPath.description: StaticMesh to skin, e.g. a coat downloaded as a rigid mesh.

steps.description: Several edits in order, each an object with edit and its own fields as above; the first that fails stops the rest, and those before it stay (failedStep names it).

suffix.description: Suffix appended to each retargeted asset name.

targetChain.description: Target IK Rig chain to map; required unless autoMap.

targetMesh.description: SkeletalMesh to retarget onto. Defaults the same way as sourceMesh.

targetMeshPath.description: Skeletal mesh whose weights are replaced in place.

targetWeightInterpolationSpeed.description: Sample weight speed per second (0 turns weight smoothing off).

threshold.description: Influences below this weight are removed, above 0 and below 0.5 (default 0.01).

to.description: connect, disconnect: the input pin, Node.Pin.

trackIndex.description: Notify track index within the animation sequence.

transitions.description: Transitions to create between the listed states, as [{ sourceState, targetState }].

transmission.description: Transmission settings: finalDrive and forward gearRatios.

treeName.description: Comment/name for the blend node (alias of name).

unit.description: add_unit: the unit, as an object path (/Script/ControlRig.RigUnit_SetTransform), its struct name with or without RigUnit_ (SetTransform), or its display name.

oneOf.description: Property value (any type).
The value: a number, boolean or string, an {x,y,z} or {r,g,b,a} object for a struct, or for an asset property the asset path (/Game/Anims/A_Idle).
set_pin: the value as text (Bone, foot_l), a number, or true/false.

vehicleType.description: Vehicle movement to set up; only a wheeled vehicle is supported (default WheeledVehicle4W).

weights.description: Per-vertex skin weight descriptors with bone influences.

wheels.description: Wheel setups, replacing the existing ones: [{ boneName, offset {x,y,z}, radius, width, friction }].

tools.name: build_environment
tools.description: Build environments: landscapes, foliage, procedural terrain/biomes, lighting setups, spline roads/rivers/fences, and world decoration.

actorName.description: Actor name in the current level.

amount.description: Bloom intensity, 0 or more (0.675 by default; 8 is the top of the editor slider).

amplitude.description: Same as waveHeight; waveHeight wins when both are given.

area.description: A box min..max. Painting: instances spread evenly over min..max in X and Y, and each drops onto the ground found between 500 above max.z and 1000 below min.z. Removing: only the instances whose location lies inside min..max on all three axes (a pit or a path), every type unless foliageType names one.

items.description: A box min..max. Painting: instances spread evenly over min..max in X and Y, and each drops onto the ground found between 500 above max.z and 1000 below min.z. Removing: only the instances whose location lies inside min..max on all three axes (a pit or a path), every type unless foliageType names one.

areas.description: Several area boxes at once, each {min, max}: every instance inside any of them is removed under one consent (every type unless foliageType names one).

assetPath.description: Canonical /Game static mesh path (one asset; assetPaths takes several).

azimuth.description: Sun azimuth in degrees: the yaw of the light.

bClosedLoop.description: Whether the spline is a closed loop.

bounces.description: Lightmass indirect lighting bounces (World Settings), used by baked lighting.

bounds.description: The area {location, size}: a box of size (default 1000 on each axis) centred on location (default the origin); it must enclose a surface to place on.

captureOffset.description: Offset in cm from the capture actor.

captureSource.description: What the capture renders: FinalColorLDR, SceneColorHDR, SceneDepth, BaseColor, Normal or an SCS_ value. Required.

channelTarget.description:
Which set light channel variant to run; omit for 'light'.
light: Turn lighting channels on or off for a light actor.
actor: Turn lighting channels on or off for a target actor's primitives.

closedLoop.description: Close the spline into a loop, joining the last point back to the first.

collisionEnabled.description: Collision of placed instances: true = query and physics, false = none.

color.description: Light color {r, g, b, a}. Linear 0-1 channels, stored by the engine as the 8-bit sRGB color: {r: 1, g: 0.7, b: 0.42} reads back as (255, 218, 173). A missing channel reads 0 (alpha 1). properties.color wins over it.

compensationValue.description: Exposure bias in stops (+1 is twice as bright).

count.description: How many instances to place over the brush disc (location + radius) or the area; overrides density.

cubemapPath.description: Cube texture the sky light uses (switches its source to a specified cubemap); a path that does not load fails the call.

curvePath.description: The curve asset to edit, created there when missing (default /Game/Environment/Curves/MCP_SkyColorCurve or MCP_LightColorCurve).

density.description: Fog density, the height fog's FogDensity (0.02 a light haze, 0.05 and up a thick fog).

oneOf.description: Direction rotation.
Wind direction: its yaw sets where the waves travel.

directionalLightActorPath.description: Directional light actor path. As input, selects the light to snapshot; the first directional light in the level is used when omitted. As output, the resolved actor path.

distance.description: Focal distance in cm, 0 or more.

edit.description:
Which edit landscape variant to run.
paint_landscape: Paint a landscape layer (layerName) at strength over a brush disc (location + radius), a vertex region, or the whole landscape. The edit goes into the landscape's edit layer (the one being edited in Landscape mode, else the first; other layers still add on top), is one undo step (undo), and the layers are merged before the reply, so the drawn landscape and its collision show it.
paint_landscape_layer: Paint a landscape layer (layerName) at one weight (strength) over a vertex region, or the whole landscape. The edit goes into the landscape's edit layer (the one being edited in Landscape mode, else the first; other layers still add on top), is one undo step (undo), and the layers are merged before the reply, so the drawn landscape and its collision show it.
import_heightmap: Write a raw 16-bit heightmap file (heightmapPath, project-relative, no header, machine byte order, as export_heightmap writes it) into a landscape's heights, over its whole extent or region; the file must hold at least one sample per vertex of that area, row by row. The edit goes into the landscape's edit layer (the one being edited in Landscape mode, else the first; other layers still add on top), is one undo step (undo), and the layers are merged before the reply, so the drawn landscape and its collision show it.
configure_landscape_lod: Tune how a landscape lowers its detail with distance: settings sets its LOD properties by name, such as LOD0ScreenSize (where full detail ends, default 0.5), LOD0DistributionSetting (default 1.25) and LODDistributionSetting (the spacing of the other LODs, default 3; higher keeps detail farther), MaxLODLevel (-1 for no cap) and StaticLightingLOD; from UE 5.4 also bUseScalableLODSettings with the per-quality Scalable versions and LODBlendRange. It is one undo step, reaches the landscape's World Partition streaming proxies as an edit in the Details panel does, and reads back what was set (values). Nothing set is NO_SETTING_SUPPLIED; an unknown or bad value is CONFIGURATION_FAILED, listed in configurationErrors.
configure_landscape_material: Assign the material a landscape renders with (materialPath: a material or material instance; its layer blend nodes name the layers that can be painted), as one undo step. A path outside the project is refused, one that loads nothing is ASSET_NOT_FOUND and another kind of asset LOAD_FAILED. The reply gives landscapeName and landscapePath. Painting a layer creates its layer info when the landscape has none.
configure_landscape_splines: Replace a landscape's splines with one through the given points (width, loop, terrain deform, painted layer).
generate_lods: Give static mesh assets (foliage meshes included) numLODs LODs in all (default 4, LOD 0 included): each LOD keeps half the triangles of the one before, LODs past the count and hand-tuned LOD settings are replaced, and each mesh is rebuilt and saved. Engine meshes are not changed (engineContentPaths; ENGINE_CONTENT when nothing else was given): duplicate one into /Game first. The reply counts processed out of requested and lists notFoundPaths and notMeshPaths.

elevation.description: Sun elevation: degrees above the horizon (90 = overhead, negative = below it).

enabled.description: Indirect lighting cache on (point sampled) or off for each primitive.

feature.description:
Which configure ray tracing variant to run.
ao: Turn ray-traced ambient occlusion on or off (r.RayTracing.AmbientOcclusion) and set its intensity and radius. Values are set as a console command would set them (console_command and this call replace each other, last one wins) and last for this editor session, not saved to the project. With hardware ray tracing off for the project (r.RayTracing 0, fixed at startup) they are stored, draw nothing, and the reply warns (rayTracingEnabled false). A variable that did not take is listed under unsupportedCVars with why: missing in this engine version, read-only, or reset by the engine; refused with CVAR_UNAVAILABLE when none took.
gi: Turn ray-traced global illumination on or off (r.RayTracing.GlobalIllumination) and set its samples and bounces. Values are set as a console command would set them (console_command and this call replace each other, last one wins) and last for this editor session, not saved to the project. With hardware ray tracing off for the project (r.RayTracing 0, fixed at startup) they are stored, draw nothing, and the reply warns (rayTracingEnabled false). A variable that did not take is listed under unsupportedCVars with why: missing in this engine version, read-only, or reset by the engine; refused with CVAR_UNAVAILABLE when none took.
reflections: Turn ray-traced reflections on or off (r.RayTracing.Reflections) and set their samples and roughness cutoff. Values are set as a console command would set them (console_command and this call replace each other, last one wins) and last for this editor session, not saved to the project. With hardware ray tracing off for the project (r.RayTracing 0, fixed at startup) they are stored, draw nothing, and the reply warns (rayTracingEnabled false). A variable that did not take is listed under unsupportedCVars with why: missing in this engine version, read-only, or reset by the engine; refused with CVAR_UNAVAILABLE when none took.
shadows: Turn ray-traced shadows on or off (r.RayTracing.Shadows) and set their samples per pixel. Values are set as a console command would set them (console_command and this call replace each other, last one wins) and last for this editor session, not saved to the project. With hardware ray tracing off for the project (r.RayTracing 0, fixed at startup) they are stored, draw nothing, and the reply warns (rayTracingEnabled false). A variable that did not take is listed under unsupportedCVars with why: missing in this engine version, read-only, or reset by the engine; refused with CVAR_UNAVAILABLE when none took.
path_tracing: Set the path tracer's samples per pixel and bounces. Its switch r.PathTracing is read-only, fixed at startup by the project's config, so enabled cannot turn it on or off here (the reply lists it under unsupportedCVars); to see the path tracer, set_view_mode PathTracing. Values are set as a console command would set them (console_command and this call replace each other, last one wins) and last for this editor session, not saved to the project. With hardware ray tracing off for the project (r.RayTracing 0, fixed at startup) they are stored, draw nothing, and the reply warns (rayTracingEnabled false). A variable that did not take is listed under unsupportedCVars with why: missing in this engine version, read-only, or reset by the engine; refused with CVAR_UNAVAILABLE when none took.

foliageOp.description:
Which add foliage variant to run; omit for 'scatter'.
scatter: Add foliage: with only meshPath (+ name) create or update a foliage type asset; with a foliage type or a placement (locations, position, location + radius + count) scatter instances onto the ground, a bare meshPath standing in for its auto foliage type.
instances: Add explicit foliage instances: full transforms, or bare locations varied by minScale/maxScale/randomYaw. One undo step removes them all; the reply's undo block says so.
paint: Paint foliage over a brush disc (location + radius) or a box area: count instances dropped onto the ground, each with a random scale and yaw. One undo step removes the whole stroke; NO_SURFACE (no ground below any point) adds nothing.

items.description: Foliage type with mesh and density.

foliageTypes.description: At least one {meshPath, density}: the static mesh to scatter and its density, the seeds per 10 m x 10 m the simulation starts from (default 10). Its steps then spread, age and thin them (instances keep a collision radius apart), so the count placed differs; get_foliage_instances reads it.

forwardAxis.description: Mesh axis laid along the spline: X (the default), Y or Z, any case; another name is refused.

height.description: Height in world units, over 0 (default 300 for a wall, 100 for a fence); the mesh's bottom stands on the route. With meshPath, omit it to keep the mesh's own height.

heightData.description: Raw heights, 0-65535: 32768 sits at the landscape's own Z and 128 units are one landscape Z-scale step (ScaleZ cm). set takes one for the whole region or one per vertex; flatten takes the first (default 32768).

index.description: Insert the point before this index; appended when omitted or out of range.

indirectLightingIntensity.description: Indirect lighting intensity, written with its override on the level's post-process volume (spawned when missing).

infiniteUnbound.description: Whether the volume is infinite and unbound.

items.description: Spline point with a world location.

keys.description: Color keys that replace the curve's keys; required to change an existing curve. A new curve without keys is flat white.

time.description: Key time, e.g. the hour of day.

color.description: Color {r, g, b, a}; a defaults to 1.

kind.description:
Which create atmosphere actor variant to run.
sky_sphere: Create the sky lighting rig in the level being edited: a Sky Atmosphere, a sun (Directional Light) and a Sky Light, labelled <name>_Atmosphere, <name>_Sun and <name>_SkyLight (SkyAtmosphere, DirectionalLight and SkyLight without a name). An actor already carrying one of those labels is reused and set up rather than doubled, but a sun or atmosphere labelled otherwise is not found, so the level gets a second one. No sky sphere mesh, clouds or fog: add those with configure_volumetric_cloud and kind=fog_volume. Replies createdActorCount (0 when all three existed) and the three actor names.
fog_volume: Create an Exponential Height Fog actor in the level being edited, or set up the one already labelled name (default ExponentialHeightFog), with density and settings (properties of its fog component). It is height fog over the whole level, not a local volume, and a fog labelled otherwise is not found, so the level gets a second one.
time_of_day_system: Create one actor, TimeOfDaySystem (or name), carrying its own sun (a directional light at intensity 10, the atmosphere sun), sky light (intensity 1) and sky atmosphere, all movable, with the sun at noon; an actor already labelled so gets the missing parts. Nothing animates it, no curves and no day cycle: move the sun with set_time_of_day. A level that already has a sun or sky atmosphere (kind=sky_sphere, the default level template) ends up with two of each, so use one rig or the other.

landscapeActorPath.description: Landscape actor path in the level.

layerInfoPath.description: Layer info asset to use when the landscape has no layer of that name yet (else one lives only inside the landscape).

levelName.description: Level name; appended when path is a folder.

lightClass.description: Light class name or path, for a class lightType does not name, including a Blueprint light (/Game/Lights/BP_Lamp.BP_Lamp_C); build_environment list_light_types lists the loaded ones. Wins over lightType.

lightType.description: Light kind: point, spot, directional, rect or sky (any case), or the class name PointLight, SpotLight, DirectionalLight, RectLight or SkyLight. A light class of your own goes in lightClass.

limit.description: Return at most this many instances; truncated says when more exist (count stays the total).

oneOf.description: World-space location {x, y, z}.
Brush centre in world space; paints the disc of radius around it (radius required).
Proxy location (default the landscape's).
Where the actor is spawned when it does not exist yet; an existing actor is not moved.
Where the actor is spawned when the level has none; an existing actor is not moved.
World location {x, y, z}; 0, 0, 300 when omitted.
World-space location {x, y, z}.

location.description: Brush centre in world space; paints the disc of radius around it (radius required).

lowerTerrain.description: Whether the spline lowers the terrain down to it (default true).

material.description: Material for the terrain; a path that does not load fails the call.

maxBrightness.description: Highest auto exposure (EV100 with the extended luminance range).

method.description: Auto-exposure method written on the post-process volume.

minBrightness.description: Lowest auto exposure (EV100 with the extended luminance range).

name.description: Label of the terrain actor (default ProceduralTerrain; actorName is accepted too).

noWeightBlend.description: Disable weight blending for the landscape layer.

operation.description: set (default), raise (add), lower (subtract), flatten or smooth.

outputPath.description: Filesystem path the heightmap is written to.

pointType.description: Spline point type (Linear, Curve, Constant, etc.).

oneOf.description: Spline points.

items.description: Spline point with position and tangent.
Spline point with position and tangent.

oneOf.description: Spline points.
Point position relative to the spline actor {x, y, z}: its local space, the location get_splines_info with actorName reports (worldLocation is where the point lies in the level).
Position {x, y, z}.

position.description: Point position relative to the spline actor {x, y, z}: its local space, the location get_splines_info with actorName reports (worldLocation is where the point lies in the level).

properties.description: Light component settings, applied to the lights they fit; the reply lists what went in as details.applied, what did not as details.refused ("name: why") and any value replaced for being out of range as details.adjusted. Keys: intensity (0 or more; a negative reads 0), color (as above), castShadows (true or false), useAsAtmosphereSunLight (true or false; a directional light given properties is the atmosphere sun unless this says false), attenuationRadius (above 0, point and spot lights; an invalid value reads 1000), innerConeAngle and outerConeAngle (0 to 180 degrees, spot lights; clamped), sourceWidth and sourceHeight (above 0, rect lights; an invalid value reads 100). A sky light takes only the top-level intensity and color. Any other key, or one that does not fit the light, is refused by name.

quadsPerSection.description: Quads per section: 7, 15, 31, 63 (default), 127 or 255. A component spans sectionsPerComponent sections.

quality.description: Ambient occlusion quality on the post-process volume (25, 50 or 100 of 100).

radius.description: Ambient occlusion radius in world units.

raiseTerrain.description: Whether the spline raises the terrain up to it (default true).

rayTracedShadows.description: Whether ray-traced shadows are enabled (r.RayTracing.Shadows). Distinct from virtualShadowMaps.

recapture.description: Recapture the sky light after the change.

resolution.description: Width and height in pixels, 1 to 4096.

oneOf.description: Actor rotation, applied on every call.
Proxy rotation (default the landscape's).
Rotation {pitch, yaw, roll} in degrees. A spot or directional light shines along its forward axis, so pitch -90 points it straight down.
Rotation {pitch, yaw, roll}.
Water body rotation, applied on every call.

rotation.description: Actor rotation, applied on every call.

save.description: Whether to save after the operation.

saveToProject.description: Also write the method to Project Settings > Rendering (DefaultEngine.ini), so it survives an editor restart and reaches the packaged game (default false: this session only).

sculptOp.description:
Which sculpt variant to run; omit for 'sculpt'.
sculpt: Sculpt a landscape at location (world space) with a round brush: tool Raise (default) or Lower moves the ground strength x 100 cm at the brush centre (strength default 0.1), Flatten pulls it toward location.z by the strength fraction. radius is in world units (default 1000) and falloff (default 0.5) is the outer share of it that fades out. modifiedVertices counts the vertices that moved (0 when all were clamped); an unknown tool, or a location off the landscape (OUT_OF_BOUNDS), is refused. The edit goes into the landscape's edit layer (the one being edited in Landscape mode, else the first; other layers still add on top), is one undo step (undo), and the layers are merged before the reply, so the drawn landscape and its collision show it.
heightmap: Change a landscape's heights over a region of its vertices (minX..maxX and minY..maxY, or region; default the whole landscape) by operation: set (default) writes heightData raw heights, one for the whole region or one per vertex row by row; raise and lower (add, subtract) move it by amount cm; flatten sets it to heightData[0]; smooth runs one 3x3 averaging pass. An unknown operation, a heightData count that fits neither form, or raise/lower without amount is refused; modifiedVertices counts the vertices that changed. The edit goes into the landscape's edit layer (the one being edited in Landscape mode, else the first; other layers still add on top), is one undo step (undo), and the layers are merged before the reply, so the drawn landscape and its collision show it.
material: Set the material a landscape renders with, in one undo step: materialPath must load as a material or material instance (ASSET_NOT_FOUND when nothing is there, LOAD_FAILED for another asset type). paint_landscape_layer then paints the layers its Landscape Layer Blend names.

sectionSize.description: Quads per section (same as quadsPerSection): 7, 15, 31, 63 (default), 127 or 255.

sectionsPerComponent.description: Sections per component side: 1 (default) or 2, for 2x2 sections per component.

seed.description: Random seed of the scatter (default 12345); the same seed gives the same placement.

setting.description:
Which configure atmosphere variant to run.
sky_atmosphere: Configure sky atmosphere settings.
sky_light: Configure sky light intensity and cubemap.
sun_position: Configure sun azimuth and elevation (or an hour of day) on the level's sun.
directional_light: Configure a directional light: its angle (azimuth, elevation above the horizon), intensity, and any light property such as LightColor through settings.
height_fog: Configure exponential height fog settings.
volumetric_cloud: Configure volumetric cloud settings.
time_of_day: Set the time of day: the hour sets the sun's elevation (azimuth and elevation may be given directly).
sky_color_curve: Set the color keys of a sky color curve asset (made at curvePath when missing) for time-of-day.
light_color_curve: Set the color keys of a light color curve asset (made at curvePath when missing) for time-of-day.

oneOf.description: Console values by key, only these (any other key is refused and nothing is set): Radius (0-10000 world units).
Action-specific settings key-value pairs.

FPostProcessSettings fields by engine name, e.g. {"ColorSaturation": {"x": 1.1, "y": 1.1, "z": 1.1, "w": 1}, "VignetteIntensity": 0.3}; each field's bOverride_ flag is set for you. A key that is not a field is listed under unsupportedSettings, and when no key is one the call fails naming the closest fields.
Landscape properties by name, e.g. {"MaxLODLevel": 2, "LODDistributionSetting": 1.5}.

Property values for the actor or its component, keyed by the Unreal property name (case-insensitive): {"Intensity": 2, "LightColor": {"R": 0.6, "G": 0.7, "B": 1}} for a light, {"FogDensity": 0.02} for fog. A key neither declares is named in configurationErrors and fails the call.
Reflection capture component properties by name, e.g. {"Brightness": 1.5}.
The same shadow keys as the top level, nested; a value here wins.

shadowBias.description: Shadow depth bias of the light (actorName).

shadowQuality.description: Shadow quality scalability level (sg.ShadowQuality): Low, Medium, High, Epic or Cinematic.

shadowResolutionScale.description: Shadow resolution scale of the light (actorName).

shadowSlopeBias.description: Shadow slope bias of the light (actorName).

size.description: Box size in world units {x, y, z} (default 1000 on each axis).

sizeX.description: Landscape size along X, in vertices like the editor Overall Resolution (1009 is 16 components of 63 quads) or in quads; it becomes the fewest whole components that cover it.

sizeY.description: Landscape size along Y, in vertices like the editor Overall Resolution (1009 is 16 components of 63 quads) or in quads; it becomes the fewest whole components that cover it.

skipFlush.description: Do not wait for the GPU (default false): the upload and the edit layer merge finish on a later editor tick, so read heights, paint or collision back only after that. Faster for many edits in a row.

skyLightActorPath.description: Sky light actor path. As input, selects the light to snapshot; the first sky light in the level is used when omitted. As output, the resolved actor path.

skyLightOp.description:
Which create sky light variant to run; omit for 'create'.
create: Create a sky light actor, capturing the scene or lighting from a cubemap.
ensure_single: Make sure the edited level has exactly one sky light: spawn one when it has none, relabel the only one; with several, refuse and name the ones to delete.

snapToSurface.description: Drop each point onto the first static surface below it (default true). Points with no surface below - over a pit or off the level - are skipped and reported as skippedNoSurface.

splineType.description: Point type for every point: Linear, Curve (default), Constant, CurveClamped or CurveCustomTangent.

steepness.description: Crest sharpness of the short waves, 0 (smooth swell) to 1 (peaked); the long waves take about half. Keep it under about 0.3: steep crests from many waves fold the surface over itself.

summary.description: Count only: byType and count, no instance list. A level-wide listing runs to tens of KB.

targetActor.description: Target actor name for the operation.

threshold.description: Brightness a pixel needs to bloom: -1 (the default) blooms everything, 0 or more only brighter pixels.

tileSize.description: Side of one simulated tile in world units (default 1000); the scatter repeats 10 unique tiles across the area.

tool.description: Sculpt tool: Raise (default), Lower or Flatten (towards the location's z). Any other name is refused.

useRandomOffset.description: Apply a random offset to scattered meshes.

viewDistance.description: Volumetric fog view distance in world units.

virtualShadowMaps.description: Whether virtual shadow maps are enabled. Distinct from rayTracedShadows.

volumeName.description: Label of the procedural foliage volume (name is accepted too).

waveHeight.description: Height (amplitude) of the largest wave in cm; the body's other waves shrink to 15% of it, as a real sea's do. A calm harbour is about 5-10, open sea 50 or more.

waveLength.description: Wavelength of the longest wave in cm, crest to crest; the shortest waves are 13% of it (a harbour is about 1500-2500).

width.description: Size across the route in world units, over 0: a road or river slab's width (default 400), a wall's or fence's thickness (default 20 / 10), a pipe's or cable's diameter (default 50 / 4). With meshPath, omit it to keep the mesh's own width.

tools.name: control_actor
tools.description: Spawn actors, set transforms, enable physics, add components, manage tags, and attach actors.

actorClass.description: Alias of classPath accepted by the spawn handler (normalizeArgs alias).

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

oneOf.description: Actor names to act on (batch delete).

Only these actors may move, by the names audit_placement reports. Names not found come back under missing; what they intersect stays put and they are pushed off it. A floor, a locked or an attached actor among them is listed under skipped with the reason.

Report only the relations these actors take part in, as subject or object, and the patterns they belong to; the rest of the level is still judged, so a lamp still rests on a table nobody named. Names not found come back under missing; when none is found the call fails with ACTOR_NOT_FOUND.

Several actors to change in one call and one undo step, in place of actorName; names not found are listed back under missing, and the actors changed under affectedActors (which the receipt lists as changes, with an actor handle each).

Several actors to give the same material in one call and one undo step, in place of actorName; each is reported under results, and the actors changed under affectedActors (which the receipt lists as changes, with an actor handle each); the call fails naming any that did not take it.
Several actors to move in one call and one undo step, in place of actorName; names not found are listed back under missing, and the actors moved under affectedActors.

Several actors to show or hide in one call and one undo step, in place of actorName; names not found are listed back under missing, and the actors changed under affectedActors (which the receipt lists as changes, with an actor handle each).

Several actors to tag in one call and one undo step, in place of actorName; names not found are listed back under missing, and the actors tagged under affectedActors (which the receipt lists as changes, with an actor handle each).

Several actors whose component of componentName takes the same properties in one call and one undo step, in place of actorName (a row of point lights, each LightComponent0). The actors changed are counted in updatedActors and listed under affectedActors (which the receipt lists as changes), names that matched no actor come back in missing, and an actor whose component did not take everything is a results row {actorName, error} that fails the call PARTIAL_FAILURE.

The actors that may move; omit to move every relation's left-hand actor. A floor or landscape, an actor with Lock Actor Movement and an attached actor never move: they come back under skipped with the reason. What is not named stays put and is kept clear of.
Many actors given the same change: the location, offset, rotation or scale beside it (forty frost caps rescaled by one scale, a group raised by one offset). Reported as actors is.

The actors to settle, by exact name (1-64). Each needs a root that is a body with physics collision (a static mesh with simple collision: the engine cubes and most props); a floor or landscape, an actor with Lock Actor Movement, an attached actor, or one whose root is no body comes back under skipped with the reason and stays put. A name that matches no actor refuses with ACTOR_NOT_FOUND (missing lists them); when none of them can fall it refuses with NOTHING_TO_SETTLE. Everything else in the level takes part in the simulation as it is (static actors are what the bodies land on).

actorNames.description: Actor names to act on (batch delete).

oneOf.description: Actors to spawn, 1-500. Each is a spawn payload: classPath, blueprintPath or meshPath, plus actorName, location, rotation, scale ([x, y, z] arrays). Optional per item: materialPath (applied like set_material; componentName/materialSlot/allComponents narrow it), variables ({name: value} Blueprint variables set on the new instance, like set_blueprint_variables; in a running game they are set before its BeginPlay, so it starts with them), properties ({name: value} set on the root component, or on componentName's, as edit_component sets them: a light's Intensity, LightColor and AttenuationRadius), folder (outliner folder path), tags (actor tags; delete_by_tag removes the batch again), repeat ({count, offset [x, y, z], rows, rowOffset [x, y, z]}: count x rows copies of the item, each moved from its location by offset per copy and rowOffset per row, actorName numbered _1, _2, ...; a row of racks, a grid of lights; at most 1000 actors once unrolled). Items that fail are reported; the rest still spawn. Parts meant to hang in the air or sit inside another (ceiling ducts, lights, a flange on a pipe) take the tag mcp.placement.ok (defaults.tags covers the whole batch), so the reply keeps only what needs fixing.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

location.description: World or relative location as [x, y, z].

offset.description: Move by [dx, dy, dz] from where the actor stands now, instead of to an absolute location; give one or the other.

rotation.description: Rotation as [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees.

oneOf.description: Many actors in one call, each {actorName, location? or offset?, rotation?, scale?} with its own values; a part an item leaves out takes the call's own location, offset, rotation or scale when given, else keeps its current value. Every actor is reported, and the call fails naming any that did not move.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

variables.description: Blueprint variable name to value map. An actor variable, or an array of them, takes each actor by its label or name as list shows it ("Door_1", ["Fire_1", "Fire_2"]) or by its object path.

oneOf.description: Many actors in one call, each {actorName, variables} with its own values; every actor is reported, the actors that took a variable come back under affectedActors (which the receipt lists as changes, with an actor handle each), and the call fails naming any that did not take all of its variables.

actors.description: Actors to spawn, 1-500. Each is a spawn payload: classPath, blueprintPath or meshPath, plus actorName, location, rotation, scale ([x, y, z] arrays). Optional per item: materialPath (applied like set_material; componentName/materialSlot/allComponents narrow it), variables ({name: value} Blueprint variables set on the new instance, like set_blueprint_variables; in a running game they are set before its BeginPlay, so it starts with them), properties ({name: value} set on the root component, or on componentName's, as edit_component sets them: a light's Intensity, LightColor and AttenuationRadius), folder (outliner folder path), tags (actor tags; delete_by_tag removes the batch again), repeat ({count, offset [x, y, z], rows, rowOffset [x, y, z]}: count x rows copies of the item, each moved from its location by offset per copy and rowOffset per row, actorName numbered _1, _2, ...; a row of racks, a grid of lights; at most 1000 actors once unrolled). Items that fail are reported; the rest still spawn. Parts meant to hang in the air or sit inside another (ceiling ducts, lights, a flange on a pipe) take the tag mcp.placement.ok (defaults.tags covers the whole batch), so the reply keeps only what needs fixing.

allComponents.description: When true, apply the material to all mesh components.

blueprintPath.description: Audit the mesh parts of this actor Blueprint instead of the level: a preview instance (the level is untouched) has every visible static mesh part measured against every other and against its ground (a Character's capsule bottom). problems[] then lists componentName, kind (buried: inside otherComponent; sunk: below the ground), depth and severity in cm, insideShare and the issue; minSeverity is the tolerance (default 0.5 cm), and kinds, nameFilter and maxTilt are refused (INVALID_ARGUMENT). A part tagged mcp.placement.ok in its ComponentTags is a deliberate embed (an eyeball in its socket) and is left out; mcp.placement.ok:<component> accepts the embed in that one part only and keeps every other check. Blueprint component edits report the same for the parts they touch, as partWarnings.

center.description: With radius: judge only the actors whose bounds come within radius cm of this point (named actors always count). Refused without radius.

class.description: Unreal class name or path (alias of className).

className.description: Only actors of this class or a subclass, by name or path: TextRenderActor, Light (every light type), or a Blueprint such as BP_Sign, with or without _C.

classPath.description: Unreal class path (e.g. /Script/Engine.PointLight or /Game/Enemies/BP_Enemy) of the actors to find (alias of className).

collisionEnabled.description: Turn collision on (true) or off (false). Omitted with profile or responses, the mode stays as the preset sets it.

componentName.description: Call the function on this component of the actor instead of on the actor itself (refused with COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND when the actor has none of that name).

componentNames.description: Return only these components, by name (case-insensitive); a name that matches none is listed under missingComponents.

contactCm.description: With groundTrace: how far above its own lowest height a point still counts as planted (default 2 cm), so an ankle bone that never reaches the floor still counts as down when the foot is.

defaults.description: Fields shared by every item (e.g. meshPath, materialPath, folder, tags); an item's own fields win.

deleteScope.description:
Which delete variant to run; omit for 'actors'.
actors: Permanently delete one actor or a batch of actors by name.
by_tag: Permanently delete every actor matching a gameplay tag, or any of several tags in one call.

distance.description: How far each face moves, in world units (0.1-20, default 1): far enough for the depth buffer, too little to see.

dryRun.description: List the first round of moves without making them (default false).

durationSeconds.description: Game seconds to watch (default 2, at most 30). Game time, so a clock slowed with set_game_speed still covers the same span of play; a run that needs more wall-clock time than maxRealSeconds stops there (endedBecause realTimeCap).

edit.description:
Which edit component variant to run.
add: Add a new component of a given type to an actor. If any requested property (or meshPath) does not apply, the call fails naming what did not, although the component was added.
remove: Remove a component that was added to this actor (edit=add, or by hand in the editor), by its exact name, in one undo step, leaving the level unsaved. A near miss is refused with COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND naming the closest component; a component of the actor class or its Blueprint, or the root, is refused with COMPONENT_NOT_REMOVABLE (a Blueprint one comes out with edit_scs).
set_property: Set one or more properties on a named actor component. For RelativeScale3D/RelativeLocation, note that a child inherits its parent's scale: Unreal multiplies parent and child scale COMPONENT-WISE in the child's own local axes, and rotation does NOT permute which axis each factor lands on. World size = ParentScale * ChildScale * MeshExtent per local axis, and world offset = ParentScale * RelativeLocation. Under a parent scaled non-uniformly, divide the offset you want by the parent scale on that axis.
set_properties: Alias of edit=set_property. The bridge dispatches both names to the same handler.

fallCm.description: A body that ends more than this many cm below its START height fell (10-100000, default 500), measured from where it started, not from the floor: its old pose is kept rather than one under the floor, and it is listed under unstable. Dropping props from higher than 5 m onto the floor needs a larger fallCm.

filter.description: Optional name substring filter for list.

findBy.description:
Which find variant to run.
class: Find the actors in the level of a class or any subclass of it (a short native name such as PointLight, /Script/Engine.PointLight, or a Blueprint asset path), each with name and path: the first limit (default 200), with truncated and totalCount when more match. A class that resolves to nothing is refused with CLASS_NOT_FOUND, naming assets of that name.
name: Find the actors in the level whose label, object name or path contains a query (case-insensitive; a full object path is cut to its actor name), each with label, name, path and class: the first limit (default 200), with truncated and totalCount when more match. With no match, similar offers labels that match once case, separators and leading zeros are ignored.
mesh: Find the actors in the level that draw a static mesh (instanced and foliage components included), each with the components that do.
material: Find the actors in the level with a component that uses a material in any slot, as an override or as its mesh's default, each with the components and slots that do.

folder.description: Only actors in this outliner folder or a folder under it (Level/Stage matches Level/Stage/Signs); "(none)" for the actors at the root.

force.description: The push as [x, y, z], applied once as an impulse in kg cm/s: a 100 kg crate given [30000, 0, 0] starts at 300 cm/s along X. A body that does not simulate is made to, in the running game only.

groundTrace.description: With points: each sample's aboveGround gives each point's height over the first surface below it that blocks Visibility (the actor and what is attached to it ignored), negative when the point is inside that surface, and pointStats sums up its contact.

info.description:
Which get components variant to run; omit for 'components'.
components: List all components attached to an actor with their relative transforms.
bounds: Read the world-space bounding box of an actor; normalizes to get_bounding_box.

key.description: Key name as simulate_input takes it: SpaceBar, D, A, Left, Enter.

atSeconds.description: Game seconds after the run starts to press it (default 0).

inputs.description: Keys pressed and released at exact game times during the run (at most 32), e.g. [{"key":"D","atSeconds":0,"holdSeconds":2},{"key":"SpaceBar","atSeconds":0.6,"holdSeconds":0.2}]. A key still held when the run ends is released.

intervalSeconds.description: Game seconds between samples (default 0.05; 0 samples every frame). At most 400 samples are kept.

oneOf.description: Which relations and patterns to report: on (rests on the actor under it; read from short traces down from its bottom, so an actor without collision rests on nothing), mounted (held from the side, as a picture on a wall), inside (within another's bounds, the tightest such), nextTo (side by side, their sides within 2 cm, judged on boxes turned with the actors), faces (the line ahead of its front, its X axis, meets the nearest actor that is not a copy of it, or points within 20 degrees of the centre of that actor; a prop without a front, such as a crate or a table, faces whatever lies along its X axis), groups, rows (with grids), rings and roles. Omit for all of them but faces, which is listed only when kinds names it or actorNames or nameFilter narrow the report: across a whole level it would name a front for most props.

Report only these problem kinds, e.g. ["coplanar"] to list z-fighting alone in a platformer full of platforms that float on purpose. default_material: a visible mesh slot drawing the engine's default grid (no material, or one made from it). placeholder_text: a text render still reading the engine default "Text" (give it its label, or an empty text when a script writes it in play). duplicate: an actor that is a copy of another in the same place with the same meshes, drawn twice. An actor whose worst problem is another kind still counts for these, as for coplanar, when its contentIssues hold them. An actor whose worst problem is another kind still counts for coplanar when it has coplanarFaces. An actor whose bounds touch or overlap another actor's vertical face (a window band on a hall, an awning on a facade) is mounted, never floating or unsupported. Two faces pointing down with something solid right below them (pieces lying on a floor) are not reported as coplanar: no camera sees them. Omit for every kind.

What to fix, as audit_placement names it: sunk (moved up by its depth, onto the surface under it), floating (moved down by its clearance onto that surface; mounted actors, held from the side, are never floating), overlapping (pushed out of the actors it intersects). Required: every kind can be deliberate.

kinds.description: Report only these problem kinds, e.g. ["coplanar"] to list z-fighting alone in a platformer full of platforms that float on purpose. default_material: a visible mesh slot drawing the engine's default grid (no material, or one made from it). placeholder_text: a text render still reading the engine default "Text" (give it its label, or an empty text when a script writes it in play). duplicate: an actor that is a copy of another in the same place with the same meshes, drawn twice. An actor whose worst problem is another kind still counts for these, as for coplanar, when its contentIssues hold them. An actor whose worst problem is another kind still counts for coplanar when it has coplanarFaces. An actor whose bounds touch or overlap another actor's vertical face (a window band on a hall, an awning on a facade) is mounted, never floating or unsupported. Two faces pointing down with something solid right below them (pieces lying on a floor) are not reported as coplanar: no camera sees them. Omit for every kind.

oneOf.description: Maximum number of actors to return in a list.
Maximum problem entries to return (1-200, default 25). Entries come worst-first, so a small limit still shows the placements that matter; flagged is always the true total.
Most actors to return (1-1000, default 200); a longer match list is cut and reports truncated and totalCount.

limit.description: Maximum number of actors to return in a list.

location.description: World or relative location as [x, y, z].

materialIndex.description: Alias of materialSlot accepted by the material handlers (normalizeArgs alias).

materialPath.description: Canonical /Game material asset path to apply.

materials.description: One material per slot in place of materialPath and materialSlot: entry i goes into slot i, "" leaves that slot as it is. Every slot is reported under slots, in one undo step; the call fails naming any slot that did not take its material. A mesh made with several material ids (an SDF part) needs this once instead of one call per slot.

maxActors.description: At most this many actors are judged (1-400, default 300): named actors first, then the nearest to center, else the largest. A level cut short says so with truncated and actorsInScope.

maxRealSeconds.description: Wall-clock cap (default 25, at most 50): the run stops here and reports how much game time it covered, so a long run or an editor throttled to 3 fps still answers before a client that gives up at 30 s. Raise it only for a client that waits longer.

maxTilt.description: Degrees off vertical an actor may lean before it is reported as tilted (1-90, default 30). Lean is the angle between the up vector of the actor and world up, so yaw never counts and a fully inverted actor reads 180. Raise it for a level whose props are deliberately strewn about; lower it to catch subtler leans.

meshPath.description: Canonical /Game mesh asset path to assign on spawn.

minSeverity.description: Drop findings whose severity (worst penetration, ground error, tilt displacement, or the side of the largest z-fighting patch, in world units) is below this. Use it to skip cosmetic grazes on a large level.

name.description: Actor name or search query.

nameFilter.description: Only actors whose label or object name contains this text may move. Omit it, with no actorNames, to fix every actor in the level.

near.description: A world point as [x, y, z] (an {x, y, z} object works too): list what is close to it, nearest first, each row with its distance. With radius, only actors whose bounds come within radius of the point; without it, every matching actor sorted by distance. Combines with filter, tag, className and folder.

newName.description: Label for the copy. Without it the editor numbers the copy after the highest label of its series (Desk_1 copied becomes Desk_20 when Desk_19 exists); the reply's actorName names the copy either way.

oneOf.description: Move by [dx, dy, dz] from where the actor stands now, instead of to an absolute location; give one or the other.

World offset [x, y, z] in cm from the original's location (default [0, 0, 0]). With no offset the copy sits exactly on the original: both draw every face in the same place, which flickers, and the reply's warnings call it a duplicate. Wherever it lands, the reply's warnings name a copy left sunk, floating or intersecting.
Skip this many matching actors; the next page starts at nextOffset from the previous reply.

offset.description: Move by [dx, dy, dz] from where the actor stands now, instead of to an absolute location; give one or the other.

overlaps.description: Also watch which actors overlap the watched one, checked every frame: a sample names those that began (overlapsBegan) or stopped (overlapsEnded) touching it since the sample before, and overlapped lists every actor it touched. Finds what killed a pawn, what a pickup or trigger fired on, or an enemy wandering into a spawn point.

parentActor.description: Parent actor name to attach to.

points.description: Places on the actor sampled with it (at most 8): a component by its name (LegL), a bone or socket of any of its components (foot_l, hand_r), or a component's own socket as Component.Socket (Weapon.Muzzle). Each sample's points gives each one's world location [x, y, z]; a name the actor lacks is refused with the names it has. Fewer samples are kept with points: 400 x 2 / (2 + points).

profile.description: A collision preset of the project (BlockAll, BlockAllDynamic, OverlapAll, OverlapAllDynamic, NoCollision, Pawn, Trigger, PhysicsActor...); an unknown name is refused with the list. The reply reads the preset back.

properties.description: Component property key-value pairs. Each key is a name or dotted path, as propertyName takes it (BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled works). Collision goes through the component setters: CollisionProfileName (a preset), CollisionEnabled, CollisionResponses ({"Pawn": "Ignore"}), PhysMaterialOverride (a physical material path, None to clear).

propertyName.description: Component property to read or write: a name (Intensity), or a dotted path through structs at any depth (BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled, LightmassSettings.bShadowIndirectOnly). A bare name that is not on the component itself resolves to the one struct member carrying it (CollisionEnabled reads and writes BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled); a name several structs carry is refused with the full paths to choose from.

oneOf.description: Actor properties read at every sample, each as JSON (a number, true or false, the name of an enum value, the path of an object, or an array of them), e.g. ["bDead", "HP"], or a component's as "Component.Property" ("Visual.RelativeScale3D" catches a squash on landing), the component by its name or by the actor property that holds it ("CharacterMovement.MaxWalkSpeed"); a name that resolves to nothing is listed under missingProperties.

Property or Blueprint variable names to read on every listed actor, returned per actor under properties, each as JSON (a number, true or false, the name of an enum value, the path of an object, or an array of them), e.g. Kind and Content, or a component's as "Component.Property" (StaticMeshComponent.LDMaxDrawDistance, Visual.RelativeScale3D; the component by its name, or by the actor property that holds it, as CharacterMovement.MaxWalkSpeed), keyed as asked. A name that an actor lacks, or whose component it lacks, is listed under missingProperties for that actor.

propertyNames.description: Actor properties read at every sample, each as JSON (a number, true or false, the name of an enum value, the path of an object, or an array of them), e.g. ["bDead", "HP"], or a component's as "Component.Property" ("Visual.RelativeScale3D" catches a squash on landing), the component by its name or by the actor property that holds it ("CharacterMovement.MaxWalkSpeed"); a name that resolves to nothing is listed under missingProperties.

propertyPath.description: Same as propertyName (a name or a dotted path such as BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled); used when propertyName is absent.

oneOf.description: With center: the radius in cm of the area judged; above 0. Refused without center.

World units from near: an actor is listed when its bounding box comes within this distance of the point (the distance is 0 for a box that contains the point, such as a floor slab under it). Needs near.

radius.description: With center: the radius in cm of the area judged; above 0. Refused without center.

readMode.description:
Which get transform variant to run; omit for 'transform'.
transform: Read the world transform (location, rotation, scale) of an actor.
motion: Watch an actor over game time in Play-In-Editor and return its location, velocity, rotation and chosen properties at every interval, plus start/end and min/max extents, in one call; it can also follow points on the actor (bones, sockets, components) with their height over the ground, press keys at exact game times (inputs) and wait for another actor's property to change before it starts (startWhen). The warnings say what the game logged while it ran, and a Blueprint runtime error names the node, graph and Blueprint that raised it.

relations.description: What should hold, one relation per entry between two actors by name (names with spaces in double quotes): A on B, A inside B, A nextTo B, A against B, A facing B, or A near B within d. Anything else (a comparison, exists, not, and, or) is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT, as is a relation from an actor to itself; a name that matches no actor refuses with ACTOR_NOT_FOUND (missing lists them) and nothing moves.

relativeLocation.description: With snapToTarget: offset from the bone or socket in its own space, as [x, y, z].

relativeRotation.description: With snapToTarget: rotation relative to the bone or socket, as [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees.

renameObject.description: Also rename the object itself to newName, made valid and unique (default false: the label only). The label is editor-only; the object name ships in the cooked level. References from inside the same level follow the rename, a Level Sequence binding or a soft reference by the old path does not. An actor saved in its own package (World Partition) keeps its object name, with a note.

report.description: Which items results lists: all, or failures only (items that failed to spawn or to take their material or variables, and items with a placementWarning); spawned and failed still count every item. Default all, or failures for a batch of more than 20 items once repeats are unrolled; the receipt still names every actor.

responses.description: How the components answer each named channel, {"Pawn": "Ignore", "Visibility": "Block"}: an engine channel (WorldStatic, WorldDynamic, Pawn, Visibility, Camera, PhysicsBody, Vehicle, Destructible) or one the project added, by its name; each Block, Overlap or Ignore. Applied after profile, so the preset then reads Custom; the reply reads each channel back.

rotation.description: Rotation as [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees.

seconds.description: At most this much physics time (0.5-10, default 3): the run stops sooner once every body sleeps. A body still moving at the end comes back under unstable with its pose at that moment, which is kept.

snapToTarget.description: Snap the child onto the bone or socket instead of keeping its current world placement (default false).

socketName.description: Bone or socket on that component to attach to (hand_r, weapon_r, head). Refused with SOCKET_NOT_FOUND when the component has neither.

spawnKind.description:
Which spawn variant to run; omit for 'class'.
class: Spawn a new actor instance from a class path into the current level, or a mesh actor from a mesh path alone.
blueprint: Spawn an actor instance from a Blueprint asset path into the current level.
batch: Spawn many actors in one call; each item is a spawn payload, optionally with a material, Blueprint variables, outliner folder and tags.

spawnOf.description: In place of actorName, for an actor the game has not spawned yet: its class (a Blueprint as BP_Thing or its _C path, a native class by its short name; a subclass counts too). The call waits for the first one spawned after it and watches it from its first frame; actorName in the reply names it.

spawnWaitSeconds.description: With spawnOf: game seconds to wait for the spawn (default 10, at most 30); nothing spawned ends with endedBecause spawnTimeout and no samples. The wait comes out of maxRealSeconds, so the wait and the run still answer inside it.

actorName.description: Actor whose property starts the run.

propertyName.description: That actor's property, as propertyNames reads it: bActorEnableCollision, or a component's as Component.Property (CharacterMovement.MovementMode starts the run on a landing when equals is MOVE_Walking).

equals.description: Value that starts the run, as samples show it (true, false, 3, "Walking").

waitForChange.description: Default true: start only when the value BECOMES equals (a platform appearing), not while it already is.

maxWaitSeconds.description: Game seconds to wait before giving up with endedBecause startWhenTimeout (default 10, at most 30).

startWhen.description: Hold the run (samples and inputs) until another actor's property takes a value, so the timeline starts on a game event instead of whenever the call arrived.

summary.description: Count the matching actors by class, actor tag and outliner folder (byClass, byTag, byFolder) instead of listing them; limit and offset do not apply. The cheap first look at an unfamiliar level.

tag.description: Actor tag: one entry in the Tags list of an actor (not a Gameplay Tag) to add, remove, find or delete by.

tagOp.description:
Which add tag variant to run; omit for 'add'.
