add: Add a tag to an actor, or with actorNames to many actors in one call and one undo step; their level is left unsaved. A tag already there is kept once (wasPresent). actorNames that match nothing come back in missing, and ACTOR_NOT_FOUND answers when none matched. Tags drive find_by_tag, delete_by_tag and the Actor Has Tag node; mcp.placement.ok makes the placement checks skip the actor.
remove: Remove a gameplay tag from an actor.

oneOf.description: Actor tags for the new actor: delete_by_tag removes them again, and mcp.placement.ok marks a deliberate overlap before the placement is judged.
Several actor tags at once, in place of tag: every actor carrying any of them is deleted under one consent.

tags.description: Actor tags for the new actor: delete_by_tag removes them again, and mcp.placement.ok marks a deliberate overlap before the placement is judged.

transformMode.description:
Which set transform variant to run; omit for 'transform'.
transform: Move, rotate or scale an actor by setting its world transform (location, rotation, scale) or moving it by an offset, or many actors in one call: actors gives each its own, actorNames gives all the same.
location: Alias of transformMode=transform (location-only intent); normalizes to transformMode=transform.
rotation: Alias of transformMode=transform (rotation-only intent); normalizes to transformMode=transform.
scale: Alias of transformMode=transform (scale-only intent); normalizes to transformMode=transform.
teleport: Alias of transformMode=transform. The bridge dispatches both names to the same handler.

variables.description: Blueprint variable name to value map. A name the actor does not have refuses the whole call before anything is set; the error lists the variables it does have. An actor variable takes the other actor by label, name or path. A value that does not take (an object path that loads nothing) fails the call, naming it; the variables that did take are listed under updated.

tools.name: control_editor
tools.description: Start/stop PIE, control viewport camera, run console commands, take screenshots, simulate input.

acceptRadius.description: How near the goal counts as reached, in cm (default 100).

actorName.description: Name of the actor to target.

arguments.description: Argument values keyed by parameter name. Converted per-property, so structs and arrays are accepted in their JSON form. Omitted parameters keep their zero-initialised default and are listed in unsetParameters.

assetPaths.description: Save only these assets or levels, e.g. ["/Game/UI/WBP_Menu"], and leave every other dirty package as it is; omit to save everything dirty. A named asset the editor has loaded is written even when it is not marked dirty (a material usage flag the editor set while loading).

blendTime.description: Blend time in seconds for set_view_target.

cameraOp.description:
Which set camera variant to run; omit for 'transform'.
transform: Set the viewport camera position and rotation: the level viewport, or, while Play In Editor runs with the player ejected (control_editor play control=eject), the free camera the game view is drawn from.
fov: Set the camera field of view of the view on screen: the level viewport, the free view of an ejected player, or while the player plays the running game's camera (method player_camera_manager; locked to the value until play stops).
view_target: Set the PIE view target to a specific actor by name.

cell.description: continue: the archive index of the cell the next round starts from (read with detail lists them).

cellCm.description: start: the cell size on the floor plan, in cm (50-2000, default 200).

checks.description: Assertions judged when the leg ends, in execute's expect language (Door_1 hidden, BP_Player.Health > 0), at most 16.

classPath.description: Alias for className, the spelling the rest of the catalog uses.

control.description:
Which play variant to run; omit for 'play'.
play: Start Play-In-Editor (PIE) session; answers once the play world has begun play.
pause: Pause the running Play In Editor session, as the toolbar pause does; the reply says alreadyPaused when it was. No session is NO_ACTIVE_SESSION.
resume: Resume a paused Play In Editor session; wasPaused false says it was not paused and nothing changed. A pause the game holds itself (a pause menu) is GAME_PAUSED unless unpauseGame is true, and a widget that still holds keyboard focus is named in warnings. No session is NO_ACTIVE_SESSION.
stop: Stop the running PIE session.
eject: Eject the player from its pawn in PIE, as the editor's Eject button does: the session switches to Simulate in Editor and the view becomes a free camera that set_camera moves and screenshot photographs. Answers once the view has switched.
possess: Possess a pawn in PIE: the player controller takes the pawn named by actorName. Without actorName it brings an ejected player back to its own pawn, as the editor's Possess button does (the way back from eject). Answers once the player is back in the game.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds to wait before restarting, so the response reaches the caller first. Clamped to 0.1-30.

deltaTime.description: Seconds every frame advances the running game, however long the frame really took (deterministic runs); 0 turns fixed stepping off. It also ends when PIE stops.

detail.description: read and stop: list the archive, each cell as {cell, where, parent, chosen, leads, flags}, at most 200.

discardUnsaved.description: Restart even though packages have unsaved changes, discarding them. Omitted, a restart with unsaved work is refused.

durationSeconds.description: Stop the recording by itself after this many seconds of game time.

fallCm.description: How far below its start the pawn may drop before it counts as fallen (default 500).

filter.description: Case-sensitive substring matched against function names.

fov.description: Camera field of view in degrees.

frameRate.description: Replay frames recorded per second, 1 to 120 (sets demo.RecordHz; the engine default is 8).

functionName.description: Function name exactly as reported by describe_reflected_api.

goal.description: Where the pawn should get to.

goalActor.description: An actor of the running game to walk to, in place of goal.

heightCm.description: start: the height band, in cm (25-1000, default 100): a ledge above another floor is another cell.

history.description:
Which undo variant to run; omit for 'undo'.
undo: Undo the last editor transaction; the reply names it, and NOTHING_TO_UNDO means there was none.
redo: Redo the last undone editor transaction; the reply names it, and NOTHING_TO_REDO means there was none.
restore_point: Mark a restore point to roll the editor back to, undoing only what calls through this server changed, chosen by op. begin opens it (one at a time; label names it); status lists the editor's transactions since it, newest first, each with byMcp, and the assets created, removed or saved since (assetsCreated, assetsRemoved, packagesSaved); rollback undoes every step since it and refuses before undoing anything when a step was not made through this server (USER_STEP_SINCE_RESTORE_POINT names it) or the editor's history was cleared since (UNDO_HISTORY_CLEARED: a Blueprint compile or a level load clears it); end closes it. Undo deletes no created asset and restores no saved file: status and rollback list them, and cleanupCall is the manage_asset bulk_delete of the assets calls through this server created that are still there, ready to send (it asks for consent); an asset made by hand in the editor is listed but never in it. A rollback is refused while Play runs (PIE_RUNNING).

holdSeconds.description: Keep injecting inputAction, or keep a raw key_down/key_tap key pressed, for this many seconds of GAME time so the pawn actually travels (default 0: an action lasts one frame, a key_down stays down until key_up, a key_tap lets go after 0.1s). Game time, not wall time: under set_game_speed 0.05 a 2s hold still delivers 2s of in-game input, which takes 40s of real time. A key_up for the same action or key stops the hold early. The reply comes back at once, while the key is still down: read the pawn after the hold, or press and watch in one call with control_actor sample_motion inputs.

id.description: Bookmark slot number, 0 to 9 on a default level (the slots Ctrl+0..9 set). Unreal bookmarks are numbered slots, not names; a number outside the level's range is refused.

includeMetadata.description: true: echo metadata back in the reply (default false).

oneOf.description: The tool's arguments, shaped by the inputSchema list_editor_toolsets returned for toolName. Omit for a tool without arguments.
The tool's arguments, shaped by the inputSchema list_editor_toolsets returned for toolName.

input.description: The tool's arguments, shaped by the inputSchema list_editor_toolsets returned for toolName.

inputAction.description: Enhanced Input action to inject directly, as an asset path such as /Game/Input/IA_Move. A raw key already reaches Enhanced Input through the active mapping contexts (key_down D moves a pawn whose context maps D); use inputAction when no key is mapped to the action, or to inject an analog value.

inputType.description: Alias for type used by simulate_input.

keepFile.description: false: hand the image back without leaving a file in Saved/Screenshots (refused with returnBase64 false, which would leave no output at all). Default true. Files already written are listed by system_control list_output_files and removed by delete_output_file.

key.description: Key name: SpaceBar, D, Left, Enter, P. Escape is the editor stop-play key: in Play In Editor it ends the session instead of reaching the game, so test an action bound to Escape through another key mapped to it.

label.description: Name for the restore point (begin); default restore point.

limit.description: Most tools listed (default 50); matchedTools and hasMore tell what was left out.

oneOf.description: 3D location (x, y, z).

editor_viewport (and game_viewport while the player is ejected): put the camera here first, in the same call ({x, y, z}); it stays there. Water and streamed texture detail follow the view over the next frames, which this call does not wait for: after a jump far from the last view (or right after a level opens) the picture can show black water or soft textures, so capture again from the same spot, or move with set_camera first. That is the level viewport camera, or, while Play In Editor runs with the player ejected, the ejected view. While Play In Editor runs and the player is not ejected there is no free camera to move and the call is refused with PIE_VIEW_NOT_EJECTED (eject first, or point the game camera with set_camera cameraOp=view_target), exactly as set_camera is.

maxSeconds.description: Game seconds the leg may take (default 15, at most 60; at most 25 real seconds).

metadata.description: An object of your own, such as a label or a step number, returned under metadata when includeMetadata is true; the capture itself never reads it.

minimize.description: Minimize the main editor window instead of restoring it, without taking focus, and turn Use Less CPU when in Background back on (saved). unthrottle is ignored. Default false.

mode.description: Editor mode id to activate: EM_Default, EM_Landscape, EM_Foliage, EM_MeshPaint or any registered mode id; a bare name (landscape) is tried as EM_<name>. The call fails when the mode is not active afterwards.

name.description: Name identifier.

op.description: begin opens the restore point, status lists what changed since it (the default), rollback undoes it, end closes it.

path.description: Directory to save the PNG in, inside the project (relative to it, or absolute under it). Default Saved/Screenshots (game_viewport: Saved/Screenshots/WindowsEditor). A path outside the project is refused.

query.description: Words that must all appear in a tool's name or description (any case), e.g. "state tree add".

relaunch.description: false closes the editor instead of relaunching it (default true). Unsaved packages are refused the same way.

resolution.description: Maximum WxH for the returned PNG (e.g. "1280x720"). The capture is downscaled to fit inside this box with its aspect ratio preserved; a box at least as large as the viewport leaves the image untouched. Without it an image returned inline fits 1600x900, and a file-only capture (returnBase64 false) keeps the viewport size.

returnBase64.description: Return the PNG inline as an image (default true); a capture also saves a file unless keepFile is false. With no resolution, an inline image is downscaled to fit 1600x900. false returns only the saved path and metadata, at the full viewport size.

oneOf.description: 3D rotation (pitch, yaw, roll).

editor_viewport (and game_viewport while the player is ejected): turn that camera to this first ({pitch, yaw, roll}), in the same call. Refused like location while Play In Editor runs and the player is not ejected.

seconds.description: start and continue: real seconds to explore before answering (1-22, default 10).

seed.description: start: the seed of the random moves (default 1): the same seed repeats the same moves.

setting.description:
Which configure editor variant to run.
open_tab: Open a registered editor tab by id via FGlobalTabmanager, the same path the Window menu uses. Content-source plugins register their windows globally — Bridge as "BridgeTab" — so this reaches them without depending on either plugin. Fab registers no fixed id (it numbers each tab Fab1, Fab2, ...), so tabId "Fab" opens a new Fab tab through the Fab browser API (UE 5.8+). This is also the correct way to authenticate against those services: each owns its own sign-in and persists its own session, so opening its window lets it log in on its own terms rather than reimplementing a login.
preferences: Set editor preferences, preferences {name: value} in a category: a key naming a console variable is set as the console sets it and read back; any other is a property of the category's settings class (EditorPerformanceSettings, LevelEditorPlaySettings, LevelEditorViewportSettings and the like, the U prefix and Settings suffix optional), written through the property's own text import, saved to the settings ini and applied at once; LevelEditor RealtimeAudio mutes or unmutes editor audio. Keys that did not apply are listed under failed with why, and the call answers PREFERENCES_PARTIALLY_APPLIED or PREFERENCES_NOT_APPLIED. This plugin's own settings are refused. Distinct from system_control set_project_setting.
window: Restore or minimize the main editor window without giving it focus. Restoring also stops the editor throttling itself while in the background (a minimized editor runs Play In Editor at about 3 fps, which makes every timed test lie); minimize puts the window away and turns the throttle back on, so an editor kept out of the way costs the machine next to nothing.

speed.description: Clock multiplier for the running game: 1 is normal, 0.05 runs it twenty times slower (above 0, up to 20).

stat.description: One stat to show or hide (FPS, Unit, Game, SceneRendering...). show_stats without it shows FPS and Unit; hide_stats without it hides every stat. A stat already in the wanted state is left alone, so repeating a call never toggles it back.

stuckSeconds.description: Game seconds without getting nearer that count as stuck (default 2).

tabId.description: Registered nomad tab id, for example "BridgeTab" (Quixel Bridge); "Fab" opens a new Fab tab.

toolName.description: Full name of one tool, Toolset.Tool: returns its schema (description, inputSchema) and effect instead of the list.

toolset.description: List only the tools of this toolset, by the name the toolsets list shows.

track.description: start: assertions in execute's expect language whose truth joins the cell (Door_1 hidden, BP_Key exists), at most 16: the same place with a door open is a new cell to explore from. A teleport cannot restore them; such cells are marked.

type.description: Input event type (key_down, key_up, key_tap = press then release, mouse_click, mouse_move), or widget_list / widget_click to operate the live UMG of a PIE session.

unpauseGame.description: Also lift a pause the game holds itself (SetGamePaused from its pause menu or a title screen), as its own unpause does. Without it, a game that paused itself fails the call with GAME_PAUSED and pausedBy: the editor pause is off, but nothing ticks.

unthrottle.description: Also turn off Use Less CPU when in Background (EditorPerformanceSettings.bThrottleCPUWhenNotForeground) for this editor session; it is not saved, so the next launch throttles again. Default true; ignored with minimize.

validateOnly.description: Report whether a restart would proceed, and what it would discard, without restarting.

value.description: Scalar value to inject for inputAction (default 1; use a negative value for the opposite direction), or the value to set a Slider to with widget_click. Ignored for a raw key.

viewMode.description: Viewport view mode (e.g. Lit, Unlit, Wireframe).

waitForShaders.description: true: when shaders are still compiling (after a scalability or material change), wait for the queue to drain before capturing, polling without blocking the game thread, for at most 25 seconds; shaderWait in the reply says how long it waited and how many jobs were left. Default false: capture now and report shadersCompiling.

widget.description: For type widget_click: the live UMG widget to drive, by name (PlayButton), or Owner.Name (WBP_MainMenu.PlayButton) when several share it. widget_list shows both.

window.description: With mode full_editor_window, which window to capture: a list index (2, or "2") or a case-insensitive substring of its title ("WBP_HubUI"). Omit for the main editor frame, which is then always what is captured: a minimized main frame is restored without taking focus, and when that is not possible the call fails with EDITOR_WINDOW_MINIMIZED instead of capturing another window. A window restored for the capture is minimized again right after it. Every response lists the open windows under windows[], so read that to pick one.

x.description: Mouse X for simulate_input: while a game runs, mouse_move takes pixels of the game viewport and moves the game cursor there (where Get Mouse Position and Get Hit Result Under Cursor read it; a click at it is a key_tap of LeftMouseButton); otherwise desktop coordinates for the editor UI. Or the X value of an Axis2D or Axis3D inputAction.

y.description: Mouse Y for simulate_input, in the same space as x, or the Y value of an Axis2D or Axis3D inputAction.

z.description: Z value of an Axis3D inputAction (x and y give the other two).

tools.name: inspect
tools.description: Inspect any UObject: read/write properties, list components, export snapshots, and query class info. Actions: inspect_cdo (Blueprint CDO properties + all components without spawning an actor; use blueprintPath, optional detailed/componentName/propertyNames), inspect_class (class metadata), inspect_object (world actor), get_property/set_property, get_components, get_component_details (WORLD actors: actorName+componentName; a blueprintPath is routed to inspect_cdo), list_objects, find_by_class, find_by_tag, runtime_report.

actionPath.description: The Input Action asset the key should fire, e.g. /Game/Input/IA_Jump.

actorName.description: The actor to show (label, name or path). One that matches no actor refuses with ACTOR_NOT_FOUND; one that draws nothing the game shows (only editor icons) refuses with NOTHING_DRAWN.

actorNames.description: Several world actors to act on in one call, in place of actorName; names not found are listed back.

actors.description: Only these actors (label, name or path): their rows under actors (a row whose box nearer actors partly cover names them under coveredBy, as a sign half behind a row of blocks), and under notVisible each one that drew no pixel with its reason, outside the frame or hidden, with hiddenBy naming the actors drawn over its box (up to three, by share of the box). Names that match no actor are listed under notFound. limit does not apply.

aspects.description: What to judge (default saliency, palette and light; cost draws the viewport once in another view mode). Any other name refuses with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

blueprintPath.description: Blueprint asset /Game path (for CDO/component inspection without spawning).

channel.description: Collision channel traced: Visibility (default), Camera, WorldStatic, WorldDynamic, Pawn, PhysicsBody, Vehicle, Destructible, or a project trace channel by its name. What blocks depends on each component's response to that channel: most meshes block Visibility, a character capsule blocks Pawn.

checks.description: What to check (default all three). Any other name refuses with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

className.description: Class name or /Script/ class path to inspect.

compareWith.description: Compare this frame with the one saved under that name, taken again from its camera: change lists what changed beyond the renderer's own noise. Refused with VIEW_BASELINE_NOT_FOUND for a name not saved, VIEW_SIZE_CHANGED when the viewport changed size, and CAMERA_MOVED when location or rotation (or the field of view) differs from the saved camera. With saveAs in the same call, the comparison comes first.

oneOf.description: Return only these components in components, by name (case-insensitive); a name that matches none is listed under missingComponents.
Return only these components, by name (case-insensitive); a name that matches none is listed under missingComponents.
Specific component names to include.

componentNames.description: Return only these components in components, by name (case-insensitive); a name that matches none is listed under missingComponents.

detailed.description: Every property the component's class declares, as text (up to 200): a Niagara or mesh component declares about 200, most of the reply. Prefer propertyNames.

editorState.description:
Which get editor state variant to run.
selected_actors: Return the actors currently selected in the editor viewport.
viewport: Return viewport information (view target, camera manager, world type).
world_settings: Return the current world/level settings summary (worldName, gravity, killZ, time).
project_settings: Return project settings key/value pairs.
editor_settings: Return editor settings key/value pairs.
focus: Read what the user is working on: the open asset editors (most recently used first), each open Blueprint editor's graph in front and its selected nodes (title and nodeId), the selected actors, the distinct warnings and errors of the last minute, and the Blueprint runtime errors of the last play session.

event.description: The event that should happen: overlap (default) or hit.

format.description: Exporter format by file extension, default T3D (the text form of the object); fails with EXPORT_FAILED when no exporter for that format handles the object.

ignoreActors.description: Actors (label, name or path) the lines pass through, such as the player pawn a line starts inside; an unknown name is refused.

info.description:
Which get component details variant to run; omit for 'details'.
details: Return a single component of a world actor (TS dispatches get_components to control_actor and filters locally).
property: Read a property on a world actor component (cross-parent to control_actor).

key.description: The key pressed, by engine key name (SpaceBar, E, Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom); omitted, any key mapped to the action counts.

kind.description:
Which inspect class variant to run; omit for 'class'.
class: Inspect a UClass: metadata, parent, default CDO properties.
struct: Inspect a UserDefinedStruct layout (member names, types, defaults) read-only.
cdo: Inspect a Blueprint Class Default Object (CDO) and its default components without spawning an actor.

labels.description: Also return the frame (at most 960 px wide) with each actor listed under actors boxed in its own colour and numbered from 1 in list order, as an image (imageBase64).

last.description: How many of each node's newest runs to list (1-500, default 20).

oneOf.description: Camera location {x, y, z} in cm; omitted, the viewport's current one. The camera stays there afterwards, as describe_view leaves it.
Camera location {x, y, z} in cm; omitted, the viewport's current one. The camera stays there.

location.description: Camera location {x, y, z} in cm; omitted, the viewport's current one. The camera stays there afterwards, as describe_view leaves it.

logpointOp.description:
Which read logpoints variant to run; omit for 'read'.
set: Mark Blueprint nodes to record the values on their pins each time they run in Play, without pausing the game: a print statement that changes no graph. Before Play or during it; each play session starts the timelines empty. Read them with logpointOp=read. Marks last until logpointOp=clear or the editor closes; at most 32 at once.
read: Read what marked Blueprint nodes recorded in Play: for each node its runs and newest values, input and output pins by name, with the game time and the object it ran on. Readable during Play and after it stops, until the next play session starts.
clear: Remove logpoint marks: all of them, those of one Blueprint, or chosen nodes. With none left, nothing listens to the running game any more.

lookup.description:
Which query object variant to run.
list: List world actors (cross-parent to control_actor; dispatches action list_actors).
by_tag: Find world actors by tag (cross-parent to control_actor).
metadata: Read metadata key/value pairs from a world actor (cross-parent to control_actor).
bounding_box: Return the world-space bounding box of a world actor (cross-parent to control_actor).
export: Export a world actor or object as text (T3D by default), returned inline as exportedText and, with outputPath, also written to a file inside the project.

markDirty.description: Default true: mark the package dirty and save an asset package. false leaves the package untouched and unsaved, so the change lives in memory only.

maxHits.description: How many of each node's newest runs are kept (1-500, default 100); runs counts them all.

meshPath.description: Static mesh asset path, e.g. /Game/Meshes/SM_Rock. Its source triangles (LOD 0 as imported or built) are checked, so a Nanite mesh answers at full detail. A placed actor's mesh is named by get_components.

name.description: Actor name identifier (alias of actorName).

nodeIds.description: Nodes by id: the GUID edit_graph and get_graph_details give, or the tag read_graph_as_code prints (n + the GUID's first hex digits, as n3fa9c1).

objectKind.description:
Which inspect object variant to run; omit for 'object'.
object: Inspect a world actor or asset object by path, returning detailed properties.
actor: Inspect a world actor (alias of objectKind=object).
level: Inspect the current level/world summary (TS normalizes to get_world_settings).
material: Inspect a material or material instance: blend mode, parameters and textures. Any other object is refused with TYPE_MISMATCH.
mesh: Inspect a static or skeletal mesh asset: size, bounds, pivot, LODs, and every material slot with the triangles and bounds of the geometry it covers. Any other object is refused with TYPE_MISMATCH.
texture: Inspect a texture asset: dimensions, format and settings. Any other object is refused with TYPE_MISMATCH.

objectPath.description: Object path of the world actor or asset (e.g. /Game/Maps/Demo.Demo_PersistentLevel).

oneOf.description: The same read on several objects in one call, in place of objectPath: each entry is a target as objectPath takes it (an actor by name or label, an asset, a class default, PlayerPawn), read as a single call would be, propertyNames included. Answered under targets; a target that cannot be read carries its error and the others still answer.

The same write on several targets in one call, in place of objectPath: each entry is a target as objectPath takes it (an actor, "Actor.Component", an asset, a class default), written as a single call would be, with properties too. Answered under targets; the call fails naming each target that did not take the write, and the others keep it.

objectPaths.description: The same read on several objects in one call, in place of objectPath: each entry is a target as objectPath takes it (an actor by name or label, an asset, a class default, PlayerPawn), read as a single call would be, propertyNames included. Answered under targets; a target that cannot be read carries its error and the others still answer.

offset.description: Matching objects to skip before the first one returned, for paging (default 0); hasMore says whether more follow.

otherActor.description: The second actor, by label, name or path.

outputPath.description: File to also write the export to, inside the project (relative to it, or absolute under it), e.g. Saved/Exports/Actor.t3d. A path outside the project is refused with INVALID_PATH.

points.description: Spots of the frame as {x, y} from 0 to 1 (x from the left, y from the top; 0.5, 0.5 is the middle): each answers under points at the same index with what is drawn there and what the line from the camera through it hits. A perspective viewport only.

oneOf.description: Several component properties at once, name or dotted path to value, in place of propertyName and value.

Several writes on the same target in place of propertyName and value: {name or dotted path: value}, e.g. {"BoxExtent": {"X": 20, "Y": 90, "Z": 100}, "CollisionProfileName": "OverlapAllDynamic"}. Each is written as a single call would be and reported under properties; the call fails naming any that did not apply. watch applies to single writes only.

properties.description: Several component properties at once, name or dotted path to value, in place of propertyName and value.

propertyName.description: Property to read or write: a name, or a dotted path through structs and object references at any depth (BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled). On an actor the path may start with a component's name, including one added in the level (MyAudio.VolumeMultiplier). A bare name that is not on the object itself resolves to the one struct member carrying it. Give this or propertyPath.

oneOf.description: Properties to read, each a name or dotted path: read on each matching actor itself (its Blueprint variables, such as bIsOpen, land in the actor properties) and on each reported component (in that component properties). A name found on none of the listed actors is listed once in propertiesNotFound.

Property values to add to the reply, by name (Intensity, bIsActive), as text under properties; a name the class lacks is listed under missingProperties. CollisionResponses reads every channel's response on a primitive component ({"Pawn": "Ignore", ...}). Without propertyNames or detailed no property values come back.
Specific property names to include.

Several properties of the same target in one call, in place of propertyName: each read as a single call would (dotted paths too, such as CharacterMovement.MaxWalkSpeed). Answered under properties; a name that does not resolve is listed under missingProperties with the reason, and the others still answer.

propertyNames.description: Properties to read, each a name or dotted path: read on each matching actor itself (its Blueprint variables, such as bIsOpen, land in the actor properties) and on each reported component (in that component properties). A name found on none of the listed actors is listed once in propertiesNotFound.

propertyPath.description: Same as propertyName (a name or dotted path); used when propertyName is absent. Give this or propertyName.

origin.description: Ray start {x, y, z} in the mesh's local space, in cm; start outside the mesh to find its outer surface.

direction.description: Ray direction {x, y, z}; any length, it is normalized.

start.description: Line start {x, y, z} in local space, with end in place of origin and direction (the form raycast_world takes).

end.description: Line end {x, y, z} in local space; nothing past it is reported.

oneOf.description: Rays in the mesh's local space, each {origin, direction} or {start, end}; each answers in hits at the same index.

start.description: Line start {x, y, z} in world space, in cm.

end.description: Line end {x, y, z} in world space; nothing past it is reported.

oneOf.description: Lines in world space; each answers in hits at the same index.

rays.description: Lines in world space; each answers in hits at the same index.

rotation.description: Camera rotation {pitch, yaw, roll} in degrees; omitted, the viewport's current one.

saveAs.description: Keep this frame under a name for a later compareWith, with the camera it was taken from (until the editor closes; the same name replaces it, and a ninth name forgets the oldest). Drawn twice, to learn how much the renderer varies an unchanged frame by itself. With saveAs or compareWith the frame is read as the game draws it, so icons, gizmos and selection outlines are left out and other reads 0.

since.description: The cursor a previous changes_since reply returned. Omit it to get the most recent changes kept, and a cursor to start from.

snapshotOp.description:
Which create snapshot variant to run; omit for 'create'.
create: Remember a world actor's transform (location, rotation and scale only) under snapshotName, in editor memory, for snapshotOp=restore to set again.
restore: Set a world actor back to the transform a snapshot remembered (snapshotOp=create); transformChanged says whether anything moved.

statsKind.description:
Which get stats variant to run.
performance: Return performance statistics (frame rate, frame time, game, render and GPU thread times, actor count).
memory: Return memory statistics (allocated, virtual, resource counts).
scene: Return scene statistics (actor counts, component counts, etc.).
frame: Diagnose what a frame costs: the thread that bounds it (game, render, RHI or GPU; in Play, whether the game or the editor fills the game thread) and what in view weighs on it: movable lights that cast shadows, the heaviest non-Nanite meshes, translucent primitives and ticking actors by class.

subject.description: The actor the shot is about (label, name or path): its saliency share and rank, and its key to fill ratio against the sun. A name that matches no actor refuses with ACTOR_NOT_FOUND.

targetActor.description: The actor the light should reach; omitted, only the light itself is checked.

tileSize.description: Side of each square tile in pixels (default 320); the sheet is three tiles across.

tolerance.description: With points: a spot where no actor is drawn (just beside a thin pole, past an edge) moves to the nearest pixel within this many where one is, and its row says where under snappedTo (default 0: no move).

traceComplex.description: Trace the render triangles of meshes that allow it instead of their simple collision (default false: the shapes the game's movement collides with).

value.description: Property value to set, in the form get_property reads back: a number, string or bool, {"X": 0, "Y": 0, "Z": 100} for a vector, an object or asset path, an array for an Array or Set, and a JSON object of key: value for a Map ({"Apple": 3}), which replaces the whole map.

views.description: The views, in this order (default all six). front looks at the side the actor faces (its X axis); left and right are its own; top looks straight down with its front at the bottom of the tile; three_quarter is a perspective view from its front right, above.

watch.description: Sample a property right after the write, in the same call, to see what the write sets off before it ends: a HUD pop or fade runs on real time, even with PIE paused, and is over before a later call can read it. The reply lists each value the property took with its time t in seconds (Lives on GameInstance with watch {objectPath: "WBP_HUD", propertyName: "LivesBox.RenderTransform"}).

propertyName.description: The property to sample; a dotted path reaches through widgets and structs (LivesBox.RenderTransform). Omitted, the property the call writes.

objectPath.description: The object to sample, as objectPath takes it (GameInstance, a live widget such as WBP_HUD); omitted, the object written.

durationSeconds.description: Real seconds to sample (default 0.5, at most 20).

intervalSeconds.description: Seconds between samples (default 0: every frame); a sample is kept only when the value changed.

what.description:
Which explain variant to run.
collision: Explain why actorName and otherActor do not overlap (event overlap, the default) or hit each other (event hit), from what the engine uses to decide: collision turned off on an actor (ACTOR_COLLISION_DISABLED), no component taking part in collision queries (NO_COLLIDING_COMPONENT), a static mesh with no collision shape (NO_COLLISION_SHAPE), a channel response on either side that ignores the other's object type (RESPONSE_IGNORES; a hit needs Block both ways, RESPONSE_DOES_NOT_BLOCK), two blockers that raise hits rather than overlaps (BLOCKS_INSTEAD), Generate Overlap Events off on a side (OVERLAP_EVENTS_OFF), a simulating body without hit events (HIT_EVENTS_OFF), one told to ignore the other (IGNORED_WHEN_MOVING), and whether they touch now. Reads the running game during Play, the editor level otherwise. The reply gives verdict (failed, unknown when a check could not be made, or ok), cause (the first failed check: check, code, detail and, when one fixes it, nextCall), causes (every failed check) and checks (each check made, in order, passed, failed or unknown). Nothing is changed.
visible: Explain why actorName is not seen, from the player's camera during Play or the editor viewport otherwise: hidden in the game or in the editor (HIDDEN_IN_GAME, HIDDEN_IN_EDITOR), editor-only during Play (EDITOR_ONLY), its streaming level not visible (LEVEL_HIDDEN), no component that draws (NOTHING_TO_DRAW: each hidden, unregistered, or a static mesh component with no mesh), beyond a component's draw distance (CULLED_BY_DISTANCE), nearer than the near clip plane (INSIDE_NEAR_CLIP), outside the camera's field of view (OUT_OF_VIEW), drawn only for its owner or hidden from its owner (ONLY_OWNER_SEES, OWNER_NO_SEE), or buried in the surface under it (BURIED, with the location that rests it on top). The reply names the view it judged from (viewFrom). The reply gives verdict (failed, unknown when a check could not be made, or ok), cause (the first failed check: check, code, detail and, when one fixes it, nextCall), causes (every failed check) and checks (each check made, in order, passed, failed or unknown). Nothing is changed.
input: Explain why the Enhanced Input action at actionPath (pressed with key, when given) does nothing: no mapping context under /Game maps it (NOT_MAPPED), no Add Mapping Context node adds such a context in the game mode's player controller or pawn Blueprints, or during Play the player has none of them added (CONTEXT_NOT_ADDED: every key stays dead), and no event for the action in those Blueprints (NOT_HANDLED); during Play also no possessed pawn (NO_PAWN), a paused game (GAME_PAUSED) and a widget holding keyboard focus (WIDGET_HAS_FOCUS). A missing action is ACTION_NOT_FOUND. The reply gives verdict (failed, unknown when a check could not be made, or ok), cause (the first failed check: check, code, detail and, when one fixes it, nextCall), causes (every failed check) and checks (each check made, in order, passed, failed or unknown). Nothing is changed.
widget: Explain why the Widget Blueprint at widgetPath is not on screen. During Play: no instance exists (NOT_CREATED), one exists but was never added to the viewport or to another widget (NOT_IN_VIEWPORT), its visibility is Collapsed or Hidden (HIDDEN), its render opacity is 0 (TRANSPARENT), or its desired size is 0 by 0 (ZERO_SIZE). Outside Play: no Create Widget node for it in the game mode's player controller, pawn or HUD Blueprint or the level's own (NOT_CREATED_ANYWHERE), or the Blueprint that creates it never adds it to the viewport (NOT_ADDED); whether it is on screen is then unknown until Play. A missing Widget Blueprint is WIDGET_NOT_FOUND. The reply gives verdict (failed, unknown when a check could not be made, or ok), cause (the first failed check: check, code, detail and, when one fixes it, nextCall), causes (every failed check) and checks (each check made, in order, passed, failed or unknown). Nothing is changed.
audible: Explain why actorName's sound is not heard: no audio component (NO_AUDIO_COMPONENT), no sound on it (NO_SOUND), not playing during Play (NOT_PLAYING) or not starting by itself (NOT_AUTO_ACTIVATED), a volume multiplier of 0 (MUTED), or the listener beyond its attenuation range (OUT_OF_RANGE: inner radius plus falloff). The listener is the player's during Play (often the camera, far from the pawn in a side view) and the editor viewport otherwise (listener in the reply). The reply gives verdict (failed, unknown when a check could not be made, or ok), cause (the first failed check: check, code, detail and, when one fixes it, nextCall), causes (every failed check) and checks (each check made, in order, passed, failed or unknown). Nothing is changed.
lit: Explain why the light actorName lights nothing, or does not light targetActor: hidden or not affecting the world (LIGHT_OFF), an intensity of 0 (NO_INTENSITY), a Static light with lighting unbuilt (UNBUILT_LIGHTING), and against targetActor: beyond the attenuation radius (OUT_OF_RANGE, with the radius that reaches it), outside a spot light's outer cone (OUTSIDE_CONE), or no lighting channel in common (CHANNEL_MISMATCH). A light not found is LIGHT_NOT_FOUND. Auto exposure can also hide a lighting change: look with a fixed exposure before judging by eye. The reply gives verdict (failed, unknown when a check could not be made, or ok), cause (the first failed check: check, code, detail and, when one fixes it, nextCall), causes (every failed check) and checks (each check made, in order, passed, failed or unknown). Nothing is changed.

widgetPath.description: The Widget Blueprint that should show, e.g. /Game/UI/WBP_HUD.

width.description: Width of every pass in pixels (default 960, 64 to 4096); the height follows the viewport's shape so the passes line up with it.

tools.name: manage_ai
tools.description: Build AI systems: AI controllers, Behavior Trees, Blackboards, EQS, perception, State Trees, Smart Objects, NavMesh settings, nav modifiers, links, and pathfinding.

activityTags.description: Registered gameplay tags added to the slot activity tags; an unregistered tag fails the call.

actorName.description: Label for the placed spawner; a label already in the level is refused.

agentStepHeight.description: Maximum step height the agent can climb (default: 35).

areaCost.description: Pathfinding cost multiplier for the area (1.0 = normal).

avoidanceWeight.description: RVO avoidance weight (0 or more); left unchanged when omitted.

bCreateBoxObstacle.description: true sets the box obstacle of the smart link, which marks the navmesh with obstacleAreaClass.

baseObjectClass.description: Class an Object key holds or a Class key names, as a class path or name (e.g. /Script/Engine.Actor); Object and Class keys only. Without it the key is based on Object, which actor-only key filters such as the MoveTo target skip.

blueprintPath.description: Blueprint that receives a NavModifier component; omit to place a NavModifierVolume in the editor level instead.

brakingDeceleration.description: Braking deceleration while walking; left unchanged when omitted.

broadcastInterval.description: Seconds between repeats of that notice; 0 sends it once.

broadcastRadius.description: Radius, in units, of the agents told when the smart link switches; the engine default 0 tells none.

cellCm.description: Spacing of the nav mesh samples, in cm (default 100): a smaller cell sees narrower gaps and takes longer.

center.description: Centre of the box to read, with extent; omit both to read the whole navigable area.

comment.description: Comment text applied to the graph node.

componentName.description: Name of the component to add.

compositeType.description: Composite node type: Selector, Sequence, or SimpleParallel (Parallel is the same).

configPath.description: Canonical /Game Mass Entity config asset path.

contextClass.description: Context class for contextType Custom: a Blueprint based on EnvQueryContext_BlueprintBase, or a context class path.

contextProperty.description: Context property of the generator or test to set (SearchCenter, GenerateAround, DistanceTo, Context); default the first one it has.

contextType.description: Querier (the AI running the query), Item (each item being tested), or Custom with contextClass.

control.description:
Which run behavior tree variant to run; omit for 'run'.
run: Make an AIController Blueprint run a Behavior Tree whenever it possesses a pawn: its On Possess event calls Run Behavior Tree (which also starts the Blackboard) with its BehaviorTree variable, set to behaviorTreePath as control=assign_tree does. Engine nodes in the Blueprint, compiled and saved, so it works in a packaged game, for every pawn whose AI Controller Class is this one and whose Auto Possess AI covers how it enters the level. Re-running replaces it; control=stop takes it out. NOT_AI_CONTROLLER for another Blueprint, NOT_FOUND for a missing tree, and refused during Play.
stop: Take out the Run Behavior Tree logic control=run wrote into an AIController Blueprint, so possessing a pawn no longer starts a tree (its BehaviorTree variable and On Possess event stay), compiled and saved; removed false, and nothing changed, when there was none.
assign_tree: Put a Behavior Tree in an AIController Blueprint: its BehaviorTree variable (one it declares, else a new instance-editable DefaultBehaviorTree) holds behaviorTreePath by default, compiled and saved. Nothing runs the tree until control=run writes Run Behavior Tree on possess, or the controller calls it itself. NOT_AI_CONTROLLER for another Blueprint, NOT_FOUND for a missing tree.
assign_blackboard: Assign a Blackboard to an AIController or Behavior Tree asset.

definitionPath.description: Canonical /Game Smart Object definition asset path.

direction.description: Which way agents may cross: BothWays (default), LeftToRight (start to end) or RightToLeft.

disabledAreaClass.description: Navigation area class the smart link marks while off, e.g. /Script/NavigationSystem.NavArea_Null (impassable).

edit.description:
Which edit behavior tree variant to run.
add_composite: Add a composite to a Behavior Tree and save it: compositeType Selector (runs its children until one succeeds), Sequence (until one fails) or SimpleParallel (Parallel is the same: its first child is the main task, the second runs beside it). It goes under parentNodeId (a composite by nodeId or nodeName), else under the root, and a tree with no root takes it as the root (isRoot). nodeName names it; nodeId and nodeName in the reply address it for edit=add_task, edit=add_decorator and edit=add_service. Another compositeType is refused (INVALID_ARGUMENT), as is a parent that is not found (PARENT_NOT_FOUND).
add_task: Add a task node to a Behavior Tree asset.
add_decorator: Add a decorator to a Behavior Tree node, or to the root when no node is named.
add_service: Add a service to a Behavior Tree asset.
add_node: Add a node through the Behavior Tree graph route.
add_subnode: Add a Behavior Tree decorator or service subnode.
connect: Connect Behavior Tree graph nodes.
break_connections: Break Behavior Tree graph connections.
configure_node: Configure a Behavior Tree node.
set_node_properties: Set Behavior Tree graph node properties.
remove_node: Remove a Behavior Tree graph node.

enabledAreaClass.description: Navigation area class the smart link marks while on, e.g. /Script/NavigationSystem.NavArea_Default.

endPoint.description: End of the link, relative to the link actor (its location and rotation).

enumType.description: Enum an Enum key holds, by path (/Game/Enums/E_State, /Script/Engine.ECollisionChannel); Enum keys only. Without it the key has no enumerators to hold.

oneOf.description: Half-size of that box per axis, in cm.
Half-size of the placed NavModifierVolume (volume form only; default 200, 200, 100).

extent.description: Half-size of that box per axis, in cm.

failsafeExtent.description: Failsafe extent used when the actor has no collision.

failsafeToDefaultNavmesh.description: Fall back to the default navmesh area when the modifier area class is unset.

fixedAreaEnteringCost.description: Flat cost added once when a path enters the area; left unchanged when omitted.

focusOp.description:
Which set focus variant to run; omit for 'set'.
set: Make an AIController Blueprint keep its focus on a target: the player 0 pawn (focusPlayer) or the first actor carrying focusTag. Each frame it has no focus actor, its Tick finds the target and calls Set Focus, so a target that spawns after the AI, or respawns, is picked up again; a pawn that uses its controller rotation turns to face it. Engine nodes in the Blueprint, compiled and saved; re-running replaces the target and focusOp=clear takes it out. Exactly one of focusPlayer and focusTag (INVALID_ARGUMENT); NOT_AI_CONTROLLER for another Blueprint.
clear: Take out the focus logic focusOp=set wrote into an AIController Blueprint, so it stops seeking a target each frame (a focus already set in a running game stays until something clears it), compiled and saved; removed false, and nothing changed, when there was none.

focusPlayer.description: Focus the pawn of player 0, picked up again when it spawns late or respawns.

focusTag.description: Focus the first actor carrying this tag (mark the target with control_actor add_tag).

fromActor.description: An actor whose location is the start, in place of from.

generatorSettings.description: Settings the generator reads, refused when it does not: ActorsOfClass searchRadius (also keeps items inside it) and actorClass; SimpleGrid and PathingGrid gridSize (half the grid side) and spacesBetween; OnCircle searchRadius or outerRadius (the circle radius) and spacesBetween; Donut innerRadius and outerRadius. Where a generator centers is set with add_eqs_context.

goal.description: Point to walk to from the start.

goalActor.description: Actor to walk to from the start, in place of goal.

image.description: Also write a top-down PNG of the spaces (each its own colour, doors white, start green, goal red) under the project's Saved/EngineWire/Layout; its path is imagePath.

info.description:
Which get ai info variant to run; omit for 'ai'.
ai: Read AI asset information.
navigation: Read navigation state and settings.
path: Say whether a pawn could walk from one point to another on the editor level's nav mesh, and why not: an end off the mesh within projectExtent (start_off_navmesh, goal_off_navmesh), both ends on it with nothing connecting them (no_path), or a partial path that stops gap cm short (partial). from and to are points, or fromActor and toActor stand for where those actors are. The reply gives reachable, reason, the path points (100 at most), pathLength in cm, and where each end lands on the mesh (fromOnMesh, toOnMesh). Refused with NAV_DATA_MISSING when the level has no nav mesh, and NAV_BUILD_IN_PROGRESS while it builds.

isInstanceSynced.description: Share the value of the key across every Blackboard component using this asset, so a value one AI sets reaches them all.

jumpZVelocity.description: Initial upward jump velocity; left unchanged when omitted.

keyName.description: Blackboard key name, matched in any case.

kind.description:
Which create behavior tree variant to run; omit for 'behavior_tree'.
behavior_tree: Create a Behavior Tree asset named name in path (default /Game/AI/BehaviorTrees; savePath when path is absent), saved (saved); an asset already at the path is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS). It has no root yet: the first add_composite_node becomes the root.
graph_route: Create a Behavior Tree named name in savePath (default /Game; a path without a leading slash goes under /Game) with its editor graph, saved (saved). An asset already at the path is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS).
blackboard: Create a Blackboard asset named name in path (default /Game/AI/Blackboards), saved (saved). A Blackboard already there is kept as it is (alreadyExisted true); another kind of asset at the path is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS).

linkEnabled.description: Switch the smart link on (true) or off.

linkType.description: simple (the point link of the proxy) or smart (its smart link, which can switch on and off).

oneOf.description: World location for the spawned link actor.
World location of the spawner (default the world origin).

location.description: World location for the spawned link actor.

loseSightRadius.description: Radius at which sight is lost.

maxAcceleration.description: Maximum acceleration; left unchanged when omitted.

maxFlySpeed.description: Maximum flying speed; left unchanged when omitted.

maxNodes.description: Most samples to take (default 6000); a larger area is read with a wider cell, and the message says so.

maxWalkSpeed.description: Maximum ground speed; left unchanged when omitted.

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

nodeName.description: Name for the created composite node.

obstacleAreaClass.description: Area the box obstacle marks (default /Script/NavigationSystem.NavArea_Null, impassable).

obstacleExtent.description: Half size of the box obstacle (default 100 on each axis).

obstacleOffset.description: Offset of the box obstacle from the link actor.

offset.description: Slot offset relative to the definition origin.

optionIndex.description: Option whose generator takes the context when no testIndex is sent (default 0).

orientRotationToMovement.description: Rotate the pawn toward its movement direction; left unchanged when omitted.

parentConfigPath.description: Parent Mass entity config asset to inherit from.

parentNodeId.description: ID of the parent node: 'root', a node GUID, or a node id as returned by add_composite/add_task (for example BTComposite_Selector_0).

parentStateName.description: Parent state name for the added state.

path.description: Canonical /Game output path for the created asset.

projectExtent.description: How far from an end, per axis in cm, the nav mesh may be found (default 100, 100, 250).

oneOf.description: Key-value property map.
Task property values keyed by UPROPERTY name, imported by reflection onto the task instance.
Trait property values keyed by UPROPERTY name.

roomWidthCm.description: How wide a space must be to count as a room, in cm (default 400): some point of it lies at least half this far inside the nav mesh's edge (which keeps the agent's radius off the walls), counted in whole cells. Narrower spaces are corridors.

rotation.description: Rotation as {pitch, yaw, roll} in degrees.

rotationRate.description: Yaw rotation rate in degrees per second; left unchanged when omitted.

save.description: Save the Blueprint asset after adding the component (Blueprint form only).

savePath.description: Directory path used when saving the created Behavior Tree.

schema.description: What runs the tree: component (default, a StateTreeComponent on any actor), ai (a StateTreeAIComponent on an AI controller, UE 5.4+), or the class path of another State Tree schema (a UStateTreeSchema subclass, such as /Script/MassAIBehavior.MassStateTreeSchema for Mass entities).

selectionBehavior.description: State selection behavior (e.g. TryEnterState, TrySelectChildrenInOrder, TryFollowTransitions).

setting.description:
Which configure navigation variant to run.
mesh_settings: Configure project NavMesh generation settings.
agent_properties: Set project navigation agent properties.
area_cost: Configure navigation area cost data.
area_class: Set the navigation area class on a placed actor that already carries a NavModifierComponent (add one with create_nav_modifier first).
nav_link: Change the link of a placed NavLinkProxy (actorName): startPoint and endPoint (relative to the actor) and direction go on its smart link when it uses one, else on its point link, and snapRadius on the point link (refused for a smart link). Only what is sent changes, and a call that sends none of them is refused. The navmesh takes the change at once; one undo step, the level left unsaved; the reply gives the link as it is now.
link_type: Switch a placed NavLinkProxy (actorName) between a simple link, its point link, and a smart link, its smart link alone (linkType simple or smart), carrying the endpoints and direction over. A proxy already of that type changes nothing (changed false). One undo step; the level is left unsaved.
smart_link_behavior: Change the smart link of a NavLinkProxy (actorName): linkEnabled switches it on or off; enabledAreaClass and disabledAreaClass are the navigation areas it marks while on and off (NavArea_Null blocks it); broadcastRadius and broadcastInterval set who hears it switch, heard only while its Notify When Enabled or Disabled is on, and the one left out keeps its value; bCreateBoxObstacle true sets its box obstacle of obstacleAreaClass (default NavArea_Null), obstacleExtent (default 100) and obstacleOffset. An area class that does not load is refused before anything changes, as is a call that sets nothing. The settings stay on a proxy that uses its point link and apply once setting=link_type makes it smart. One undo step; the level is left unsaved.
rebuild: Rebuild navigation for the loaded editor world.

slotIndex.description: Index of the slot to configure.

snapRadius.description: How far from each end of the point link the navmesh is looked for (default 30).

spawnCount.description: Number of entities the spawner creates.

startActor.description: Actor where routes start, standing on the nav mesh read (default the first PlayerStart, when it does); without a start, no walk or unreachable list is given.

startPoint.description: Start of the link, relative to the link actor (its location and rotation).

stateType.description: State (default), Group, Linked, LinkedAsset (UE 5.4+) or Subtree.

subnodeType.description: Behavior Tree subnode kind for add_subnode.

taskIndex.description: Zero-based task index in the state (alternative to taskName).

taskName.description: Task to configure, matched by class or instance name (defaults to the first task).

teamId.description: Team id to store, 0 to 254 (255 means no team).

testIndex.description: Test index counted across all options of the query, in the order the tests were added (the testIndex add_eqs_test returned).

tileSizeUU.description: NavMesh tile size in Unreal units (default: 1000).

toActor.description: An actor whose location is the goal, in place of to.

traitClass.description: Mass trait class (short name or path, a UMassEntityTraitBase subclass): edited when the config has it, added when it does not.

triggerType.description: OnStateCompleted (default), OnStateSucceeded, OnStateFailed, OnTick, OnEvent (needs an event tag) or OnDelegate (newer engines).

useAccelerationForPaths.description: Path following uses acceleration instead of setting velocity directly; left unchanged when omitted.

useRVOAvoidance.description: Enable RVO avoidance; left unchanged when omitted.

value.description: The default, in the kind the key holds: a boolean, a number, {x, y, z}, {pitch, yaw, roll}, text, an enumerator, or an asset or class path.

tools.name: manage_asset
tools.description: Create/import/manage assets, material graphs, material instances, procedural textures, render targets, and dependency analysis.

additionalOutputs.description: Extra output pins after the return value, each {name, type}: type Float1 (default), Float2, Float3, Float4 or MaterialAttributes. Assign each by name in the HLSL (Emis = ...;) and wire it as "$node.Name".

adjust.description:
Which adjust texture variant to run.
curves: Apply curve-based adjustments to a texture.
levels: Adjust levels (black/white points, gamma) on a texture.
blur: Apply a blur filter to a texture.
sharpen: Apply a sharpen filter to a texture.
desaturate: Desaturate a texture by an amount.
invert: Invert color channels of a texture.

againstPath.description: Another asset of the same kind to compare with, such as a duplicate kept as a backup. Omitted, the asset is compared with its own saved file, so the reply lists its unsaved edits.

alphaTexture.description: Alpha channel source: an 8-bit BGRA8 or G8 texture.

assetId.description: Fab asset id, used as the cache key.

assetName.description: The name for the import's one mesh: SM_<assetName>, or SK_ for a skeletal mesh, with its material instance and textures following (MI_<assetName>, T_<assetName>_<suffix>); a surface with no mesh is named by its one material instance. Letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit, 64 at most, for example ConcreteBarrier. Without destinationPath the assets are renamed where they are. Not applied when the import holds no single mesh or material instance to name; relocationNote says so.

oneOf.description: Several asset paths checked in one call; the reply maps each to true or false under existsByPath.
Absolute paths of the downloaded pack files. Used with folderName to synthesize a single-entry envelope when payload is omitted.
Assets to delete (/Game paths); one that does not exist is skipped.
Explicit asset paths.

Several asset paths to process in one call: lods generates LODs for each; mesh_materials sets the same materials entries on each mesh by slot name, passing over a slot a mesh lacks (an entry no mesh has fails the call), as a whole imported pack needs.
Several static meshes, each turned on, rebuilt and saved in this one call (a whole imported pack, or every heavy mesh get_stats statsKind=frame lists); one mesh that fails does not stop the others.

assetPaths.description: Absolute paths of the downloaded pack files. Used with folderName to synthesize a single-entry envelope when payload is omitted.

assetType.description: Bridge asset type: 3d, 3dplant, atlas or surface.

assets.description: Several materials or material instances at once, in place of assetPath: each {assetPath, and parameters or parameterName with value}; the call's own save applies to every entry. Every entry is reported under assets, and the call fails naming any that did not apply.

backgroundColor.description: Background (default transparent, so the alpha channel is the text mask) as {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1.

baseTexture.description: Base texture path; its source must be an 8-bit BGRA8 or single-channel G8 texture (a channel_extract result, read as gray in R, G and B with alpha 255). Other source formats (G16, RGBA16, float, HDR) fail with an error naming the format found.

blendMode.description: Blend mode, such as Opaque, Masked, Translucent, Additive, Modulate or AlphaComposite. The Details panel label and the BLEND_ name work too.

blendTexture.description: Blend texture path; it must have the width and height of baseTexture. Its source can be BGRA8 or G8 whichever baseTexture is. Other source formats (G16, RGBA16, float, HDR) fail with an error naming the format found.

blendType.description: Blend for the layers that do not name one: LB_WeightBlend (default), LB_HeightBlend or LB_AlphaBlend (Weight, Height or Alpha work too).

blueTexture.description: Blue channel source: an 8-bit BGRA8 or G8 texture.

caption.description: What it shows, in plain words (a mossy grey boulder, flat on top); empty with no tags removes the caption.

tags.description: Words or short phrases to find it by (rock, moss, cliff edge).

checkoutFiles.description: Check out files in source control.

class.description: Only assets of this class by its name (default: likeAsset's class, else every class).

classNames.description: Asset classes to filter: a short class name (StaticMesh, Blueprint, ObjectRedirector, InputMappingContext) or a full class path (/Script/Engine.StaticMesh).

clearExisting.description: Drop every existing row first (default false): before an import, or instead of migrating rows to a new row struct.

collectionPath.description: Material Parameter Collection a CollectionParameter node reads (name picks its parameter); a collection that does not load, or lacks the parameter, adds nothing and fails, listing its parameters.

collisionType.description: box, sphere or capsule: one shape fitted to the mesh bounds (a capsule stands upright along Z) replaces its simple collision. complex: the render triangles are the collision, exact for terrain-like or concave meshes but costlier. none: no collision, so pawns and traces pass through.

color.description: Text colour (default white) as {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1.

colour.description: A colour the asset should mostly be: #RRGGBB or red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, pink, brown, black, white, grey.

columnTypes.description: Column struct paths to read, for example "/Script/Fab.FabObjectNameColumn". Defaults to the name column plus "/Script/Fab.FabObjectColumn", which carries AssetId, ListingType, Seller and Source. Selecting a column is also the row filter, so naming one Fab does not write for every row will hide rows. Override this when a Fab update renames or adds columns; unresolved paths are reported rather than failing the call.

combineMeshes.description: Only for source mesh formats (fbx, obj, gltf, glb, usdz) that Fab imports itself; ignored for Megascans and unreal-engine packs. Omit to leave Fab's behaviour alone: every mesh of a file is merged into ONE static mesh. false imports each mesh as its own asset: the adapter switches off Interchange's mesh combining on the pipelines Fab generated for this import, and the status read's combineMeshesApplied says whether that landed in time (COMBINE_UNSUPPORTED refuses the call when this engine gives no way to). true accepts the single merged mesh explicitly, which a scene-sized file (one mesh file of 50 MB or more) requires.

compileOp.description:
Which compile material variant to run; omit for 'compile'.
compile: Compile a material and report its compile errors.
rebuild: Rebuild and compile a material (alias of compileOp=compile).

compressionSettings.description: Engine compression name, with or without TC_: Default, Normalmap, Masks, Grayscale, Displacementmap, VectorDisplacementmap, HDR, EditorIcon (UserInterface2D), Alpha, DistanceFieldFont, HDR_Compressed, BC7, HalfFloat, and from UE 5.1 SingleFloat and HDR_F32.

constA.description: Value used while input A is unwired (Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, Lerp).

constB.description: Value used while input B is unwired (Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, Lerp).

createPhysicsAsset.description: Skeletal mesh: make a physics asset for it (default true); false makes none.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned by a previous list response. Forward verbatim to resume.

curvePoints.description: Curve control points as {x, y} pairs in 0-1; at least two.

oneOf.description: Initial value for a Constant (number) or Constant3Vector (rgb array or {r,g,b}) node.
Default value as string.

deleteScope.description:
Which delete data table row variant to run; omit for 'row'.
row: Delete the row rowName from a DataTable; a name the table lacks is ROW_NOT_FOUND. One undo step (the undo block in the reply says so); the table is saved unless save is false (saved).
all: Clear all rows from a DataTable.

destinationDirectory.description: Where the pack lands. Defaults to the Fab library cache directory, which list_fab_downloads and the fabLibrary source root both read.

destinationFolder.description: Folder to move the renamed struct into, e.g. /Game/Data.

destinationName.description: Name of the new asset. With destinationPath it is placed in that folder; on its own the copy stays beside the source.

oneOf.description: Root the copied tree lands under. Leave at "/Game" to preserve the source layout and keep internal references valid; any deeper path relocates the tree and flags referenceIntegrity as "at-risk".

A /Game folder to move what the import created to, for example /Game/Props/Barriers. The layout beneath the import's own folder (StaticMeshes, Materials, Textures) is kept under it. Omit to leave the import where Fab put it. The shared master materials in /Game/Fab/Materials, MaterialFunctions and Textures never move, and a unreal-engine pack is left where Fab put it.
Destination /Game asset path.

Folder for the copy, e.g. /Game/Structs, when destinationName is given, the path ends in "/" or the folder exists; the copy is destinationPath/destinationName, or keeps the source name without one. Otherwise the full new asset path, e.g. /Game/Structs/S_WeaponRow_V2. A copy onto an existing struct is refused with ALREADY_EXISTS.
The folder the asset goes in, e.g. /Game/Imports (it keeps the source file's name), or an object path such as /Game/Chars/SK_Hero.SK_Hero to name it.
Where the copy goes: a folder (one that exists, or ending in /) where it keeps the source name or takes newName, a full asset path, or a bare name, which lands beside the source.

destinationPath.description: A /Game folder to move what the import created to, for example /Game/Props/Barriers. The layout beneath the import's own folder (StaticMeshes, Materials, Textures) is kept under it. Omit to leave the import where Fab put it. The shared master materials in /Game/Fab/Materials, MaterialFunctions and Textures never move, and a unreal-engine pack is left where Fab put it.

direction.description: Connection direction to report (inputs or outputs).

downloadType.description: Transfer mode: "http" or "buildpatch". BuildPatchServices is for Marketplace-era packs; pointing it at a plain URL stalls rather than failing, so it must be opted into.

downloadUrl.description: Signed https download URL issued by Fab. Short-lived: a stale URL fails with DOWNLOAD_FAILED.

downstream.description: Report downstream connections instead of upstream.

dryRun.description: Check the batch without running a step (default false): every edit and "$id", with every problem in one reply. Node names, pins and values are checked only when it runs. Nothing is changed, compiled or saved.

edit.description:
Which edit data table variant to run.
create: Create a new DataTable asset.
create_row_struct: Create a new UScriptStruct suitable as a DataTable row type.
add_row: Add a row named rowName to a DataTable from rowData (column names as the row struct spells them; columns left out take the row struct defaults). A taken name is ROW_ALREADY_EXISTS, data the struct refuses INVALID_ROW_DATA. One undo step (the undo block in the reply says so); the table is saved unless save is false (saved).
update_row: Change columns of an existing DataTable row: the columns rowData names change, the others keep their values. One undo step (the undo block in the reply says so); the table is saved unless save is false (saved).
import_rows: Import multiple rows into a DataTable from an array.
set_row_struct: Bind a row UScriptStruct to an existing DataTable.
set_struct_as_row_struct: Set an existing UScriptStruct as the row struct for a DataTable (a user-defined struct is validated and compiled first).

endColor.description: End colour (default white) as {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1.

endPin.description: Terminal pin name to stop the chain walk at.

exportMode.description: Bridge export mode: normal, normal_drag or progressive.

exposeToLibrary.description: Expose in the material function library.

expressionIndex.description: Zero-based position in the expression list; picks the node when nodeId is omitted.

filter.description: Case-sensitive substring matched against each serialized row. Use "fab" to drop the legacy "uem" engine and plugin entries that otherwise fill the row limit.

fixupRedirectors.description: Default true. After a delete that removed something, resolve the redirectors that already exist in the folders the assets were deleted from, subfolders included: their referencers are re-pointed and re-saved, then the redirectors nothing points at any more are removed. Deleting creates no redirectors, so this only cleans older ones.

folderName.description: Destination folder name under /Game/Megascans. Required when synthesizing from assetPaths.

fontFamily.description: Font asset, e.g. /Engine/EngineFonts/Roboto (default) or a project font.

force.description: Delete an asset even when assets outside this delete still reference it (their references break). Default false: such an asset is kept and listed in referencedPaths, and so is one of this delete that only a kept asset uses. Folders are always deleted whole.

format.description: File format; default glb, or the extension outputPath ends in. glb and gltf are scaled to meters with materials converted to glTF PBR; fbx and obj keep centimeters.

greenTexture.description: Green channel source: an 8-bit BGRA8 or G8 texture.

importAnimations.description: Import animation takes from an FBX. Off by default, which imports mesh only.

importMesh.description: With skeletonPath: import the skeletal mesh onto that skeleton (its takes too when importAnimations) instead of the take alone.

importMorphTargets.description: Skeletal mesh: import its morph targets (blend shapes).

includeLevel.description: Also search the actors and components of the open level: true or false outright; omitted, only when that level lies under packagePaths (always with the default /Game).

includeMetadata.description: When true, include the file size and modification date of each asset.

includePackageCounts.description: Include packageCount per source. Costs a recursive file scan per returned entry, so leave off for a broad sweep and turn on once the candidate list is short.

includeTags.description: When true, include asset tags in the listing response.

index.description: Split position: every value from this zero-based index on is copied into the new enum. Pass this or values.

info.description:
Which get material info variant to run; omit for 'material'.
material: Read a material or material function (domain, blend mode, parameters, node count), or a material instance (its parent and parameter overrides).
function: Retrieve information about a material function.
find_node: Find a node in a material graph by type or name.
node_details: Retrieve details of a material node.
node_properties: Retrieve properties of a node in a material graph.
node_connections: Retrieve connections for a node in a material graph.
node_chain: Retrieve the chain of nodes connected to a starting node.
subgraph: Retrieve the connected subgraph from a starting node.

inputType.description: input only: Scalar, Vector2, Vector3 (default), Vector4, Texture2D, TextureCube, Bool or MaterialAttributes (Float1 to Float4 work too); another type is refused. An output takes the type of what is wired into it.

oneOf.description: Input definitions, each {name}; wire one with connect_nodes targetPin set to that name.
Replacement input list, each {name}; inputs whose names stay keep their connections.

inputs.description: Input definitions, each {name}; wire one with connect_nodes targetPin set to that name.

instances.description: Several instances in one call, in place of name: each {name, and any of parentMaterial, savePath, parameters, save}; the call's own parentMaterial, savePath and save are every entry's defaults. Every entry is reported under instances; the call fails naming any that were not created.

io.description:
Which add function io variant to run.
input: Add a function input to a material function.
output: Add a function output to a material function.

justification.description: Line alignment of multi-line text: left, center (default) or right.

key.description: Metadata key on the entry, such as ToolTip.

kind.description:
Which create material variant to run; omit for 'material'.
material: Create a new material asset.
decal: Create a decal material asset (DeferredDecal domain, Translucent by default).
landscape: Create a landscape material asset (Surface domain, Opaque by default).
post_process: Create a post-process material asset (PostProcess domain by default).
function: Create a new material function asset.
parameter_collection: Create a Material Parameter Collection, values every material that reads it shares, or add parameters to one and set their defaults.

layers.description: The paint layers, in order, each { name } or { name, blendType } to give that layer its own blend.

letterSpacing.description: Extra space between letters, in thousandths of an em (0 normal, 100 airy, negative tighter).

likeAsset.description: An example asset, by package path: assets like it are found (its own pack first, then by look and size).

oneOf.description: Maximum rows to return, clamped plugin-side.
Assets on the page (1-16, default 12).
Rows returned (1-50, default 10).
Page size (1-500, default 50).

lineWidth.description: Grid line width as a fraction of a tile (default 0.02).

listingId.description: Fab listing uid, as it appears in a fab.com/listings/<uid> URL. Restricted to [A-Za-z0-9_-], 64 characters max, because it is used to build an API path.

listingType.description: Only this content kind, as a row's listingType names it, for example 3d-model or material. One token of [A-Za-z0-9_-], at most 40 characters. Omit for every kind.

lodBias.description: Whole mips to drop (a fraction is cut off): 1 halves each side, 0 restores full size.

lodCount.description: Number of LOD levels to generate (1-50, default 4).

lookup.description:
Which inspect asset variant to run.
metadata: Retrieve metadata and tags for an asset.
dependencies: List the packages an asset uses, or with referencers the packages that use it. Direct packages only; lookup "graph" walks dependencies recursively.
graph: Retrieve the asset reference graph directly via the lookup=graph bridge action.
validate: Confirm an asset exists and loads. It runs no content, reference or data checks.
report: Generate an asset report for a directory.
diff: Compare a Blueprint, DataTable or data asset with its saved file (its unsaved edits) or with another asset: changed, added and removed properties and class defaults, Blueprint components and graph changes, DataTable rows. Read-only.

maintenance.description:
Which maintain content variant to run.
bulk_rename: Rename multiple assets in one call: by a pattern (search/replace, prefix, suffix) over a folder or a list, or to explicit new names with renames.
fixup_redirectors: Fix up redirector assets in a directory.
refresh_blueprints: Refresh every node of the Blueprints under a folder (or listed), then compile and save each; run it after renaming or moving classes so casts and node titles follow.
migrate: Copy a content tree from an allowlisted source root into this project and scan it into the asset registry. This is how a Quixel Bridge / Fab pack or an engine template (its Blueprints, meshes, materials and maps) becomes usable content in the current project. IMPORTANT: package files store their references as absolute /Game/... paths and a copy cannot rewrite them, so the default destinationPath of "/Game" — which reproduces the source layout exactly — is the only setting that guarantees the migrated assets still resolve each other. Any other destinationPath relocates the tree and comes back with referenceIntegrity "at-risk". Run with dryRun first to see the file count and the package paths that will appear.
