marketplace.description:
Which import marketplace asset variant to run.
fab_listing: Start importing one Fab listing into this project through the signed-in Fab tab and return as soon as Fab accepts the download. The tab is opened when it is closed and the page is waited for up to 15 seconds (PAGE_NOT_READY after that); the account must be signed in there. The content does NOT exist yet when this replies: downloading and importing take minutes and hold the editor, far longer than a client waits, so poll asset.query_marketplace with lookup=fab_import_status and the returned operationId until phase is done or failed (marketplace=fab_cancel stops one that is queued or downloading). Never call this again to see progress: a repeat for a listing that is queued or running only hands back the same operation (alreadyRunning), and a repeat that asks for a different quality, combineMeshes, destinationPath or assetName is refused with ADD_ALREADY_RUNNING, naming that operation, since it would ignore them. One import runs at a time, so an add made while another runs is queued (phase queued, queuePosition) and starts by itself, first in first out, and the status read lists the queue; only a full queue (8 waiting) is refused with QUEUE_FULL, which names the import at its head with its phase, bytes and elapsed time and returns the status call as its nextCall. A queued add is not put to Fab until its turn, so a refusal it would have got at once (NO_IMPORTABLE_FORMAT, COMPLETE_PROJECT, LARGE_SCENE_FILE) arrives later as the status read's failureCode. It claims the listing first: Fab answers 404 for a download the account does not own, so this posts add-to-library exactly as the Fab UI does when you press Add to Project — a real change to your Fab library, free to claim and harmless to repeat on a listing you already own. It claims each free license of the listing in turn until Fab accepts one. Then it picks the format the Fab importer accepts (unreal-engine, else gltf, glb, fbx, obj or usdz) and hands over the download. A unreal-engine pack that declares no build for the running engine imports the highest build at or below it, else the lowest above it, and engineMatch (older or newer) and engineVersion say which. A complete project (COMPLETE_PROJECT) cannot be added to an existing project: it is refused after the claim, so it is in your library to create a project from, and the reply says to create it as a new project from Fab and migrate its content. A MetaHuman listing (METAHUMAN_FORMAT) is refused before anything is claimed, because Fab hands it to a workflow this add does not drive. A listing Fab will not give an address for fails with NO_DOWNLOAD_URL naming the step that refused (license: no offer to claim; claim: Fab refused the account; download-info: Fab answered no address), Fab's HTTP status and Fab's own words, so the cause is in the reply rather than the editor log; the reply names the format, the file and its quality tier, and the file size when Fab publishes one. A Megascans listing publishes one file per quality tier (raw, high, mid, low); quality takes exactly the tier named, and a tier the listing does not publish is refused with QUALITY_NOT_AVAILABLE, naming the tiers it does, before anything downloads. Without quality it takes the best game-ready tier: high, else mid, low, raw. A listing that publishes no tiers, and a unreal-engine pack, ignore quality. Supply only a listing id; the signed URL, EOS token and session cookie stay inside the page and reach no response or log. Fab chooses the destination folder (a Megascans add lands under a machine-named tree such as /Game/Fab/Megascans/3D/<name>_<id>/High/<id>_tier_1), and the status read reports importedRoot once the import is done, by which time the packages Fab left unsaved in memory have been saved, and they are saved again 15 and 60 seconds after the import ends for anything the engine marks dirty late; the status read's saved, savedCount and unsavedPackages say how it went and name a package that could not be saved. destinationPath moves what the import created in its own folders to a /Game folder you name, keeping the layout beneath it (StaticMeshes, Materials, Textures), and assetName names the import's one mesh SM_<assetName> (SK_ for a skeletal mesh) with its material instance and textures following (MI_<assetName>, T_<assetName>_<suffix>); a surface has no mesh and is named by its one material instance. It runs the move and rename that asset.move runs, so references and settings follow and the redirectors left behind are fixed, and it is all or nothing: a name already taken stops it before anything moves. It never touches the shared master materials, material functions and textures in /Game/Fab/Materials, /Game/Fab/MaterialFunctions and /Game/Fab/Textures, and a unreal-engine pack, which arrives outside /Game/Fab, stays where Fab put it. The status read's relocated, movedCount and relocationNote say what happened. Fab's importer merges every mesh in a source file (fbx, obj, gltf, glb, usdz) into ONE static mesh, whatever the project's import settings say, and a file that is really a scene became a single unplaceable mesh that needed gigabytes to build while the editor stayed held for many minutes. So a single mesh file of 50 MB or more (Megascans and unreal-engine packs are not affected) is refused with LARGE_SCENE_FILE, before anything downloads, until combineMeshes says which way to import it.
fab_cancel: Stop a Fab import that asset.import_marketplace_asset (marketplace=fab_listing) started, by its operationId. Fab gives three handles and this uses exactly those: an add still waiting in the queue is dropped and never reaches Fab; a unreal-engine pack that is downloading is stopped by pressing the Cancel button on Fab's own download notification; an import whose files Interchange is translating is told to cancel its tasks. The download of a source format (fbx, gltf, obj, usdz, Megascans) has no Cancel anywhere in Fab, so it is refused with NOT_CANCELLABLE and the reason, as is an add that is still resolving (seconds, and not interruptible) and an import past its download with no Interchange task to stop; the status read's cancellable says beforehand whether a cancel would work. A running import ends as failed with failureCode CANCELLED within a second (phase cancelling until then), with whatever had already landed listed and left unsaved and unmoved, so asset.delete removes it. A call is served only while the editor is free: while Fab builds meshes the editor is held and every call answers EDITOR_BLOCKED, so a cancel has to come before that. A finished import is refused with ALREADY_FINISHED and an unknown id with NOT_FOUND.
fab_download: Download a Fab asset through the Fab plugin's own downloader (FFabDownloadRequest), so the transfer uses its HTTP/BuildPatchServices path rather than a parallel implementation that would miss its retry handling. IMPORTANT: the signed downloadUrl is NOT minted here — Fab issues it from its authenticated web session and no C++ entry point initiates that, so supply a URL obtained from the Fab tab's own flow. Once the pack lands, asset.migrate_assets with sourceRoot "fabLibrary" places it into /Game. Acquires content against the signed-in account, so it is an explicit-consent write.
megascans: Import a downloaded Megascans pack through the Bridge plugin's own importer, headlessly — no Bridge window, no drag, no sign-in. Calls FAssetsImportController::DataReceived, the exported entry point the Bridge desktop app drives over its local TCP socket, so quality tiers, master materials and the MSPresets setup all apply exactly as they would from the UI. This imports content ALREADY on disk, downloaded by the Bridge app. A Megascans listing that is not downloaded yet is fetched and imported by marketplace=fab_listing instead, which needs no Bridge window. Assets land under /Game/Megascans.

materialDomain.description: Material domain: Surface, DeferredDecal, LightFunction, Volume, PostProcess or UI (a widget, brush or font material). The Details panel label (User Interface) and the MD_ name work too.

materialProperty.description:
Which set material property variant to run.
blend_mode: Set the blend mode of a material.
domain: Set the material domain of a material.
shading_model: Set the shading model of a material.
two_sided: Set the two-sided flag on a material.

slot.description: The slot to set: its 0-based index (9) or its slot name ("hull"), as inspect_object objectKind=mesh lists them under materialSlots.

materialPath.description: Material or material instance asset path, e.g. /Game/Materials/M_Hull. It must load: a path that does not is refused, never swapped for a default material.

materials.description: The slots to set, one entry per slot: [{slot, materialPath}]. slot is a 0-based index or a slot name (inspect_object objectKind=mesh lists both under materialSlots). Every entry is checked first. One that is refused (index out of range, unknown slot name, a material that does not load) is named under refused and fails the call, while the valid entries are applied together in a single rebuild of the mesh.

maxPackages.description: Refuse the migration when the source holds more files than this, so a mistyped source cannot copy tens of gigabytes. Narrow with subPath or raise deliberately.

memberType.description: Unreal property type: Bool, Int, Float, String, Name, Text, Vector, Rotator, Transform, Object, SoftObject, Class, SoftClass, Enum:<Name>, Struct:<Path>, or with container prefix Array:..., Set:..., Map:<K>,<V>:

oneOf.description: Member definitions, each { name, type } (or memberName, memberType) with optional defaultValue, tooltip and metadata.

The columns of the new row struct, each { name, type } (or memberName, memberType) with optional defaultValue, tooltip and metadata. type takes Bool, Int, Float, String, Name, Text, Vector, Rotator, Transform, Object, SoftObject, Class, SoftClass, Enum:<Name> or Struct:<Path>, or a container: Array:..., Set:..., Map:<K>,<V>. Without members the struct keeps one placeholder member.

members.description: Member definitions, each { name, type } (or memberName, memberType) with optional defaultValue, tooltip and metadata.

oneOf.description: Metadata key-value pairs.
Metadata key/value pairs.

migrateExistingRows.description: Re-import the existing rows under the new struct (default true); rows that do not fit are reported in invalidRows.

name.description: Asset name.

neverStream.description: true keeps every mip resident, false lets the texture stream; leaving it out is refused.

newName.description: Name for the copy: in the destinationPath folder, or beside the source when destinationPath is left out.

newStructPath.description: Full new object path, e.g. /Game/Data/S_WeaponStats.S_WeaponStats; alternative to newName.

newValueName.description: New name the editor shows; the internal name stored values hold stays.

noWeightBlend.description: Exclude the layer from weight blending (default false).

nodeId.description: A node, by the id the graph lists: material and function report only the connections touching it; node_details, node_properties and node_connections describe it; node_chain and subgraph start from it (node_chain also takes it as startNodeId; subgraph needs it unless orphansOnly is true).

oneOf.description: Node IDs to delete in one batch, in place of nodeId.
Only report connections touching these nodes.

nodeIds.description: Node IDs to delete in one batch, in place of nodeId.

nodeKind.description:
Which add material node variant to run; omit for 'node'.
node: Add a generic material node by type.
custom_expression: Add a custom HLSL expression node to a material graph.
fresnel: Add a fresnel node to a material graph.
if: Add a conditional If node to a material graph.
math: Add a math operation node to a material graph.
noise: Add a noise node to a material graph.
panner: Add a panner node to a material graph.
pixel_depth: Add a pixel depth node to a material graph.
reflection_vector: Add a reflection vector node to a material graph.
rotator: Add a rotator node to a material graph.
scalar_parameter: Add a scalar parameter node to a material graph.
static_switch_parameter: Add a static switch parameter node to a material graph.
switch: Add a switch node to a material graph.
texture_coordinate: Add a texture coordinate node to a material graph.
texture_sample: Add a texture sample node to a material graph.
vector_parameter: Add a vector parameter node to a material graph.
vertex_normal: Add a vertex normal node to a material graph.
voronoi: Add a voronoi noise node to a material graph.
world_position: Add a world position node to a material graph.
material_function: Insert a material function reference into a material graph.
landscape_layer: Create the landscape layer info asset (the weight layer a landscape material paints) for a layer name, beside the material or in path.
batch: Build a material graph in one call: add nodes, wire them to each other and to the material output, and set material properties, with $id references between steps.

nodeName.description: Name to find: a node id, parameter name, function input or output name, or custom node title (substring match).

nodeType.description: Material expression to add: its class name without the MaterialExpression prefix (Constant, Lerp, TextureSample, ScalarParameter, Multiply...) or the full class name; Float, Color, TexCoord and StaticSwitch are accepted as short names. An unknown type adds nothing (UNKNOWN_TYPE).

noiseType.description: Perlin (default), FBM (same as Perlin), Ridged or Billow.

oneOf.description: Brick row offset, 0-1 (default 0.5).
Zero-based offset into the full result set.
How many assets of the list to skip (default 0): the previous reply's nextOffset.

operationId.description: Operation id from the add reply (or the status read's queue). Restricted to [A-Za-z0-9_-], 64 characters max.

operations.description: Steps run in order, 1-200. Each is {edit, ...the params of that edit}: edit is a node adder (add_material_node, add_scalar_parameter, add_vector_parameter, add_texture_sample, add_texture_coordinate, add_math_node, add_noise, add_custom_expression, ...; or add_material_node with nodeKind, as in the single call: {"edit": "add_material_node", "nodeKind": "world_position"}), use_material_function, connect_nodes, set_node_position, update_custom_expression, set_blend_mode, set_shading_model, set_material_domain or set_two_sided. Optional per step: id (names the created node; later steps use "$id" in sourceNodeId/targetNodeId/nodeId), from/to ("$id.Pin" shorthand for connect_nodes, where a source pin may be channel letters like "$uv.G"; "Main.EmissiveColor" is the material output). A created node without x/y is laid out automatically. Deleting and disconnecting are not batched. Every edit and "$id" is checked before any step runs, so a misspelled one refuses the batch with nothing applied (problems lists each); a step that fails when it runs stops the batch with the steps before it applied (their node ids are in nodeIds). When every step ran, the material is compiled and saved once.

order.description: Every value once, in the new order, by internal or shown name; a partial list is refused.

orphansOnly.description: Report only the nodes whose result reaches no output of the material or function: nothing wired to them, or a branch that ends in a node nothing reads (left behind when the node it fed was rewired). Accepted in place of nodeId.

outputPath.description: Full output asset path, e.g. /Game/Textures/T_Noise; replaces name and path.

outputType.description: Output type: Float1 (default), Float2, Float3, Float4 or MaterialAttributes.

overwrite.description: Overwrite packages that already exist at the destination. Default false, which skips them and reports skippedCount.

padding.description: Space kept clear around the text, in pixels (default 4% of the shorter side); the text is scaled to fill the rest.

offset.description: Zero-based offset into the full result set.

pagination.description: Nested pagination envelope. Top-level limit/offset take precedence when both are supplied.

parameterKind.description:
Which set material parameter variant to run; omit for 'parameter'.
parameter: Set a material parameter value by parameterType: scalar (the default) takes a number value, vector {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a], texture a texturePath (or the path in value); a missing value is refused. parameters sets several on one asset, assets several material instances under one consent, each entry checked on its own (the reply lists the ones that failed). On a material instance an override of its parent (a name the parent does not publish is PARAMETER_NOT_FOUND, listing those it does), on a base material the parameter node's default (refused while the material is open in its editor). Saved unless save is false (saved).
scalar: Set a scalar parameter to value (a number): on a material instance an override of its parent (a name the parent does not publish is PARAMETER_NOT_FOUND, listing those it does), on a base material the parameter node's default (refused while the material is open in its editor). Saved unless save is false (saved).
vector: Set a vector (colour) parameter to value, {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a]: on a material instance an override of its parent (a name the parent does not publish is PARAMETER_NOT_FOUND, listing those it does), on a base material the parameter node's default (refused while the material is open in its editor). Saved unless save is false (saved).
texture: Set a texture parameter to the texture at texturePath: on a material instance an override of its parent (a name the parent does not publish is PARAMETER_NOT_FOUND, listing those it does), on a base material the parameter node's default (refused while the material is open in its editor). Saved unless save is false (saved).
static_switch: Turn a static switch parameter on or off (value true or false; an instance rebuilds its shader permutation): on a material instance an override of its parent (a name the parent does not publish is PARAMETER_NOT_FOUND, listing those it does), on a base material the parameter node's default (refused while the material is open in its editor). Saved unless save is false (saved).

parameterType.description: Parameter kind: scalar (default), vector, or texture. Selects which parameter expression the value is written to.

parameters.description: Several parameter values at once, each {parameterName, parameterType (scalar | vector | texture), value, or texturePath for a texture}; applied counts those that took, and an entry that did not is listed under parameters with why and fails the call.

parentMaterial.description: The parent, as a /Game path: a Material, or another Material Instance for a child instance.

oneOf.description: Canonical /Game path to list.
Alternative directory path.
Folder for the layer info asset, e.g. /Game/Landscape/Layers (overrides the material folder).
Folder path, e.g. /Game/Art/Props; a path outside the allowed roots is refused (INVALID_PATH).
Package path (default /Game/Enums).
Package path (default /Game/Structs).
Package path of the new asset: default /Game/DataTables for a table, /Game/Structs for a row struct.
Package path to search (default /Game/Structs), recursive.
Package path.
Single asset path (alternative to paths).
Asset paths to check out.
Asset paths to delete.

pattern.description: Search pattern (used when searchText is absent).

patternType.description: Checker (default), Grid, Brick, Stripes or Dots.

payload.description: A complete Bridge export envelope: { exportPayload: [ { assetId, assetType, exportMode, exportType, folderName, name, assetPaths[] } ] }. Use this to pass through exactly what Bridge would have sent.

physicalMaterialPath.description: Physical material the layer applies, e.g. /Game/Physics/PM_Grass.

physicsAssetPath.description: Skeletal mesh: an existing physics asset to use instead of making one.

pinName.description: Input to unplug: a pin of nodeId by name or label (a custom node input such as OB), or for nodeId Main a material output input (BaseColor, Normal...). A name that matches none fails listing the inputs; only a material function's output node takes none, unplugging every output.

position.description: Where the moved member goes: first or last of the struct, or before or after the member named in relativeTo.

primaryColor.description: Main colour (default white) as {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1.

process.description:
Which process asset variant to run.
thumbnail: Render the preview of an asset and store it as its thumbnail (the asset is left unsaved; engine content keeps its own), and write it as a PNG when outputPath is given.
lods: Give one or several static mesh assets lodCount LODs in all (default 4, 1 to 50, LOD 0 included): each LOD keeps half the triangles of the one before (50%, 25%, ...), LODs past the count and the hand-tuned settings of the others are replaced, and each mesh is rebuilt and saved. Engine meshes are not changed: they are listed under engineContentPaths (ENGINE_CONTENT when nothing else was given), so duplicate one into /Game first. The reply counts processed out of requested and lists notFoundPaths and notMeshPaths; in a headless editor the build is skipped and each mesh is only checked.
mesh_materials: Set the materials in the slots of a static or skeletal mesh asset, by slot index or slot name, so every placement of the mesh shows them.
mesh_collision: Set the collision of a static mesh asset: one box, sphere or capsule fitted to its bounds, its own render triangles (complex), or none; every placed copy is rebuilt to match and the mesh is saved.

provider.description: Provider name as the editor registers it, e.g. Git or Perforce. Omit to report the current provider without changing it.

quality.description: Quality tier of the file to fetch, for a listing that publishes one file per tier, as Megascans does: raw (the unprocessed scan, hundreds of MB), high, mid or low. Omit to take the best game-ready tier: high, else mid, low, raw. A tier the listing does not publish is refused with QUALITY_NOT_AVAILABLE, naming the tiers it does. Ignored for a listing that publishes no tiers and for a unreal-engine pack. The reply's quality, fileName and downloadBytes say which file was chosen.

query.description: Free-text search. At most 128 characters, and no quotes, backslashes or control characters.

rayDistance.description: Farthest occluder counted, in cm; 0 (default) means unlimited, negative is refused.

recursive.description: Also report every /Game package the assets depend on, transitively (up to 512).

redTexture.description: Red channel source: an 8-bit BGRA8 or G8 texture.

referencers.description: List the packages that USE this asset (Blueprints that spawn it, levels that place it) instead of the ones it uses; check this before deleting or replacing an asset.

relativeTo.description: Name or GUID of the member to place the moved member next to. Required for before and after; ignored for first and last.

renames.description: Explicit renames, each asset to its own new name in its own folder, all in this one call: [{sourcePath, newName}]. An entry whose asset is missing, or whose newName is taken, is skipped and named under skipped. Replaces the pattern fields.

renderTargetPath.description: Full asset path, e.g. /Game/RenderTargets/RT_Capture; replaces name and packagePath.

replacement.description: Replacement text (used when replaceText is absent).

rowStructPath.description: Asset path of a row struct: the one the table is bound to (create, set_row_struct), or the new struct (create_row_struct, in place of name and path).

rows.description: Rows to import, each { rowName: <name>, rowData: { <field>: <value>, ... } }. The field names inside rowData are the row struct own property names, e.g. { rowName: ArcRifle, rowData: { DisplayName: Arc Rifle, Damage: 42 } }. A flat entry such as { rowName, Damage } is rejected as missing rowData.

samples.description: Occlusion rays per texel, 1-1024 (default 64); more is smoother and slower.

save.description: Persist the asset to disk. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

scalars.description: Scalar parameters, each {name, default}: a name the collection lacks is added, one it has takes the new default (0 when a new one gives none).

secondaryColor.description: Second colour (default black) as {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1.

seller.description: Only listings published by this seller, by name, for example Quixel Megascans. At most 128 characters, and no quotes, backslashes or control characters. Omit for every publisher.

setting.description:
Which configure texture variant to run.
compression: Set a 2D texture's compression setting by its engine name, with or without the TC_ prefix (Normalmap or TC_Normalmap). The reply names the setting applied (compressionSettings) and whether the texture reached disk (saved). An unknown name is refused with the valid names and nothing changes.
lod_bias: Set a 2D texture's LOD bias: the number of top mips dropped at runtime (1 halves each side, 0 restores full size). The reply carries lodBias and saved.
streaming_priority: Set never-stream on a 2D texture (neverStream, required): true keeps every mip resident instead of streaming them in, false lets it stream again. UTexture has no per-texture streaming priority to set. The reply carries neverStream and saved.
texture_group: Set a 2D texture's texture group (its LOD group) by engine name, with or without the TEXTUREGROUP_ prefix (UI or TEXTUREGROUP_UI), so it follows that group's LOD and streaming rules. The reply names the group applied (textureGroup) and saved; an unknown name is refused with the valid names and nothing changes.
virtual_texture: Switch virtual texture streaming on or off for a 2D texture (virtualTextureStreaming, required). Materials that sample the texture must then use the matching sampler type (Virtual Color, Virtual Normal and so on, or the plain type when it is switched off), or they stop compiling. The reply carries virtualTextureStreaming and saved.

shadingModel.description: Shading model, such as DefaultLit, Unlit, Subsurface, ClearCoat or TwoSidedFoliage. The Details panel label and the MSM_ name work too.

sizeCm.description: About how big, in cm (the largest of its three dimensions; meshes only).

skeletonPath.description: Existing skeleton, e.g. /Game/Chars/SK_Hero_Skeleton. Alone it imports the FBX's animation take ALONE against it (implies importAnimations); with importMesh it binds the imported skeletal mesh to it instead, so the mesh shares that skeleton's animations.

sourceControlOp.description:
Which source control variant to run.
checkout: Check out assets (paths, or assetPath) in the enabled revision-control provider so they can be edited and submitted. Paths that name no asset in the project are skipped and listed (skipped); none left is NO_VALID_ASSETS, and source control off is SOURCE_CONTROL_DISABLED (turn it on with sourceControlOp=enable). The reply gives checkedOut and assets.
submit: Submit (check in) saved assets (paths, or assetPath) to the enabled provider with description as the change description. Paths that name no asset are skipped and listed (skipped); none left is NO_VALID_ASSETS, a provider refusal SUBMIT_FAILED, and source control off SOURCE_CONTROL_DISABLED. The reply gives submitted.
enable: Turn revision control on with the provider named (Git, Perforce or Subversion, as the editor registers it), switching from another provider that is on; with that provider already on, or none named while one is on, it reports the current provider. A provider whose plugin is off or that cannot connect (Git needs a repository at the project root: sourceControlOp=init) is SOURCE_CONTROL_ENABLE_FAILED.
init: Put the project under Git: create a repository at the project root when there is none, write an Unreal .gitignore when there is none (Binaries, Intermediate, Saved, DerivedDataCache), stage everything, make the first commit (description, default "Initial commit") and turn the Git provider on. userName and userEmail go to the repository config only and cannot hold quotes or control characters. The reply gives committed, commit (short hash), provider and steps (each git command with its exit code and output); a failing step answers GIT_INIT_FAILED, GIT_ADD_FAILED or GIT_COMMIT_FAILED.
commit_all: Stage every change in the project (git add -A, honouring .gitignore) and commit it with description as the message; a clean tree answers success with alreadyClean true and committed false. Needs a repository (NO_REPOSITORY: sourceControlOp=init). userName and userEmail, when sent, go to the repository config and cannot hold quotes or control characters. The reply gives committed, commit and steps.

sourceId.description: Relative id under sourceRoot, exactly as returned by list_content_sources (for example "TP_VehicleAdvBP"). Must be relative: no "..", no leading "/", no drive prefix. Omit to migrate the root itself.

sourcePath.description: File to import, inside the project folder: relative to it (Saved/Imports/Crate.fbx) or absolute under it; any other path is refused.

sourcePin.description: Source output: its name, its index, or channel letters of the default output ("G", "RG"; X/Y/Z/W work too). Omit for the default output.

sourceRoot.description: Content source root token. One of: engineTemplates | engineFeaturePacks | engineContent | enginePlugins | megascansLibrary | fabLibrary | projectContent | projectPlugins. A filesystem path is never accepted here — the token is resolved plugin-side, so no directory outside these roots is reachable. megascansLibrary probes both the shell Documents folder and the profile Documents folder (OneDrive redirects the first) and honours MCP_MEGASCANS_LIBRARY_DIR; fabLibrary reads the Fab plugin's own UFabSettings.CacheDirectoryPath and honours MCP_FAB_LIBRARY_DIR. The Fab plugin owns its own sign-in and downloading — these roots only read what it already placed on disk.

sourceTexture.description: Source heightmap texture path; its source must be an 8-bit BGRA8 or single-channel G8 texture, read as its luminance (a G8 source is its gray). Other source formats (G16, RGBA16, float, HDR) fail with an error naming the format found.

startColor.description: Start colour (default black) as {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a] in 0-1.

startNodeId.description: Starting node ID accepted by the handler in place of nodeId.

structPath.description: Asset path of the Blueprint Struct (e.g. /Game/Structs/S_MyStruct).

subPath.description: Optional folder under the source content directory, to migrate one subtree instead of the whole pack.

tag.description: Asset-registry tag name, for example ParentClass, which every Blueprint carries.

tags.description: Tag names to set; each is written as package metadata with the value "true".

targetPin.description: Target pin name. On the material output (targetNodeId Main): BaseColor, Metallic, Specular, Roughness, Anisotropy, EmissiveColor, Opacity, OpacityMask, Normal, Tangent, WorldPositionOffset, SubsurfaceColor, ClearCoat, ClearCoatRoughness, AmbientOcclusion, Refraction, PixelDepthOffset (and SurfaceThickness, Displacement on newer engines); a Cloth material's Cloth and FuzzColor, and CustomData0/CustomData1, name the clear-coat and subsurface pins they share.

text.description: The words to draw; a newline starts a new line.

textureGroup.description: Engine texture group, with or without TEXTUREGROUP_: World, WorldNormalMap, WorldSpecular, Character, CharacterNormalMap, Weapon, Vehicle, Cinematic, Effects, Skybox, UI, Lightmap, Shadowmap, ColorLookupTable, Bokeh, Pixels2D and the rest.

trianglePercent.description: Percent of the source triangles Nanite keeps, 0-100 (default 100).

typeface.description: Face of the font: Regular, Bold, Italic, Light... (default Bold when the font has it). A face the font lacks is refused with the list it has.

uncaptionedOnly.description: Only assets with no caption yet (default true); false shows every asset.

upstream.description: Walk every upstream producer, overriding direction and depth.

userEmail.description: Commit author email, written to the repository config only.

userName.description: Commit author name, written to the repository config only.

uvChannel.description: UV channel to bake into (default 0, the one materials sample); a lightmap channel avoids overlapping UVs.

oneOf.description: Metadata value (text).
Parameter value.
Two-sided value: true renders both faces, false only the front.
Optional tag value to match, ignoring case.

valueName.description: Enum value (entry), by its internal name or the name the editor shows (get_enum lists both as name and displayName).

values.description: create: the initial value names in order, as strings or { name } objects (a name given twice is refused and nothing is made). split: the values to copy into the new enum, by internal or shown name.

varGuid.description: Stable member GUID, as get_struct lists it; pass this or memberName.

vectors.description: Vector parameters, each {name, default}: default as [r, g, b, a] or {r, g, b, a} (alpha 1 when omitted); a name the collection lacks is added, one it has takes the new default.

virtualTextureStreaming.description: true streams the texture as a virtual texture (the project must have virtual texturing enabled), false stops; leaving it out is refused.

x.description: New X coordinate (posX is the fallback spelling).

y.description: New Y coordinate (posY is the fallback spelling).

tools.name: manage_audio
tools.description: Play/stop sounds, add audio components, configure mixes, attenuation, spatial audio, and author Sound Cues/MetaSounds.

actorName.description: Target actor label or name in the current level.

all.description: Also act on every sound the editor and a running Play In Editor game play, game music included (default false: only the 2D sounds play_sound started). Stop silences every audio device; pause and resume take soundPath to narrow it to one sound.

applyEQ.description: Whether the mix applies its EQ (default true).

applyToChildren.description: Whether the modifier also applies to the child sound classes (default true).

attachPointName.description: Socket or bone name to attach the sound to.

attenuateWithLPF.description: Air absorption on or off: a low-pass whose cutoff drops with distance. Sending any lpf value turns it on unless this is false.

autoPlay.description: Whether the sound plays now and again every time the game starts (default true); false leaves starting it to a Blueprint.

childIndex.description: Input pin of the source node that receives the target (default 0); missing pins are added up to the node maximum.

componentName.description: Name of the component to create or address.

control.description:
Which control sound mix variant to run.
push: Push a Sound Mix (mixName: an asset path or a bare asset name) onto the mix stack of the sound being heard: the running game while one plays, else the editor (inGame says which). While pushed, its sound class adjustments (volume, pitch, EQ) apply, such as ducking music under dialogue; control=pop removes it. A name that loads no Sound Mix is ASSET_NOT_FOUND. Runtime state only: nothing is saved.
pop: Pop a Sound Mix that control=push pushed, on the sound being heard: the running game while one plays, else the editor (inGame says which); its adjustments fade out over the fade-out time of the mix. A mix pushed twice needs two pops, and popping one that is not pushed changes nothing.
set_base: Make a Sound Mix the base mix of the sound being heard: the running game while one plays, else the editor (inGame says which): the one mix that always applies beneath any pushed ones, replacing the previous base. Runtime state only.
set_class_override: Override how a Sound Mix adjusts one Sound Class (soundClassName) and its child classes: volume and pitch multipliers (default 1), reached over fadeTime seconds (default 1); the class joins the mix when the mix lacks it. It acts on the sound being heard: the running game while one plays, else the editor (inGame says which), only while that mix is pushed or the base mix, and leaves the asset unchanged. A name that loads no mix or class is ASSET_NOT_FOUND.
clear_class_override: Remove the override control=set_class_override put on a Sound Mix for soundClassName, fading back over fadeOutTime seconds (default 1), on the sound being heard: the running game while one plays, else the editor (inGame says which).

decayHFRatio.description: Reverb high-frequency to mid-frequency decay time ratio (0.1 to 2).

decayTime.description: Reverb decay time in seconds (0.1 to 20).

defaultValue.description: Value in the data type of the input: a number (Float, Int32, Time, enums), a boolean, a string, or a JSON array of them for an array input such as Float:Array. Converted to the declared type; a mismatch is refused.

delay.description: Delay in seconds, for a delay node.

distanceAlgorithm.description: Distance falloff curve: Linear, Logarithmic, Inverse or NaturalSound. Left unchanged when omitted.

dopplerIntensity.description: Doppler pitch-shift strength (default 1, the normal shift; 0 turns the shift off; negative is refused).

edit.description:
Which edit metasound variant to run.
create: Create a MetaSound asset, named by name and path or by its full assetPath, and return its asset path. A MetaSound already at that path is refused (ASSET_EXISTS), never replaced. A one-shot source (the default: On Play in, On Finished out) is never virtualized by the engine, so one left playing on an AudioComponent that starts out of earshot is dropped for good; make a drone, hum or ambience with oneShot false.
add_input: Add an input to a MetaSound graph.
add_output: Add an output to a MetaSound graph.
add_node: Add a node to a MetaSound graph.
connect_nodes: Connect two MetaSound graph pins.
disconnect: Remove a link from a MetaSound graph: the one into targetNodeId.targetInputName, or every link out of sourceNodeId.sourceOutputName; with both ends given, that exact link. Refused when there is no such link.
remove_node: Remove one node, or several with nodeIds, and every link on them from a MetaSound graph; graph inputs and outputs (On Play, Out Mono) are refused. All or nothing.
set_default: Set the default of a MetaSound graph input, or with nodeId the literal on a node input (an oscillator frequency, an envelope time, a note array).
batch: Run many MetaSound graph edits in one call: add nodes, inputs and outputs, connect pins and set literals, with $id references between steps.

effectPresetPath.description: Canonical /Game source effect preset asset to add; an alternative to effectType.

effectType.description: Source effect preset class or short name.

enableReverbSend.description: Whether the sound sends to reverb.

eqPriority.description: EQ priority of the mix; the active mix with the highest priority supplies the EQ.

eqSettings.description: Four-band EQ as {frequencyCenter0..3, gain0..3, bandwidth0..3}; a missing key keeps its value.

extent.description: A Box shape's half-size on each axis in cm, {x, y, z}, each above 0: a zone the length of a hall without reaching as far sideways. It replaces the size innerRadius gives a box; another shape is refused.

fade.description:
Which fade sound variant to run; omit for 'to_volume'.
to_volume: Fade a named sound instance to a target volume.
in: Fade a sound instance in.
out: Fade a sound instance out.

falloffDistance.description: Distance over which attenuation falls off, in centimetres.

falloffMode.description: Attenuation falloff curve: Linear (the default), Logarithmic, Inverse or NaturalSound.

filter.description: Part of a class name, display name or category, spaces and case ignored ("Trigger", "Envelope", "Filters"); omitted, every class up to limit.

gender.description: Grammatical gender of the voice: Masculine, Feminine or Neuter (default Masculine).

highFrequency.description: Centre frequency of EQ band 3 in Hz.

highGain.description: Linear gain of EQ band 3 (0 to 4).

highMidFrequency.description: Centre frequency of EQ band 2 in Hz.

highMidGain.description: Linear gain of EQ band 2 (0 to 4).

includePins.description: Also list each class's input and output pins as "Name (Type)", the names connect and set_default take.

indefinite.description: Whether a looping node loops forever (default true); false plays loopCount extra times.

innerRadius.description: Inner radius of full volume, in centimetres: a Box shape takes it as its half-size on every axis, a Capsule as its radius (half height at least that), a Sphere or Cone as its radius.

inputType.description: Graph input data type (Float, Int32, Bool, String, Trigger, Audio).

kind.description:
Which create audio actor variant to run.
ambient_sound: Create an ambient sound actor.
audio_component: Create an audio component on an actor, or on a new actor at location when actorName is omitted.
reverb_zone: Create a runtime reverb zone actor.

lfeBleed.description: Share of the sound sent to the LFE channel (0 to 1).

limit.description: At most this many classes (default 50), those whose own name equals, starts with or contains filter first, the engine's UE nodes first among those, then by name; matchCount and truncated say what was left out.

localizationKeyFormat.description: Localization key format of the context (default {ContextHash}).

location.description: World location as [x, y, z] (an {x, y, z} object is accepted).

loopCount.description: Extra plays of a looping node when indefinite is false.

lowFrequency.description: Centre frequency of EQ band 0 in Hz.

lowGain.description: Linear gain of EQ band 0 (0 to 4).

lowPassFilterFrequency.description: Low-pass filter cutoff frequency in Hz.

lpfFrequencyAtMax.description: Low-pass cutoff in Hz at lpfRadiusMax and beyond (900 sounds like a distant, muffled engine).

lpfFrequencyAtMin.description: Low-pass cutoff in Hz at lpfRadiusMin and nearer (20000 leaves the sound unfiltered).

lpfRadiusMax.description: Distance in cm where the cutoff reaches lpfFrequencyAtMax.

lpfRadiusMin.description: Distance in cm where the low-pass starts closing; nearer than this the cutoff is lpfFrequencyAtMin.

maxSeconds.description: Longest the measurement runs, in seconds (default 5, 0.2 to 20). A sound that ends sooner ends it then; looping sounds, music and MetaSounds that never trigger On Finished play until this.

midFrequency.description: Centre frequency of EQ band 1 in Hz.

midGain.description: Linear gain of EQ band 1 (0 to 4).

name.description: Name of the asset, actor or mapping to create, or of the mapping to remove.

nodeClassName.description: Node class name; short names such as Sine resolve against the MetaSound registry (UE.Sine.Audio).

nodeId.description: Graph node id (the id add_node returned, or one from get_metasound_graph).

nodeIds.description: Several node ids to remove in one call, in place of nodeId; every one must exist or nothing is removed.

nodeType.description: Node type or class short name.

occlusionFilterScale.description: Low-pass filter scale applied while occluded (0-1).

oneShot.description: false makes a continuous source with no On Finished output: the engine treats it as looping, so a hum or ambience whose AudioComponent starts out of earshot resumes when the listener comes near. Default true (it plays until On Finished fires).

operations.description: Steps run in order, 1-200, stopping at the first failure; every add_node class is looked up first, so a node class the registry does not hold fails the batch with nothing applied, and so is every pin a connect or set_default names on a node the batch adds (a wrong one fails with PIN_NOT_FOUND and that node's pins). Each is {edit, ...the params of that edit}: edit is add_node, connect, disconnect, remove_node, set_default, add_input or add_output (the add_metasound_node, connect_metasound_nodes, disconnect_metasound_nodes, remove_metasound_node, set_metasound_default, add_metasound_input, add_metasound_output params). Optional per step: id (names the node it creates; later steps use "$id" in nodeId/nodeIds/sourceNodeId/targetNodeId), from/to ("$id.PinName" shorthand for connect; interface nodes such as the On Play input are named with the explicit fields).

parentClass.description: Canonical /Game SoundClass asset path of the new parent; an empty string clears the parent.

path.description: Canonical /Game folder for the created asset.

pitchAdjuster.description: Pitch multiplier applied by the mix modifier.

playback.description:
Which play sound variant to run.
2d: Play a sound asset 2D, tied to no place, at volume and pitch (default 1) from startTime seconds, on the running game while one plays, else in the editor; it plays to its end, a looping one until stop_sound. A path that loads no sound is ASSET_NOT_FOUND, and an editor with sound off answers NOT_PLAYED.
at_location: Play a sound once at location (and rotation), at volume and pitch (default 1) from startTime seconds, with an optional attenuationPath and concurrencyPath (ASSET_NOT_FOUND when one does not load). It plays in the running game while one plays, heard from its listener, else in the editor. Fire and forget: only stop_sound with all true stops it.
spawn_at_location: Spawn a transient sound at a world location.
attached: Play a sound attached to an actor (actorName; in the running game while one plays, else in the level) on the component or socket attachPointName names, else on its root, at volume and pitch. The reply gives componentName, attachedTo and playing; an unknown actor is ACTOR_NOT_FOUND and an unknown attach point ATTACH_POINT_NOT_FOUND.
prime: Prime a sound asset for playback.
measure: Play a sound 2D and measure how loud it played, from the mixer's own meter: peak and average level in dB and a timeline, with silent: true when it played but produced no audio (an empty Sound Cue, a MetaSound whose audio output is unconnected). A Sound Wave also gets the peak, RMS and length of the recording itself (wavePeakDb, waveRmsDb, waveSeconds), which hold however slowly the editor draws. Answers when the sound ends or after maxSeconds.

plurality.description: Grammatical number of the voice: Singular or Plural (default Singular).

replace.description: Swap the context this speaker already has with these same listeners (its sound and key format) instead of refusing with CONTEXT_EXISTS (default false).

reverbDistanceMax.description: Distance at which the reverb wet level reaches its maximum.

reverbDistanceMin.description: Distance at which the reverb send starts.

rotation.description: World rotation in degrees as [pitch, yaw, roll] (a {pitch, yaw, roll} object is accepted).

save.description: Persist the asset to disk (default true); false leaves the change in memory only.

setting.description:
Which configure sound attenuation variant to run.
distance: Configure distance attenuation: inner radius (or a box's size per axis), falloff distance and curve, and air absorption (a low-pass that muffles the sound with distance).
spatialization: Set how a Sound Attenuation asset places its sounds in space: spatialize on or off, and spatialization Default (panning) or Binaural (HRTF, for headphones). Only what is sent changes, a call with neither is refused, and another algorithm is INVALID_ARGUMENT. Saved unless save is false.
occlusion: Set occlusion on a Sound Attenuation asset (assetPath), each value only when sent: enable turns it on or off, occlusionFilterScale (0-1) times 20000 Hz is the low-pass cutoff when blocked, occlusionVolumeScale (0-1) the volume kept, occlusionInterpolationTime the seconds to blend. The reply reads the four values back; the asset is saved unless save is false.
reverb_send: Configure an audio reverb send.
audio_occlusion: Configure occlusion settings on a sound asset.
preset: Create a Sound Attenuation asset name in path (default /Game/Audio/Attenuation): innerRadius (default 400), falloffDistance (default 3600), attenuationShape Sphere (the default), Capsule, Box (sized per axis with extent) or Cone, and falloffMode Linear (the default), Logarithmic, Inverse or NaturalSound; another shape or mode is refused. An asset already at the path is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS (change one with setting=distance). Saved unless save is false; the reply reads the values back.

size.description: Reverb zone box size in centimetres as [x, y, z] (default 500 each; an {x, y, z} object is accepted).

smoothing.description: Smooth the Doppler pitch change instead of applying it each frame (default false).

soundName.description: Actor label/name or AudioComponent name of the playing sound.

soundOp.description:
Which stop sound variant to run; omit for 'stop'.
stop: Stop sounds: the 2D sounds play_sound started (only that sound with soundPath), or with all every sound the editor and a running game play, its music included.
pause: Pause the sounds soundOp=stop would stop, each held where it is. Sounds already paused are not counted.
resume: Resume the paused sounds soundOp=stop would stop, each from where it was paused.

soundPath.description: Canonical /Game sound asset path (SoundWave, SoundCue or MetaSound).

soundPaths.description: The Sound Waves, by asset path (1-64). A Sound Cue or MetaSound is refused with ASSET_NOT_FOUND naming it: measure the waves it plays.

soundWavePath.description: Canonical /Game SoundWave asset spoken in this context.

sourceOutputName.description: Output pin name on the source node.

spatialization.description: Spatialization algorithm: Default (the panner) or Binaural (HRTF). Left unchanged when omitted.

spatialize.description: Whether the sound is spatialized (default true).

speakerPath.description: Canonical /Game DialogueVoice asset path of the speaker.

targetInputName.description: Input pin name on the target node.

targetLufs.description: The loudness each wave should play at, in LUFS (-23 is broadcast; games and streaming commonly sit around -14 to -18).

targetVoices.description: Canonical /Game DialogueVoice asset paths the line is spoken to.

voiceCenterChannelVolume.description: Share of the sound sent to the centre speaker (0 to 1).

volumeAdjuster.description: Volume multiplier applied by the mix modifier.

tools.name: manage_blueprint
tools.description: Create Blueprints and UMG widgets, add SCS/UI components, set defaults, and manipulate Blueprint graphs, bindings, and widget layouts.

actionPath.description: Enhanced Input action asset path accepted in place of inputActionPath.

activeIndex.description: Index shown first by a widget switcher.

actorName.description: For nodeType K2Node_ActorBoundEvent or K2Node_Literal, which belong in a level Blueprint: the placed actor of its level (label, name or object path) the event fires for, with eventName one of its event dispatchers (OnActorBeginOverlap), or the node references. Without it, or outside a level Blueprint, the node is refused.

alignment.description: CanvasPanel child: the pivot {x, y}, each 0-1. Any other slot (box, overlay, border, scroll box): x is the horizontal and y the vertical alignment, each a number (0 left/top, 0.5 center, 1 right/bottom) or a word: "fill", "left", "center", "right", "top", "bottom"; leave one out to keep it. {"x": "fill", "y": "center"} spans the width and centers vertically.

animationName.description: The animation to read in full; omitted, every animation is listed with its timing.

applyAndSave.description: Whether to save the Blueprint after applying SCS changes.

attachTo.description: Socket or parent component to attach to: one of this Blueprint's own, a parent Blueprint's part, or a native one (Mesh, CapsuleComponent).

autoPlay.description: Start when the game starts, without a Play call.

barName.description: The ProgressBar in the widget that shows the health (default HealthBar_Bar, the bar of the health bar piece). A bar named here must already be in the widget.

behaviour.description:
Which add behaviour variant to run.
health: Give an actor health: Health and MaxHealth variables, damage from any source (ApplyDamage, a pain causing volume, a projectile) lowers it and negative damage heals, a Heal function, OnHealthChanged and OnDied dispatchers, and optional destroy on death.
damage_on_touch: Make an actor damage whatever touches it: ApplyDamage with TouchDamage on each overlap, which an actor with health loses (a negative amount heals); with knockback a touching Character is also launched away from it. It fires on overlap, so the actor needs a component that overlaps pawns (a sphere or box with the Trigger or OverlapAllDynamic profile).
pickup: Make an actor a pickup: a pawn that touches it collects it, which heals the pawn (heal) or adds to a number variable of the collector class (coins, keys, ammo), plays a sound and destroys the pickup. It fires on overlap, so the actor needs a component that overlaps pawns (a sphere or box with the Trigger or OverlapAllDynamic profile).
sprint: Give a Character a sprint: while the key is held its MaxWalkSpeed is sprintSpeed, and on release the walk speed it had at BeginPlay comes back. The key gets an Input Action and a mapping, registered when the character is possessed.
shoot: Give a pawn a key that shoots: each press spawns projectileClass in front of it, facing its way and owned by it, and launches it at projectileSpeed, at most fireRate shots a minute. The key gets an Input Action and a mapping, registered when the pawn is possessed.
chase: Make a pawn chase the player: every quarter second, while the player is within chaseRange, its AI controller moves it toward the player and stops stopDistance away; out of range it stops. The pawn is set to be possessed by an AI controller when placed or spawned.
patrol: Make a pawn patrol: its AI controller walks it to each of points in turn (offsets from where it starts), it waits waitTime at each and the route loops; with chaseRange it chases the player who comes that close and goes back to its route after. A chase the pawn already has is taken over. The pawn is set to be possessed by an AI controller when placed or spawned.
turret: Make an actor a turret: every frame, while the player is within range, it turns about its vertical axis to face the player and fires projectileClass at them at projectileSpeed, at most fireRate shots a minute; each projectile is owned by the actor, so it never hits it. Nothing checks line of sight: a wall between them stops the shots.
stomp: Make an enemy the player defeats by landing on it: a player-controlled Character that lands on top of the actor bounces up at bounceSpeed and the actor dies (with the health behaviour it takes damage enough to die, else it is destroyed); one that bumps it from the side or below takes sideDamage, at most once a second.
explosive: Make an actor with health explode when it dies: every actor within explosionRadius with a clear line to it takes up to explosionDamage (less with distance), effectPath plays and soundPath sounds at the spot, and the actor is gone. An explosive the blast kills explodes in turn.
moving_platform: Make an actor a moving platform or an elevator: it travels to each of points in turn (offsets from where it starts) at speed, waits waitTime at each, and loops; a Character standing on it rides along. Its root must be movable (a Blueprint made with manage_blueprint create is).
controls: Give a Character the controls a player steers it with: WASD or the left stick walk it relative to where the controller faces, the mouse or the right stick turn the view, and the jump key jumps (held longer, higher). It makes IA_Move and IA_Look (Axis2D) and IA_Jump next to the Blueprint, maps the keys and registers the context when the character is possessed.
respawn: Make a pawn come back when it falls off the level or dies: to its start, or to where it last touched an actor tagged checkpointTag (a checkpoint), once it falls fallHeight below that point, and when it dies (back at full health) if it has the health behaviour. Respawn, SetRespawnPoint and OnRespawned are left for other logic.
goal: Make an actor the goal of a level: the first time the player touches it, OnGoalReached fires and soundPath plays there, and with nextLevel that level opens delay seconds later. It fires on overlap, so the actor needs a component that overlaps pawns (a sphere or box with the Trigger or OverlapAllDynamic profile).
launch_pad: Make an actor launch a Character that touches it: LaunchCharacter with launchVelocity, replacing its vertical speed so every bounce reaches the same height (overrideXY replaces its horizontal speed too), and soundPath plays at the pad. It fires on overlap, so the actor needs a component that overlaps pawns (a sphere or box with the Trigger or OverlapAllDynamic profile).
teleporter: Make an actor a teleporter: a pawn that touches it is moved to TeleportTarget, keeping its rotation, and soundPath plays where it arrives. Set TeleportTarget on each placed teleporter to the actor to arrive at (control_actor spawn variables, or set_blueprint_variables, with that actor name); a target that is a teleporter of the same class ignores pawns for cooldown seconds first, so a pair of pads does not send the pawn straight back. It fires on overlap, so the actor needs a component that overlaps pawns (a sphere or box with the Trigger or OverlapAllDynamic profile).
falling_platform: Make an actor a falling platform: the first pawn that lands on top of it starts it shaking, fallDelay seconds later it drops with gravity, and respawnTime seconds after the drop began it is back in place and ready again. A bump from the side or below does not set it off. The actor must block pawns, and its root must be movable (a Blueprint made with manage_blueprint create is).
countdown: Give an actor a time limit: at BeginPlay TimeLeft starts at seconds and drops by one every second; at zero OnTimeUp fires and, with killAtZero, the actor takes damage enough to die, so a pawn with the health behaviour dies and its game over or respawn follows. Show the time with behaviour counter_hud variableName TimeLeft.
spawner: Make an actor a spawner: every interval seconds, while fewer than maxAlive of the actors it spawned are alive, it spawns spawnClass at a random point up to radius across from itself, counts each until it is destroyed, and fires OnSpawned with it. A pawn class set to be possessed by AI when spawned (the chase behaviour sets that) moves on its own.
dash: Give a Character a dash: each press of the key launches it dashSpeed along where it faces, with a small lift so the dash carries before the ground slows it, at most once every cooldown seconds. The key gets an Input Action and a mapping, and the context is registered when the character is possessed.
health_hud: Show the health of a pawn on screen: while a local player controls it, a widget is on the screen with a bar filled to Health / MaxHealth, refilled whenever OnHealthChanged fires, and taken off when the pawn loses that player or is destroyed. Needs the health behaviour. With no widgetPath it makes UI/WBP_HealthBar next to the Blueprint.
counter_hud: Show a number of a pawn on screen (Coins, Score): while a local player controls it, a text at the top right reads label: value, the variable rounded to a whole number and refreshed every 0.1 seconds, taken off when the pawn loses that player or is destroyed. With no widgetPath it makes UI/WBP_<variable>Counter next to the Blueprint; each further counter sits a row lower.
hint: Show a message on the player's screen while the player is in the actor's area: when a locally controlled pawn starts to overlap the actor, a widget shows message at the bottom of that player's view, and it goes when the pawn leaves, or hideAfter seconds later. Each placed copy can say its own text (HintMessage is instance editable). It fires on overlap, so the actor needs a component that overlaps pawns (a sphere or box with the Trigger or OverlapAllDynamic profile).
game_over: Give the player a game over: when the pawn dies (health behaviour) while a local player controls it, that player input stops, a widget shows message over a dark shade, and the current level opens again restartDelay seconds later. The pawn stays when it dies, so the restart can run. With no widgetPath it makes UI/WBP_GameOver next to the Blueprint.

bindingKind.description:
Which bind widget variant to run.
text: Bind the Text of a widget to a Blueprint variable (any type that converts to text) or pure function.
color: Bind the tint of a widget (text or image color, progress fill, border brush) to a Blueprint variable or pure function.
enabled: Bind whether a widget is enabled to a Blueprint bool variable or pure function.
percent: Bind the fill Percent of a Progress Bar (or the Value of a Slider or SpinBox) to a Blueprint float variable or pure function, so a health or loading bar follows it at runtime.
visibility: Bind the Visibility of a widget to a Blueprint variable (a bool maps true to Visible, false to Collapsed) or pure function.
on_clicked: Wire the OnClicked event of a Button to a Blueprint function (bindingSource), creating the function when missing.
on_hovered: Wire the OnHovered (and optionally OnUnhovered) event of a Button to Blueprint functions, creating them when missing.
on_value_changed: Wire the value-changed event of a Slider, SpinBox, CheckBox or ComboBoxString to a Blueprint function (bindingSource) that receives the new value; the function is created when missing.
localized_text: Point a Text Block at a string-table entry so its text follows the active localization.
localization_key: Assign the localization namespace and key a Text Block resolves its text through.

bindingSource.description: For bind_text, bind_color, bind_enabled, bind_percent and bind_visibility: the variable (a getter converting it is generated) or pure no-input function the property reads. For bind_on_clicked and bind_on_value_changed: the function the event calls, created with the event inputs when it does not exist.

blueprintPath.description: Canonical /Game Blueprint asset path, or the path of a level open in the editor (/Game/Maps/L_Main) to compile its level Blueprint; saveAfterCompile then saves that level.

blueprintType.description: Picks the parent class when parentClass is absent: Actor, Pawn, Character or FunctionLibrary; Interface makes a Blueprint Interface (its functions with add_function, taken on with implement_interface).

bounceSpeed.description: Upward speed the stomping Character bounces off at, units per second (default 600).

buttons.description: Button labels, top to bottom: a menu's buttons, or a dialog's responses (at most 6, in place of responseCount); each becomes <Label>Button.

chaseRange.description: Distance within which the pawn chases the player, in units: chase defaults to 2000, and a patrol chases only when given one (default 0, or the range of a chase it takes over).

checkpointTag.description: Actor tag that marks a checkpoint (default Checkpoint).

code.description: One or more (event Name [(Params)] stmts...) and (fn Name (Params) stmts...) forms, as read_graph_as_code prints them; ; comments are ignored except the node ids gotos name.

collectorClass.description: Instead of heal: the class that collects it (a Blueprint path such as /Game/Blueprints/BP_Player), whose variableName goes up by amount.

columnCount.description: Columns given an equal share of the width (0-64).

compile.description: Compile the Blueprint after the operations (default false; applyAndSave also compiles).

componentClass.description: Component class path for SCS node creation.

componentName.description: Component whose delegate fires the event, added by the Blueprint or inherited (a Character's CapsuleComponent), or in a Widget Blueprint a widget of its tree that is a variable (every widget the widget handlers add is), e.g. PlayButton with eventName OnClicked. Makes a component-bound event (K2Node_ComponentBoundEvent) named by eventName.

componentNames.description: Several components to remove in one call, in place of componentName; each is reported, and the call fails naming any that were not removed.

contentColorAndOpacity.description: Tint (0-1 values) a border applies to its content.

cooldown.description: Seconds before it works again: before a Character can dash again, or before a teleporter takes a pawn after one arrived on it (default 1).

copyStyleFrom.description: Name of another TextBlock in the same Widget Blueprint whose font, colour and shadow this one takes; the other fields in the call then apply on top.

cornerRadius.description: Corner radius in pixels for a widget that draws a brush (Image, Button, Border). Switches the brush to a RoundedBox; 0 restores square corners.

createIfMissing.description: Create the Blueprint when savePath/name does not exist (default true); false only reports whether it exists.

createMode.description:
Which create variant to run; omit for 'create'.
create: Create a Blueprint asset named name in savePath (default /Game) and save it (saved). parentClass is a native class as /Script/Module.Class or a short name (Actor, Pawn, Character, PlayerController), or a Blueprint class path ending in _C; blueprintType Actor, Pawn, Character or FunctionLibrary stands in for a missing parentClass, and Interface without one makes a Blueprint Interface. A parent that resolves to nothing is CLASS_NOT_FOUND, naming classes of that name. properties sets class defaults, Component.Property and struct members by dotted path, reported as appliedProperties and failedProperties (the create stands either way). A Blueprint already at the path is answered with alreadyExists and left unchanged; one with another parent class is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS.
blueprint: Same as create: a Blueprint named name in savePath from parentClass, or from blueprintType when parentClass is left out.
ensure: Make sure a Blueprint of parentClass is at savePath/name: one already there is answered with alreadyExists and left unchanged (another parent class is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS); otherwise it is created as create does, unless createIfMissing is false, which only reports whether it exists.

currency.description: Currency name in the shop header, shown as "<currency>: 0" (default Gold).

damage.description: Damage on each touch (default 10; negative heals).

dashSpeed.description: Launch speed along the facing, units per second (default 1500).

defaultValue.description: Default value for the variable, in the form get_property reads back: a number, string or bool, {"x": 0, "y": 0, "z": 100} for a Vector, an array for an Array or Set, and a JSON object of key: value for a Map ({"Apple": 3}). A value its type cannot take is refused with DEFAULT_NOT_APPLIED and the variable is not added.

delay.description: Seconds between reaching the goal and opening nextLevel (default 2).

deleteScope.description:
Which delete node variant to run; omit for 'node'.
node: Delete a node from a Blueprint graph by its nodeGuid, or many nodes at once with nodeIds (one consent, one compile, all or nothing).
pin_links: Break (disconnect) every link of one pin on a graph node, leaving the pin unwired.

destroyOnDeath.description: Destroy the actor when its health reaches 0 (default false; OnDied fires either way).

dryRun.description: Check the batch without running any step (default false): the members, functions, variables and expressions the steps name, every "$id" against the ids of the steps before it, and every node named by guid. Every problem comes back at once in problems, and the reply fails with the first one's code; the pins of the nodes the batch would create are checked only when it runs. Nothing is changed, compiled or saved.

edit.description:
Which edit graph variant to run.
add_node: Add a node to a Blueprint graph (alias of edit=create_node with simplified type resolution).
create_node: Create a graph node (function call, event, variable, branch, etc.) in a Blueprint graph.
create_reroute_node: Create a reroute node for organizing exec/data wire paths in a Blueprint graph.
create_struct_make_break_nodes: Create a Make or Break Struct node in a Blueprint graph from a UserDefinedStruct or native UScriptStruct.
connect_pins: Connect two graph pins (exec or data) by nodeGuid and pin name. A pin the editor adds on demand is added: a Sequence's then_2, a Make Array's [2], a Switch on Int's case 7 (a new switch has only Default).
set_node_property: Set a property on a graph node by nodeGuid.
set_pin_default_value: Set the default value of a data pin on a graph node; a read-only (const reference) pin gets it through a MakeLiteral node wired into it.
add_construction_script: Add or open the Construction Script graph for a Blueprint.
arrange_nodes: Tidy a graph: move the listed nodes beside the nodes they are wired to (right of what runs them, below-left of what reads them), each to the nearest free slot; the nodes left out stay put and anchor them. layout layered instead lays the listed nodes out in columns along their links (a layered, Sugiyama-style layout), the first listed staying where it is. An unknown nodeId is refused before anything moves. The Blueprint then compiles and is saved; that compile clears the editor's undo history whenever the history holds the Blueprint (undoBufferReset, and undo.undoable false with UNDO_CLEARED_BY_COMPILE), so the move usually cannot be undone: run edit=arrange_nodes again or set positions back with edit=set_node_property.
batch: Run many graph edits in one call: add variables, functions (with their bodies), events and event dispatchers, create nodes, connect pins, set pin defaults and node properties, with $id references between steps. dryRun checks a batch without running any step.

effectPath.description: A Niagara system played at the blast (none by default).

elements.description: HUD pieces the new HUD starts with (default health_bar, crosshair, ammo_counter; [] for an empty canvas).

title.description: Role or section, such as Music.

name.description: Name credited.

entries.description: Credits entries in order; default is four placeholder sections.

enumPath.description: For SwitchOnEnum, ForEachElementInEnum, GetNumEnumEntries, EnumLiteral and CastByteToEnum: the enum whose values become the node's pins (a Switch on Enum's outputs are named after them), a Blueprint enum asset (/Game/Data/E_Phase) or a native one (/Script/Engine.ECollisionChannel); without it the node is refused.

explosionDamage.description: Damage at the centre of the blast, less toward its edge (default 50).

explosionRadius.description: Radius of the blast in units (default 400); walls between it and an actor shield that actor.

exposeOnSpawn.description: Expose on Spawn: the variable becomes an input pin on SpawnActor and Create Widget nodes for this class, set as the actor is made (before its BeginPlay). Makes it instance-editable too, as the editor does.

fadeTime.description: Seconds of the fade: the damage flash (default 0.6) or the loading screen FadeIn animation (0 makes none).

fallDelay.description: Seconds it shakes before it drops (default 0.5).

fallHeight.description: How far below its respawn point the pawn may fall before it respawns, in units (default 2000).

fillValue.description: A HorizontalBox, VerticalBox or ScrollBox child: the Fill weight, 0 or more (1 by default; a child of 2 gets twice the space of a child of 1). Given without sizeRule it makes the child Fill.

filter.description: Only nodes whose title or name, or whose pin default value or default object path, contains this text (case-insensitive, spaces ignored), e.g. "IA_Move", "Set bLocked", or "WBP_MainMenu" for the Create Widget node whose Class pin holds /Game/UI/WBP_MainMenu.WBP_MainMenu_C; or whose input is wired from a variable or component of that name, so "Arm" lists every node that reads or moves the Arm component (find each writer before driving it from Tick).

fireRate.description: Most shots a minute (default 300 for shoot, 60 for turret).

folder.description: Destination /Game folder for a Widget Blueprint.

followExec.description: Also walk this many nodes (1-50) along the exec wires leaving the node, depth-first (a Branch's then side before its else), and list each under chain with its inputs.

font.description: Font asset path. Omitted keeps the current font; fontSize alone resizes it.

fontFamily.description: Font asset for a TextBlock, e.g. /Engine/EngineFonts/Roboto or a project font.

fromNodeId.description: Node the wire leaves (its nodeGuid, an 8+ hex prefix of it, or its node name); required, or send sourceNode.

fromPinName.description: Output pin it leaves from; required, or send sourcePin.

functionName.description: Function a CallFunction node calls (the same as memberName), e.g. PrintString.

graphName.description: Event graph page to add the event to; omitted, the main EventGraph.

heal.description: Health given to the pawn that collects it; it reaches an actor with health (add_health) as negative damage.

hideAfter.description: Seconds the hint stays once shown (default 0: while the pawn stays in the area).

hoverSoundPath.description: Sound a Button plays when the pointer moves onto it (SoundCue, SoundWave or MetaSound path); an empty string clears it.

ignoreTimeDilation.description: Play at real speed while the game is slowed down or sped up.

image.description: Also return the first size's picture with each finding outlined (red, orange, yellow, grey from most to least severe).

includePins.description: When true, graph details include per-node pins and links.

includeProgressBar.description: Whether the loading screen has a progress bar (default true).

oneOf.description: Position among the children of that panel (0 = first). Default: right after the original, or last under another panel.
Position among the children of the new parent after the move (0 = first). Without it the widget goes last.

index.description: Position among the children of that panel (0 = first). Default: right after the original, or last under another panel.

info.description:
Which get blueprint variant to run; omit for 'blueprint'.
blueprint: Retrieve metadata for one Blueprint asset.
property: Read a property value from a Blueprint asset or its CDO, or a component default as Component.Property.

inputActionAssetPath.description: Enhanced Input action asset path accepted in place of inputActionPath.

inputActionPath.description: An Input Action to use instead of the one the behaviour makes next to the Blueprint (IA_Sprint, IA_Shoot, IA_Dash).

inputAxisName.description: Axis name for an InputAxis event node.

inputs.description: Function inputs, each {name, type}, with the types add_event parameters take (Float, Vector, Actor, Array<Int> ...). A nameless entry or a type no pin takes is refused (TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED) before anything changes.

interfacePath.description: The interface: a Blueprint Interface asset path (/Game/Interfaces/BPI_Interactable) or a native interface class path or name.

invulnerableTime.description: Seconds after a hit during which further damage is ignored, so one touch costs one hit (default 0, none); heals still count.

isPublic.description: Access specifier: true public (the default), false private (callable only from this Blueprint).

itemCount.description: Placeholder shop item cards when items names none (1-48, default 8).

name.description: Item name shown on its card.

oneOf.description: Shop items in order (1-48, in place of itemCount): each card shows its name and price, and its button is Item_<n>_Buy, n counting from 1.
Rows the objective or quest tracker lists, top to bottom.

items.description: Rows the objective or quest tracker lists, top to bottom.

justification.description: Text justification of a TextBlock or RichTextBlock: left, center or right. To centre the widget itself in its slot use set_alignment.

key.description: Localization key assigned to the text widget.

keyLabel.description: Key shown in the interaction prompt badge, such as E.

keys.description: Many keyframes in one call, in place of time: each {time, propertyValue or value, and any of slotName, trackType, interpolation that differ from the call's own}. Every key is checked before any is written: a refused one is named by its index (keys[3]) and nothing is added. The Widget Blueprint is saved once.

killAtZero.description: Kill the actor when the time is up (default true; it needs the health behaviour to die). False only fires OnTimeUp.

kind.description:
Which add function variant to run; omit for 'function'.
function: Add a new function graph to a Blueprint with optional inputs and outputs; an existing function of that name is reused only when it matches the pure, inputs and outputs given. A name the parent class lets a Blueprint override (a widget's OnKeyDown) makes that override with its own signature, so leave inputs, outputs, pure and isPublic out.
event: Add an event node to a Blueprint event graph: built-in, custom, or bound to a component delegate (componentName plus eventName, e.g. OnComponentBeginOverlap on a BoxComponent) or to a Widget Blueprint widget's event (componentName the widget, e.g. PlayButton with OnClicked).

knockback.description: Speed a touching Character is launched away from the actor at, in units per second (default 0, none).

label.description: Text before the number (default the variable name; empty for the number alone).

launchVelocity.description: Launch velocity [x, y, z] in units per second, world axes (default [0, 0, 1200], straight up).

layout.description: beside (default): each listed node to the nearest free slot beside a node left in place that it is wired to. layered: the listed nodes in columns along the links among them, left to right as the flow runs, a pure value in the column before its first reader, crossings reduced; the first listed node stays where it is and nodes left out are ignored (for a whole event, list the event first, then its nodes).

layoutProperty.description:
Which set widget layout variant to run.
anchor: Set the anchor points (min/max) for a widget in a canvas panel slot.
position: Set the position offset for a widget in its slot.
size: Set the size of a widget in its slot: a size override {x,y} for a CanvasPanel child, or sizeRule (Auto or Fill) and fillValue (the Fill weight) for a HorizontalBox, VerticalBox or ScrollBox child.
alignment: Set the alignment (0-1) for a widget in its slot.
padding: Set the padding for a widget in its slot.
z_order: Set the Z-order for a widget in a canvas panel slot.
visibility: Set the visibility mode (Visible, Collapsed, Hidden, etc.) for a widget.
clipping: Set the clipping mode (Inherit, ClipToBounds, etc.) for a widget.
render_transform: Set the render transform (translation, shear, angle) for a widget.
style: Set the visual style (color, font size, face and letter spacing, text, text justification, brush texture, button hover/press sounds) for a widget, or copy the look of another text block with copyStyleFrom.

length.description: How long it plays, in seconds (a new timeline: 5).

letterSpacing.description: Extra space between the letters of a TextBlock, in thousandths of an em (0 normal, 100 airy, negative tighter).

limit.description: Return at most this many nodes; totalCount and hasMore say what is left. Use it with includePins on a big graph.

location.description: Relative location {x, y, z} for an SCS component template.

look.description: Also turn the view with the mouse and the right stick (default true); false for a fixed camera.
