loop.description: Start over at the end, again and again.

mapSize.description: Minimap width and height in pixels (default 220).

mappingContextPath.description: The Input Mapping Context its keys go in (the project's own); default the one the pawn already registers, else /Game/Input/IMC_MCP.

materialPath.description: Material asset path for a component.

maxAlive.description: Most of its spawned actors alive at once (default 5); a destroyed one frees its place.

maxDesiredHeight.description: Maximum desired height of a size box.

maxDesiredWidth.description: Maximum desired width of a size box.

maxFindings.description: Most findings listed (1-200, default 50); counts and findingCount still count them all.

maxVisibleObjectives.description: Rows the objective tracker shows (1-12, default 3); longer items lists are cut to this.

memberClass.description: Only functions an object of this class calls on itself (Character, or a Blueprint path), no library functions.

memberName.description: The function, variable or event the node uses (PrintString, GetGameTimeInSeconds). A function whose name is not known: inspect_graph info functions finds it by what it does. A variable Blueprints cannot read, or for VariableSet write (not Blueprint-visible, read-only), is refused with VARIABLE_NOT_ACCESSIBLE.

menuId.description: In place of nodeType: any node by its action-menu id, Category|Title with spaces removed, as read_graph_as_code prints it (Development|PrintString, Utilities|FlowControl|Branch, Variables|GetHealth, Utilities|Operators|Add); AddEvent|Custom|Name makes a custom event named Name. An id this graph's menu does not offer is refused (MENU_ID_NOT_FOUND) with the ids it offers for that title.

meshPath.description: Static/Skeletal mesh asset path for a mesh component.

message.description: The text shown: a game over's message (default GAME OVER), or the hint itself (required for hint).

name.description: Name for the new Blueprint or asset.

newName.description: Name of the copy (default the original name with _Copy; _1, _2... is added when that name is taken). Every widget under it is copied as <its own name>_Copy, made unique the same way: copying QuitButton gives QuitButton_Copy and its label QuitButtonText_Copy. copiedWidgets lists the pairs.

nextLevel.description: Level opened once the goal is reached, by name or /Game path (a path must exist). Omitted: the game stays in this level, and OnGoalReached is left for other logic.

nodeGuid.description: Node GUID accepted in place of nodeId.

nodeId.description: Id of an existing node: the nodeGuid edit_graph returned when it made the node, or a nodeId inspect_graph lists.

oneOf.description: Several node ids or guids to delete in one call, in place of nodeId. Every id must resolve to a deletable node or nothing is deleted.
The nodes to move, by nodeId or nodeGuid. Nodes left out stay where they are and anchor the ones listed; a node wired to nothing left in place goes back where it was and is listed under unmoved.

nodeIds.description: Several node ids or guids to delete in one call, in place of nodeId. Every id must resolve to a deletable node or nothing is deleted.

nodeType.description: The node to create: CallFunction (memberName, plus memberClass for a function of another class), Event (eventName: BeginPlay, Tick), CustomEvent (customEventName), VariableGet or VariableSet (memberName), Cast (targetClass), InputAxisEvent (inputAxisName), Branch, Sequence, Select, Switch, SwitchOnInt, SwitchOnEnum (enumPath: one exec output per value, named after it), SwitchOnString, DoOnce, DoN, FlipFlop, Gate, MultiGate, ForLoop, ForEachLoop, WhileLoop (each also WithBreak), MakeArray, GetArrayItem (an array's Get: pins Array, Dimension 1 for the index, Output), MakeStruct and BreakStruct (structPath), SpawnActorFromClass, GetAllActorsOfClass, Self, CallDelegate (memberName: an event dispatcher, memberClass: another class's), BindEvent (the same, plus eventName: a Bind Event node and a custom event with the dispatcher's inputs wired to it, eventNodeGuid in the reply),Timeline (timelineName; edit_timeline keys its tracks), Reroute, Comment, MathExpression (its formula goes in set_node_property Expression) (a Switch on Int is made with only Default: wire a case by its number, from "$id.0", "$id.1"..., and the case pin is added; a Sequence or a commutative math node grows its inputs the same way); a common function by name (PrintString, Delay, SetActorLocation, GetPlayerPawn, GetActorOfClass, IsValid, PlaySound2D; IsValid is the pure function, K2Node_IsValid the Is Valid macro with exec pins exec, InputObject, Is Valid and Is Not Valid); or a K2Node class name that inspect_graph info=node_types lists. In an Animation Blueprint's AnimGraph or a state's graph (graphName), any animation node by class: AnimGraphNode_TwoBoneIK, TwoBoneIK or Two Bone IK (info=node_types with filter IK lists them; animation_physics configure_anim_graph_node set_value sets its settings); a node the graph cannot hold is refused (NODE_NOT_ALLOWED_IN_GRAPH). For create_struct_make_break_nodes: make or break.

oldName.description: Current name of the variable or component.

onHoveredFunction.description: Function the Button calls when the pointer moves onto it; created when it does not exist.

onUnhoveredFunction.description: Function the Button calls when the pointer leaves it; created when it does not exist.

openEditor.description: Also open it in the Widget Blueprint editor, which takes focus (default false).

oneOf.description: SCS operations applied in order. Each entry is an object with `type` plus that operation's own fields; `type: "add_component"` also takes componentName, componentClass (or componentType), attachTo, transform, meshPath, materialPath and a nested properties bag; `type: "modify_component"` takes the same transform, meshPath, materialPath and properties for a component that already exists (its own, or a parent Blueprint's part, edited through this Blueprint's override of it); transform is {location:{x,y,z}, rotation:{pitch,yaw,roll}, scale:{x,y,z}} (or those three directly on the operation), and a part left out keeps its current value, while a transform that cannot be applied (a part that is not an {x,y,z} or {pitch,yaw,roll} object or a three-number array, or a component with no transform) is named in warnings, not skipped, as is a meshPath or materialPath that does not load or that its component cannot take; `type: "attach_component"` (or "reparent") moves componentName under parentComponent (or attachTo/newParent). A failed operation is named in warnings, and the call fails when none applied. Each result carries instancesUpdated (placed copies that took the change, 0 included) with up to three of their paths, and a hint, repeated in warnings, when a mesh or material lands on a hidden component.

Steps run in order, 1-200. Each is {edit, ...that edit's own params}. Member steps come before the nodes that use them: add_variable (variableName, variableType as add_variable takes it: basic, class, struct, enum and container types, defaultValue, isPublic, exposeOnSpawn, category), add_function (functionName, inputs, outputs, pure, isPublic; the create steps of its body set graphName to the function name, and a connect or pin step that leaves graphName out runs in the graph of the node it names; with an id, "$id" is its entry node and "$id_return" its return node, which exists when outputs are declared), add_event (customEventName and parameters, or componentName plus eventName for a component or Widget Blueprint widget delegate, e.g. PlayButton with OnClicked) and add_event_dispatcher (dispatcherName, parameters [{name, type}]). Node steps: create_node, connect_pins, set_pin_default_value, set_node_property, create_reroute_node. create_node also takes nodeType CallDelegate (memberName: a dispatcher, memberClass: another class's), BindEvent (the same: a Bind Event node and a custom event, eventName, wired to it; with an id, "$id_event" is that event, whose then pin runs when the dispatcher fires, and the object bound goes to "$id.self"), Message (memberClass: an interface, memberName: its function), AsyncTask (memberClass: the task or async-action class, memberName: its static factory; event graphs only), FunctionResult (one more return node in a function graph) and MathExpression with expression (the formula, checked and set as set_node_property Expression sets it, before pinDefaults, which can then name its inputs; a name in the formula that is one of the Blueprint's variables reads that variable and gets no input pin, any other name becomes an input pin). Optional per step: id (names the created node; later steps use "$id" in fromNodeId, toNodeId and nodeId), from and to ("$id.PinName" shorthand for connect_pins), pinDefaults (create_node only: {PinName: value} applied to the new node; a read-only pin such as Set Text's Value gets a MakeLiteral node wired into it). "$entry" is the graph's own entry node (a Construction Script or function graph starts there: from "$entry.then"). A pure node (math, a getter) runs again for each node that reads it, so after a Set node read the new value from the Set node's Output_Get pin, not from the math that computed it. A create step without posX and posY is auto-placed, and once every step ran it moves beside a node it is wired to (right of what runs it, below-left of what reads it); one whose posX and posY overlap an existing node is placed at the nearest free position instead, and its result says where in placementWarning, so a crowded row never stops the batch (a single create_node call still refuses an overlap). Every function, variable, dispatcher and async factory a step names is checked before any step runs, so a misspelled one fails the batch with nothing applied; any other failure stops the batch at that step and undoes the steps before it (members, nodes, links and pin defaults, in every graph), so a failed batch leaves the Blueprint as it was: fix that step and send the whole batch again. Only a set_node_property on a node that was already there stays, and the error names it.

operations.description: SCS operations applied in order. Each entry is an object with `type` plus that operation's own fields; `type: "add_component"` also takes componentName, componentClass (or componentType), attachTo, transform, meshPath, materialPath and a nested properties bag; `type: "modify_component"` takes the same transform, meshPath, materialPath and properties for a component that already exists (its own, or a parent Blueprint's part, edited through this Blueprint's override of it); transform is {location:{x,y,z}, rotation:{pitch,yaw,roll}, scale:{x,y,z}} (or those three directly on the operation), and a part left out keeps its current value, while a transform that cannot be applied (a part that is not an {x,y,z} or {pitch,yaw,roll} object or a three-number array, or a component with no transform) is named in warnings, not skipped, as is a meshPath or materialPath that does not load or that its component cannot take; `type: "attach_component"` (or "reparent") moves componentName under parentComponent (or attachTo/newParent). A failed operation is named in warnings, and the call fails when none applied. Each result carries instancesUpdated (placed copies that took the change, 0 included) with up to three of their paths, and a hint, repeated in warnings, when a mesh or material lands on a hidden component.

outlineColor.description: Outline color (0-1 values) drawn around a rounded brush. Ignored unless cornerRadius is set.

outlineWidth.description: Outline thickness in pixels around a rounded brush. Ignored unless cornerRadius is set.

outputs.description: Function outputs (its return values), each {name, type}, with the types inputs take.

overrideXY.description: Replace the horizontal speed of the Character instead of adding to it (default false).

oneOf.description: CustomEvent inputs, each {name, type}: float, double, int, int64, bool, byte, string, name, text, object, class, softobject, an enum or struct name (Vector, Rotator, Transform, /Script/CoreUObject.Vector) or a class name (Actor) for an object of that class. An array, set or map parameter needs add_event. A nameless entry or another type is refused (TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED) before anything changes.

Event parameters, each {name, type}. Types: bool, byte, int, int64, float, double, string, name, text, vector, vector2d, rotator, transform, color, linearcolor, object, class, a class, struct or enum name (Actor, HitResult), Object:/Script/Engine.Actor, Struct:<path>, Enum:<path>, and Array<T>, Set<T> or Map<Key,Value>. A nameless entry or a type no pin takes is refused (TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED) before anything changes.

parameters.description: CustomEvent inputs, each {name, type}: float, double, int, int64, bool, byte, string, name, text, object, class, softobject, an enum or struct name (Vector, Rotator, Transform, /Script/CoreUObject.Vector) or a class name (Actor) for an object of that class. An array, set or map parameter needs add_event. A nameless entry or another type is refused (TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED) before anything changes.

parentClass.description: Parent class path for Blueprint creation (e.g. /Script/Engine.Actor).

parentComponent.description: Parent component to put the component under: one of this Blueprint's own, a parent Blueprint's scene component, or a native one (Mesh, CapsuleComponent).

parentSlot.description: Parent slot to add the widget to.

path.description: A folder (e.g. /Game/Blueprints) to scan instead of one Blueprint: each Blueprint under it, subfolders included, that has a component matching componentClass, its own or inherited, is listed under blueprints (at most 300 Blueprints are opened; truncated says when more exist).

pinName.description: Pin name on a graph node.

points.description: The route: [x, y, z] offsets from where the actor starts, in world axes, visited in turn and looped (default [[500, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0]], back and forth). Each placed copy keeps its own route (PatrolPoints or PlatformPoints is instance editable).

posX.description: X position of the new node in the graph (default 0, the origin). add_node and create_node move a node given no position right past any node at the origin, and refuse a given spot another node covers (NODE_OVERLAP, with a suggestedPosition).

posY.description: Y position of the new node in the graph (default 0).

positionX.description: Canvas slot X position, applied only when the parent is a canvas panel.

positionY.description: Canvas slot Y position, applied only when the parent is a canvas panel.

preset.description: Named anchor preset (e.g. TopCenter) applied in place of anchorMin/anchorMax.

pressSoundPath.description: Sound a Button plays when it is pressed (SoundCue, SoundWave or MetaSound path); an empty string clears it.

projectileClass.description: The projectile it shoots: a Blueprint path (/Game/Weapons/BP_Fireball) or class path.

properties.description: Property bag applied to the CDO, component template, or node: name to value. A dotted name reaches a member of a component or struct (CapsuleComponent.CapsuleRadius, BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled); on a Blueprint's class defaults a native component also answers to its object name (CollisionCylinder.CapsuleRadius, CharMoveComp.MaxWalkSpeed). An object or class reference takes a path (a Blueprint class path ends in _C); null or "None" clears it.

propertyName.description: A member variable to put the metadata on (as set_variable_metadata does); omitted, the keys go on the Blueprint class.

oneOf.description: The key value, by trackType: opacity a number 0-1; color {r,g,b,a} or [r,g,b,a]; translation, scale or shear {x,y} or [x,y]; angle a number in degrees; transform any of {translation:{x,y}, scale:{x,y}, angle, shear:{x,y}}. A value of the wrong shape is refused before anything is added.
Value to assign to the property. An object or class reference takes a path (a Blueprint class path ends in _C); null or "None" clears it.

set_node_property: text for NodeComment, a number for NodePosX or NodePosY, true or false for bCommentBubbleVisible or bDisabled, Enabled, Disabled or DevelopmentOnly for EnabledState, the text of a Math Expression node's Expression (each other name becomes a number input pin, except one the Blueprint has a variable of, which reads that variable; a number input is never a vector, so add to a location as VECT(x, y, z + 20) from its parts; a comparison used as a number is refused: write SelectFloat(1, 0, A > B); an input pin is never true/false, so join true/false values from other nodes with BooleanAND, BooleanOR or BooleanXOR nodes), an asset path for a reflected field. set_pin_default_value: the pin's new default as text: a number, true or false, an enum value name, a vector as X,Y,Z (0,150,110), a rotator as P,Y,R, or an asset path.

propertyValue.description: The key value, by trackType: opacity a number 0-1; color {r,g,b,a} or [r,g,b,a]; translation, scale or shear {x,y} or [x,y]; angle a number in degrees; transform any of {translation:{x,y}, scale:{x,y}, angle, shear:{x,y}}. A value of the wrong shape is refused before anything is added.

pure.description: Build a Cast node pure (no exec pins, as in the editor's Convert to pure cast); default false.

radius.description: How far across from the spawner an actor may appear, in units (default 0: on the spawner).

range.description: Distance within which it turns to the player and fires, in units (default 2000).

relations.description: How the widgets relate, each one an object; the widgets named must be children of one Canvas Panel.

widget.description: The widget the relation is about (every type but the align and same ones).

of.description: leftOf, rightOf, above, below: the widget it is placed against (widget leftOf of).

widgets.description: align and same types: the widgets lined up or sized alike.

gap.description: leftOf, rightOf, above, below: exactly this far apart, in Slate units (left out: at least 0 apart).

value.description: width, height: the size; inset: the distance from the edge; in Slate units.

edge.description: inset: the edge of the panel.

axis.description: center: across (x), up and down (y) or both (default both).

strength.description: required (default) holds exactly or the call is refused; the others are kept as far as the required ones allow, stronger first.

remove.description: Drop the interface instead (its function graphs go with it).

renderOpacity.description: Render opacity (0-1) applied to the widget and everything under it.

resolution.description: Screen size the boxes are solved at, "WxH" (default 1920x1080).

oneOf.description: Screen sizes the relations are checked at afterwards, each "WxH" up to 3840x2160 (default 1920x1080, 1280x720 and 3440x1440).
Screen sizes to lay it out at, each "WxH" (up to 3840x2160), the project's DPI scaling applied as in the game (default 1920x1080, 1280x720 and 3440x1440).

resolutions.description: Screen sizes the relations are checked at afterwards, each "WxH" up to 3840x2160 (default 1920x1080, 1280x720 and 3440x1440).

respawnTime.description: Seconds after it starts to drop until it is back in place (default 3); 0 never: it is destroyed 5 seconds into its fall.

responseCount.description: Placeholder response buttons under the dialog line when buttons names none (0-6, default 3).

restartDelay.description: Seconds before the level opens again (default 3); 0 never restarts it.

rotation.description: Relative rotation {pitch, yaw, roll} for an SCS component template.

rowCount.description: Rows given an equal share of the height (0-64).

rules.description: The rules to run, default all: tick_heavy, unreachable, random_fanout, infinite_while, never_assigned, unguarded_read. An unknown name is INVALID_ARGUMENT.

safeZone.description: Share of each side of the screen that is title-safe (default 0.9: a 5% margin on every side); 1 turns the check off.

save.description: Save the Blueprint after the edit (default true, so it survives an editor restart). false leaves it compiled in memory and unsaved: a trial change to put back, or to save later with control_editor save_all.

saveAfterCompile.description: Whether to save the asset after compiling.

savePath.description: Destination /Game folder for a new Blueprint.

scale.description: Relative scale {x, y, z} for an SCS component template, or {x, y} for a widget render transform.

screen.description:
Which create widget template variant to run.
main_menu: Create a main menu Widget Blueprint: backdrop, title and a column of buttons (default Play, Settings, Quit).
pause_menu: Create a pause menu Widget Blueprint: dimmed backdrop, PAUSED title and buttons (default Resume, Settings, Main Menu).
settings_menu: Create a settings menu Widget Blueprint: graphics, audio and controls rows with real combo boxes, check boxes and sliders, plus Apply and Back.
loading_screen: Create a loading screen Widget Blueprint: backdrop, Loading text, optional progress bar and optional FadeIn animation.
hud: Create a HUD Widget Blueprint on a canvas holding ready-made pieces (default health bar, crosshair, ammo counter).
dialog: Create a dialog box Widget Blueprint: speaker name, wrapped dialog line, response buttons and a continue hint.
inventory: Create an inventory Widget Blueprint: titled panel with a grid of item slots (default 6 by 4).
radial_menu: Create a radial menu Widget Blueprint: a ring of round buttons around a centre label (default 8 segments).
credits: Create a credits Widget Blueprint: centred scrolling list of role and name pairs with a Back button.
shop: Create a shop Widget Blueprint: header with currency, a scrolling grid of item cards each with a Buy button, and Close.

seconds.description: The time limit in whole seconds (default 60).

settingsType.description: Which settings sections the menu holds (default all).

showSpeakerName.description: Whether the dialog shows the speaker name line (default true).

sideDamage.description: Damage to a player Character that bumps it from the side or below, at most once a second (default 0, none, or the damage of a damage_on_touch it takes over).

size.description: Size override {x,y} of a CanvasPanel child. A HorizontalBox, VerticalBox or ScrollBox child is sized by sizeRule and fillValue instead.

sizeRule.description: A HorizontalBox, VerticalBox or ScrollBox child: Auto sizes it to its content, Fill shares the free space between the Fill children by their fillValue weights (case-insensitive). Two buttons in a row that should share it evenly are both Fill with the same fillValue; a ScrollBox child that is Fill spans the box when it is shorter, so a vertical alignment of center can center it.

slotName.description: Name of the root widget of the piece (default: the piece name, such as HealthBar); its parts are named <slotName>_<Part>.

soundPath.description: Sound asset played at the actor: where a pickup was collected, a goal when the player reaches it, a pad on each launch, where a teleported pawn arrives, or an explosive blows up.

sourceNode.description: Source node id accepted in place of fromNodeId.

sourcePin.description: Output pin name accepted in place of fromPinName.

spawnClass.description: The actor it spawns: a Blueprint path (/Game/Enemies/BP_Slime) or class path; not the spawner itself.

speed.description: Units per second it travels between points (default 200).

stopDistance.description: How close it gets to the player before it stops, in units (default 100).

stringKey.description: Key looked up within the string table.

stringTableId.description: String table asset backing a localized text binding.

structPath.description: For MakeStruct or BreakStruct: the struct, a Blueprint Struct asset (/Game/Data/F_Item) or a native one (/Script/SlateCore.SlateColor, /Script/CoreUObject.Vector); without it the node is refused.

targetClass.description: Target class for a node that carries one: a Cast target, a CreateWidget or SpawnActor class, the subsystem a Get Subsystem node returns, or the class GetAllActorsOfClass and GetActorOfClass look for (their result is then typed to it, so a ForEach element wires to its functions). Required for cast and subsystem nodes, whose type is stored on the node itself and cannot be set afterwards.

targetNode.description: Target node id accepted in place of toNodeId.

targetPin.description: Input pin name accepted in place of toPinName.

text.description: Text content for a text block or button.

textName.description: The TextBlock in the widget that the behaviour writes: the count of counter_hud (default <variable>Counter), or the message of game_over (default GameOver_Text) or of a hint (default Hint_Text). A text named here must already be in the widget.

textStyle.description:
Which set font variant to run; omit for 'font'.
font: Set the font asset and size on a Text Block or Rich Text Block inside a Widget Blueprint.
margin: Set the slot margin on a widget held by a Horizontal Box, Vertical Box, Overlay, or Border.

texturePath.description: Texture asset path for an image or brush.

timelineName.description: For nodeType Timeline: the timeline it plays, which edit_timeline keys; a name the Blueprint lacks makes one (omitted, a new Timeline_N). One node plays a timeline, in the event graph of an Actor Blueprint.

title.description: Objective tracker heading (default OBJECTIVES) or the quest name (default Quest Name).

toNodeId.description: Node the wire enters; required, or send targetNode.

toPinName.description: Input pin it enters; required, or send targetPin.

touch.description: The UI is touched: also flag interactive widgets under 44 Slate units on their short side (default false).

trackType.description: Animation track type: opacity/renderOpacity (RenderOpacity), color (ColorAndOpacity), translation/scale/angle/shear or transform (RenderTransform).

tracks.description: Tracks to add, or whose keys to replace (a track keeps its type): each {name, type, keys, interpolation}. name is the node pin its value comes out of; type float (default), vector, color or event (an exec pin that fires at each key time); keys [{time in seconds, value}], value a number, {x, y, z} or {r, g, b, a} by type and none for an event; interpolation auto (smooth, default), linear or constant. Every track is checked before anything changes; a bad one is named by its index (tracks[1].keys[0]).

tree.description: The layout as one nested node {type, name, children[], slot{}, ...props}. type: a UMG class short name (CanvasPanel, Overlay, VerticalBox, HorizontalBox, Border, SizeBox, ScaleBox, UniformGridPanel, Spacer, TextBlock, RichTextBlock, Image, ProgressBar, Button). name: the widget name, unique in the Widget Blueprint (each becomes a variable a graph can read). Props: text, fontSize, color [r,g,b,a] (text colour, border brush, image tint, bar fill), justify left|center|right, autoWrap, opacity, visibility, padding (number or [l,t,r,b]: a border's inner padding), radius (rounded border, image or button) with outlineColor and outlineWidth, imageSize [w,h], texture (an image's texture path), material (an Image's or Border's brush: a UI material or instance that draws the whole widget, such as a rounded panel with its rim and gradient), percent (progress bar), width, height, maxHeight (size box). Text blocks also take typeface (Bold, Regular, Light, Italic), fontFamily, letterSpacing, outline with outlineColor, and shadowOffset [x,y] with shadowColor. slot places the node in its parent: in a canvas anchors [minX,minY,maxX,maxY], alignment [x,y], position [x,y], size [w,h], autoSize, z; in a box padding, hAlign (left|center|right|fill), vAlign (top|center|bottom|fill) and fill (a share of the free space). A Widget Blueprint with no root yet gets a canvas, and a tree root with no slot (and no positionX/Y or sizeX/Y) fills it. An unknown field is refused, not ignored; at most 200 widgets.

typeface.description: Face of the TextBlock font: Regular, Bold, Italic, Light... A face the font lacks is refused with the list it has.

unusedOnly.description: Only nodes that do nothing: a call no exec wire reaches, or a getter, math or other pure node whose result nothing reads (what is left behind when the node that read it was deleted; the compiler says nothing). Events, input actions and function entries never count. Combines with filter.

useLastKeyframe.description: End at the last key instead of at length.

usePathfinding.description: Follow the navigation mesh (default true; the level needs a NavMeshBoundsVolume, from manage_level_structure create_volume); false heads straight for the player or the next point.

oneOf.description: New value for propertyName: a string, number or bool, or an object or array for a struct property.
A plain number for an opacity or angle key, in place of propertyValue.
Numeric value for a slider, spin box, or animation keyframe.

value.description: A plain number for an opacity or angle key, in place of propertyValue.

variableName.description: Variable name to add, remove, rename, or modify.

oneOf.description: Several variables to give the same metadata in one call (one compile and save), in place of or besides variableName.
Several variables to remove in one call, in place of or besides variableName. Every name must exist (any letter case), or nothing is removed and the reply lists the Blueprint's variables.

variableNames.description: Several variables to give the same metadata in one call (one compile and save), in place of or besides variableName.

variableType.description: Variable type, any case. Basic: Boolean, Byte, Integer, Int64, Float, Double, String, Name, Text, Vector, Vector2D, Vector4, Rotator, Transform, Color, LinearColor. References: Object or Class (any UObject), or Object:<class>, Class:<class>, SoftObject:<class>, SoftClass:<class> with a class name or path (Actor, /Script/UMG.Widget, /Game/Blueprints/BP_Door); a bare class name or path is an object reference to that class. Structs: struct:<path> (struct:/Game/Data/F_Item), a /Script path (/Script/Engine.HitResult) or a struct name (HitResult). Enums: enum:<object path> (enum:/Script/Engine.ECollisionChannel, enum:/Game/Enums/E_State.E_State). Containers: Array<T>, Set<T> or Map<Key,Value> (also Array:T, Set:T, Map:Key,Value); a map key is Byte, Integer, Int64, Name, String or an enum. Example: Array<Object:/Script/UMG.Widget>. An unknown spelling is refused with TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED and the reason.

waitForShaders.description: true: when the drawing left shaders compiling (the editor compiles a material's UI shaders the first time it is drawn: right after the editor starts, or after a material edit), wait for them, at most 25 seconds, and draw again; shaderWait in the reply says how long it waited. Default false: draw once and report shadersCompiling.

waitTime.description: Seconds it waits at each point (default 1).

widgetKind.description:
Which add content widget variant to run.
text_block: Add a Text Block widget for displaying read-only text.
rich_text_block: Add a Rich Text Block widget for styled/markup text.
image: Add an Image widget for displaying a texture or brush.
button: Add a Button widget for click interaction.
check_box: Add a Check Box widget for boolean toggle.
combo_box: Add a Combo Box (dropdown) widget for option selection.
slider: Add a Slider widget for range selection.
spin_box: Add a Spin Box widget for numeric increment/decrement.
progress_bar: Add a Progress Bar widget for percentage display.
text_input: Add a Text Input (editable text) widget for user text entry.
list_view: Add a List View widget for scrollable entry lists.
tree_view: Add a Tree View widget for hierarchical entry display.
component: Add a widget of any UMG class to a Widget Blueprint by class name.

widgetPath.description: A Widget Blueprint to show instead of the one made next to the Blueprint under UI/ (WBP_HealthBar, WBP_<variable>Counter, WBP_GameOver, WBP_Hint). One without the bar or the text gets it: the health bar HUD piece (add_game_widget), a text at the top right, a full-screen shade with the message, or a dark box at the bottom with the hint.

words.description: A few plain words for what the node does (game time, random number in range, distance between actors); a function matches on its name, keywords, category and description, best first, at most 10.

tools.name: manage_character
tools.description: Create Character Blueprints with movement, locomotion, and animation state machines.

acceleration.description: How fast it reaches its top speed, in cm/s per second (MaxAcceleration; engine default 2048).

airControl.description: How much it can steer in the air, 0 to 1 (AirControl; engine default 0.05).

applyAsOverrides.description: Apply exported materials back onto the character as overrides. Default true.

blocking.description: Wait for auto-rigging to finish before answering. Default false: the request is queued on the Epic cloud service and metahuman_status reports canBuild once it lands. True parks the editor until the service answers.

bodyMesh.description: Export the body skeletal mesh. Default true.

buildPath.description: Content folder for the assembled assets. Defaults to the palette setting.

cameraUsePawnControlRotation.description: Whether the spring arm follows the controller look rotation. The camera under it is always arm-relative.

canCrouch.description: Whether the character is allowed to crouch.

capsuleHalfHeight.description: Capsule collision half-height in world units.

capsuleRadius.description: Capsule collision radius in world units.

characterPath.description: Canonical /Game path of a MetaHuman Character asset.

commonFolderPath.description: Content folder for shared MetaHuman assets.

deceleration.description: How fast it stops on the ground with no input, in cm/s per second (BrakingDecelerationWalking; engine default 2048).

exportType.description: Which artifact to export: skeletal meshes, material instances, or DNA.

externalPath.description: Folder on disk for exported .dna files. DNA export only.

flySpeed.description: Top fly speed in cm/s (MaxFlySpeed; engine default 600).

fullBodyMesh.description: Export a combined full-body skeletal mesh. Default false.

gravityScale.description: Multiplier on world gravity (GravityScale; 1 is normal, 2 falls twice as hard).

groundFriction.description: How sharply it turns and stops on the ground (GroundFriction; engine default 8; lower slides like ice).

headMesh.description: Export the head skeletal mesh. Default true.

jumpHeight.description: The jump launch speed in cm/s, not a height (JumpZVelocity; engine default 420): it rises about v*v/(1960*gravityScale) cm, so 420 is about 90 cm and 600 about 1.8 m.

jumpHoldTime.description: Maximum jump hold time in seconds.

maxJumpCount.description: Jumps before landing (JumpMaxCount; 1 by default, 2 for a double jump).

movementProperty.description:
Which set movement property variant to run.
walk_speed: Set the top walking speed of a Character Blueprint (CharacterMovement MaxWalkSpeed, cm/s; engine default 600). Compiled and saved; the reply gives the value the compiled class holds. A negative speed is refused, and a Blueprint that is not a Character is NOT_A_CHARACTER.
jump_height: Set how fast a Character Blueprint leaves the ground when it jumps (CharacterMovement JumpZVelocity, cm/s; engine default 420): a launch speed, not a height. The apex is about speed squared / (1960 x gravityScale) cm, so 420 rises about 90 cm. Compiled and saved; the reply gives the value held. Negative is refused.
gravity_scale: Set the gravity multiplier of a Character Blueprint (CharacterMovement GravityScale: 1 is normal, 0 floats, negative falls upward). Compiled and saved; the reply gives the value held.
ground_friction: Set how quickly a walking Character Blueprint turns and stops (CharacterMovement GroundFriction; engine default 8, higher grips more). Compiled and saved; the reply gives the value held. Negative is refused.
braking_deceleration: Set how fast a walking Character Blueprint slows when no input is held (CharacterMovement BrakingDecelerationWalking, cm/s squared; engine default 2048). Compiled and saved; the reply gives the value held. Negative is refused.

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

nameOverride.description: Folder name for the assembled character instead of the asset name.

navAgentHeight.description: The height navigation plans paths for, in cm (NavAgentProps.AgentHeight).

navAgentRadius.description: The radius navigation plans paths for, in cm (NavAgentProps.AgentRadius).

orientToMovement.description: Whether the character orients rotation to movement.

overwrite.description: Overwrite existing assets instead of creating uniquely-named ones. Default true.

parentClass.description: Character class to derive from (default Character): a native Character subclass or a Character Blueprint path.

path.description: Canonical /Game output path for the created asset.

pipelineQuality.description: Quality level. Only meaningful when pipelineType is Optimized or UEFN.

pipelineType.description: Assembly pipeline. Cinematic is the film-quality path; Optimized and UEFN trade fidelity for runtime cost.

projectPath.description: Content folder receiving the exported assets.

reportProgress.description: Emit editor progress notifications during auto-rigging. Default false.

rigType.description: Face rig detail to request. JointsAndBlendShapes is required for facial animation.

rotationRate.description: Rotation rate in degrees per second.

runSpeed.description: Run speed; ignored when walkSpeed is also supplied.

setting.description:
Which configure character variant to run.
movement_speeds: Set a Character Blueprint's Character Movement speeds in one call, then compile and save it: walkSpeed (MaxWalkSpeed, engine default 600), crouchSpeed (300), swimSpeed (300), flySpeed (600), acceleration (MaxAcceleration, 2048), deceleration (braking while walking, 2048) and groundFriction (8), plus the jump fields setting=jump takes. A value not sent keeps its own. A Character has one walk speed: runSpeed sets it only when walkSpeed is absent, otherwise the reply says runSpeedApplied false with a warning (a sprint is game logic that raises MaxWalkSpeed while a key is held). The reply reads back every speed and jump value.
jump: Set how a Character Blueprint jumps, then compile and save it: jumpHeight is the launch speed (JumpZVelocity, engine default 420; the apex is about v squared over 1960 cm at gravity scale 1, so 420 rises 0.9 m and 600 about 1.8 m), jumpHoldTime (seconds holding the button keeps lifting, default 0), maxJumpCount (2 for a double jump), airControl (0-1 steering while falling, default 0.05), gravityScale (default 1) and fallingLateralFriction (default 0). A value not sent keeps its own; the reply reads back all six, jumpHeight as jumpZVelocity.
crouch: Let a Character Blueprint crouch, then compile and save it: canCrouch (off on a new Character, so Crouch does nothing until it is on), crouchSpeed (MaxWalkSpeedCrouched, engine default 300) and crouchedHalfHeight (the capsule half-height while crouched, default 40); a field not sent keeps its value. The reply reads back all three. Crouching still needs input that calls Crouch and UnCrouch, and an Animation Blueprint that plays a crouch pose from the crouched state.
rotation: Choose what turns a Character Blueprint, then compile and save it: orientToMovement turns it toward where it moves at rotationRate degrees per second (yaw; engine default 360); useControllerRotationYaw, Pitch and Roll make it face the controller's aim. A new Character faces the controller's yaw (useControllerRotationYaw true, orientToMovement false). A third-person character usually sets orientToMovement true and useControllerRotationYaw false; a strafing shooter the opposite. Keep only one of those two on: both on fight every frame. A value not sent keeps its own; the reply reads back all five.
capsule_component: Resize a Character Blueprint's collision capsule (capsuleRadius and capsuleHalfHeight in world units; a new Character starts at 34 by 88, the third-person template uses 42 by 96), then compile and save it; a size not sent keeps its value. The reply reads both sizes back; a Blueprint that is not a Character is refused (NOT_A_CHARACTER). Move the mesh with it: its meshOffset z is usually minus the half-height, so the feet sit on the capsule bottom.
mesh_component: Set the inherited Mesh of a Character Blueprint, then compile and save it: skeletalMeshPath, animBlueprintPath (the Animation Blueprint that animates it), and meshOffset and meshRotation relative to the capsule; a field not sent keeps its value. Refused before anything changes: a path that does not load (ASSET_NOT_FOUND), and an Animation Blueprint made for a skeleton the mesh does not take (SKELETON_MISMATCH), which would leave the character in its rest pose. The reply names skeletalMeshAssigned and animBlueprintAssigned. A mannequin-style mesh usually needs meshOffset z at minus the capsule half-height and meshRotation yaw -90 to face forward (+X).
camera_component: Give a Character a third-person follow camera: a spring arm behind it with a camera on its end, made when missing; an existing arm changes only in the fields sent.
nav_movement: Set how AI navigation sees a Character Blueprint, then compile and save it: navAgentRadius and navAgentHeight (the agent size its movement reports to pathfinding) and avoidanceEnabled (RVO avoidance, so moving characters steer around each other). By default a spawned character copies its capsule size over the nav agent size; sending a size turns that copy off so the size stays (navAgentFollowsCapsule false). A value not sent keeps its own; the reply reads back all three and navAgentFollowsCapsule. The navmesh itself is built for the agent sizes in the project's Navigation System settings.

springArmLagEnabled.description: Whether spring-arm camera lag is enabled.

springArmLagSpeed.description: How fast a lagging camera catches up (CameraLagSpeed; 10 on a new boom, higher is tighter); it lags only with springArmLagEnabled.

springArmLength.description: How far the camera sits behind the character, in cm (spring arm TargetArmLength; 300 on a new boom).

swimSpeed.description: Top swim speed in cm/s (MaxSwimSpeed; engine default 300).

useControllerRotationPitch.description: Whether controller pitch drives actor rotation.

useControllerRotationRoll.description: Whether controller roll drives actor rotation.

useControllerRotationYaw.description: Whether controller yaw drives actor rotation.

walkSpeed.description: Top ground speed in cm/s (MaxWalkSpeed; engine default 600).

tools.name: manage_combat
tools.description: Create weapons with hitscan/projectile firing, configure damage types, hitboxes, reload, and melee combat (combos, parry, block).

actorName.description: The actor to hit, by name in the running game; PlayerPawn names the pawn the player controls.

attachmentSlots.description: Attachment slots: each adds an AttachPoint_<slotName> scene component under WeaponMesh (kept when there). An empty list or a nameless slot is refused before anything changes.

slotName.description: Slot name, giving the component AttachPoint_<slotName>.

socketName.description: Socket of the WeaponMesh static mesh the attach point sits on; omitted, it sits at the mesh origin.

allowedTypes.description: Attachment types the slot takes, added to the attach point component tags for the game to read (ComponentHasTag, GetComponentsByTag).

bounceVelocityRatio.description: Fraction of velocity retained on bounce (0-1).

causerName.description: The actor that deals it (DamageCauser), by name; its controller, or the controller of the pawn it is, instigates. Omitted: no causer.

damage.description: Damage dealt to the actor it hits (default 20); kept in its Damage variable, which a placed copy can change.

damageMultiplier.description: Default of the Blueprint variable HitboxDamageMultiplier (added when missing; default 1). Nothing reads it until the Blueprint damage logic does.

damageType.description: Damage type class, a path or a name (default DamageType).

fireRate.description: Rate of fire in rounds per minute.

hitboxBoneName.description: Bone of the Blueprint skeletal mesh (an SCS SkeletalMeshComponent or an inherited one such as a Character mesh) the hitbox attaches to; fails when the Blueprint has no skeletal mesh.

hitboxSize.description: Hitbox dimensions: extent for Box, radius/halfHeight for Sphere and Capsule.

hitboxType.description: Hitbox shape and component: Capsule (default, HitboxCapsule), Box (HitboxBox) or Sphere (HitboxSphere). The component of that name is kept when the Blueprint has it, else added; any other value is refused.

info.description:
Which get combat info variant to run; omit for 'info'.
info: Read combat configuration back from a Blueprint.
stats: Read combat stats back from a Blueprint.

isDamageZoneHead.description: Default of the Blueprint variable bIsHeadshotZone (added when missing; default false), for its damage logic to read.

kind.description:
Which create combat asset variant to run.
weapon_blueprint: Create an Actor Blueprint named name in path (default /Game) for a weapon: a WeaponMesh component showing weaponMeshPath, and BaseDamage, FireRate, Range and Spread variables set to baseDamage, fireRate, range and spread (defaults 25, 600, 10000, 2). It has no firing logic of its own. A mesh that does not load, or a path an asset already holds, is refused before anything is made; the Blueprint is compiled and saved.
projectile_blueprint: Create a projectile Blueprint named name in path (default /Game) that flies, damages what it hits and is destroyed on impact; projectileMeshPath is its mesh, and one that does not load, or a path an asset already holds, is refused before anything is made.
damage_type: Create a DamageType Blueprint named name in path (default /Game), a damage class ApplyDamage can name and a damaged actor can tell apart; compiled and saved, and a path an asset already holds is refused.
damage_type_setup: Create a DamageType Blueprint named name in path (default /Game) and answer its damageTypePath; compiled and saved, and a path an asset already holds is refused.

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

path.description: Canonical /Game output path for the created asset.

projectileClass.description: The projectile the weapon shoots: its Blueprint path (/Game/Weapons/BP_Bullet) or class path.

projectileGravityScale.description: Gravity scale applied to the projectile.

range.description: Effective weapon range in world units.

setting.description:
Which configure damage variant to run.
hit_detection: Make sure a Blueprint has a hitbox of a shape and set its damage multiplier variable.
hitbox: Add a shaped hitbox component, optionally bound to a bone of the Blueprint skeletal mesh.

weaponMeshPath.description: Canonical /Game weapon static or skeletal mesh path.

tools.name: manage_effect
tools.description: Niagara particle systems, VFX, debug shapes, and GPU simulations. Create systems, emitters, modules, and control particle effects.

actorName.description: A placed actor running the system: its own user parameter values (a tint, a rate set for that placement) come back under placed, with the ones that differ from the system's defaults (userParameters value) listed as overridden.

attachToActor.description: Name of the actor the spawned system attaches to.

autoActivate.description: Start the effect at once (default true); false places it switched off until a particle track or Activate starts it.

boxSize.description: Box half extents as [x, y, z] for shapeType box (default the radius on every axis).

oneOf.description: Color as an {r, g, b, a} object or an [r, g, b, a] array: 0 to 255 channels for debug_shape, 0 to 1 for a light.

Light color as an {r, g, b, a} object or an [r, g, b, a] array. Linear 0-1 channels, stored by the engine as the 8-bit sRGB color: {r: 1, g: 0.7, b: 0.42} reads back as (255, 218, 173). A missing channel reads 0 (alpha 1).

color.description: Color as an {r, g, b, a} object or an [r, g, b, a] array: 0 to 255 channels for debug_shape, 0 to 1 for a light.

componentName.description: Actor form: which Niagara component of the actor takes the values, when it has several (a Blueprint with a fire and a smoke); default its first. A name it lacks is refused with the names it has.

control.description:
Which activate variant to run; omit for 'activate'.
activate: Activate a placed Niagara component, in the level editor or a running game; reset restarts it from age 0.
deactivate: Deactivate a placed Niagara component, in the level editor or a running game.
reset: Restart a placed Niagara component from age 0, in the level editor or a running game.
effect: Activate a Niagara component by actor, or by the system asset it plays (on actorName, else anywhere in the world).

debugOp.description:
Which debug shape variant to run; omit for 'draw'.
draw: Draw a temporary debug shape in the editor viewport (sphere, box, circle, line, point, coordinate, cylinder, cone, capsule, arrow or plane) at location, for duration seconds (default 5). Nothing is spawned or saved, and nothing shows in Play In Editor or a packaged game.
clear: Clear every debug shape drawn in the editor viewport at once, instead of waiting for each to time out.

deltaTime.description: Seconds per step (default 0.1); steps of about a frame (0.02) simulate the way the game does.

deterministicEnabled.description: Whether deterministic GPU simulation is enabled.

direction.description: Direction as [x, y, z] for a cone (default up).

edit.description:
Which edit niagara system variant to run.
add_emitter: Add an emitter to a Niagara system: an emitter asset (emitterPath), or a copy of another system's emitter with its modules, values, renderers and bindings (sourceSystemPath + sourceEmitterName), as the editor's copy and paste does.
add_user_parameter: Add a user parameter to a system.
bind_parameter: Drive a Niagara value from a parameter: a module input named as get_niagara_info lists it (InitializeParticle.Color) is linked to sourceBinding, as the stack's Link Inputs menu does; any other parameterName gets a Set Variables module in particle update that writes it from sourceBinding every frame.
set_parameter_value: Set Niagara parameter values: a user parameter, a module input named as get_niagara_info lists it (InitializeParticle.Lifetime), or a module's static switch (InitializeParticle.Ribbon Width Mode, an enum by its display name such as Direct Set); one with parameterName and parameterValue, or several with parameters, written together and saved once.
set_parameter: Set a Niagara user parameter: on a placed effect's component (actorName), so one placement of a shared system gets its own values, or its default on the system asset (assetPath).
set_dynamic_input: Configure a Niagara dynamic input expression.
set_emitter_properties: Enable or disable an emitter in a Niagara system (emitterProperties.enabled).
enable_gpu_simulation: Enable GPU simulation on a system.
connect_pins: Connect two Niagara graph pins (fromNode, fromPin, toNode, toPin), or with autoConnect wire the first compatible free pins.

emitter.description: Emitter name; alias normalized to emitterName.

emitterName.description: Emitter within the system, by the name get_niagara_info lists. Module, renderer, data interface, event, parameter and simulation edits also read emitter, and with neither use the system's only emitter (a system with several refuses with EMITTER_NOT_FOUND, listing them); graph edits without one edit the system's own script.

emitterProperties.description: Emitter settings to change: enabled (boolean) turns the emitter on or off; moduleEnabled ({ModuleName: boolean}, names as get_niagara_info lists them) turns stack modules on or off, so a template module that works against the values set (a size curve, wind) can be switched off. Any other key is refused. Module inputs are set with set_parameter_value.

endLocation.description: End point as [x, y, z] for line, arrow and cylinder shapes.

eventName.description: Optional: the name expected; the generator module names its event, and a different one draws a warning.

eventSpawnCount.description: Particles spawned per received event (default 1); the engine uses it only with spawnOnEvent true.

eventType.description: Event generator module: Location (GenerateLocationEvent, the default), Death or Collision; any other name is refused.

filter.description: Label prefix: every actor whose label starts with it is deleted (ignoring case).

fixedBoundsEnabled.description: Whether fixed system bounds are enabled.

forceType.description: Force module: Gravity (default), Drag, Wind, Curl (CurlNoise), Vortex or PointAttraction; any other name is refused.

fromNode.description: Source node: its GUID, name or title.

fromPin.description: Output pin name (or display name) on the source node.

info.description:
Which get niagara info variant to run; omit for 'info'.
info: Read Niagara system metadata.
validate: Validate a Niagara system for errors.

inputName.description: Module input name receiving the dynamic input.

interfaceKind.description:
Which add niagara data interface variant to run.
static_mesh: Add a Static Mesh data interface as a user parameter of the system, User.<parameterName> (default MCP_StaticMeshDataInterface), for modules to sample a static mesh's surface; emitterName must name an emitter of the system. A parameterName the system already has is NAME_TAKEN, nothing changed. Saved unless save is false (saved).
skeletal_mesh: Add a Skeletal Mesh data interface as a user parameter of the system, User.<parameterName> (default MCP_SkeletalMeshDataInterface), for modules to sample a skeletal mesh's bones and surface; emitterName must name an emitter of the system. A parameterName the system already has is NAME_TAKEN, nothing changed. Saved unless save is false (saved).
spline: Add a Spline data interface as a user parameter of the system, User.<parameterName> (default MCP_SplineDataInterface), for modules to sample positions along a spline; emitterName must name an emitter of the system. A parameterName the system already has is NAME_TAKEN, nothing changed. Saved unless save is false (saved).
collision_query: Add a Collision Query data interface as a user parameter of the system, User.<parameterName> (default MCP_CollisionQueryDataInterface), for modules to trace against the world; emitterName must name an emitter of the system. A parameterName the system already has is NAME_TAKEN, nothing changed. Saved unless save is false (saved).
audio_spectrum: Add an Audio Spectrum data interface as a user parameter of the system, User.<parameterName> (default MCP_AudioSpectrumDataInterface), for modules to read the spectrum of playing audio (audio-reactive particles); emitterName must name an emitter of the system. A parameterName the system already has is NAME_TAKEN, nothing changed. Saved unless save is false (saved).

kind.description:
Which create effect variant to run.
niagara_system: Create an empty Niagara System named name in path (or savePath; default /Game), compiled and saved unless save is false: it has its system scripts and no emitter yet, so it draws nothing until add_emitter_to_system adds one. A name already taken is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS, nothing changed. The reply gives systemPath.
niagara_emitter: Create a standalone Niagara Emitter asset named name in path (default /Game) with the engine's default modules and a sprite renderer (UE 5.1 and later), saved unless save is false; add_emitter_to_system puts it in a system. A name already taken is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS, nothing changed.
niagara_ribbon: Create a Niagara ribbon effect: by default the engine LocationBasedRibbon template given its own SpawnRate of 60 a second, Ribbon Width Mode Direct Set and an infinite loop, so it trails whatever it is attached to, placed in the level only when location is given; tune SpawnRate.SpawnRate, InitializeParticle.Lifetime, Ribbon Width and Color with set_parameter_value.
particle_trail: Create a particle trail effect: by default a ribbon (the engine LocationBasedRibbon template given its own SpawnRate of 60 a second, Ribbon Width Mode Direct Set and an infinite loop) that trails whatever it is attached to, placed in the level only when location is given; tune SpawnRate.SpawnRate, InitializeParticle.Lifetime, Ribbon Width and Color with set_parameter_value.
impact: Create an impact effect system asset (the engine OmnidirectionalBurst template by default), placed in the level only when location is given.
environment: Create an environment effect (weather/atmosphere) system asset, placed in the level only when location is given.
volumetric_fog: Create a volumetric fog effect.
niagara: Place a Niagara system in the level as a Niagara actor, at a location or attached to an actor; autoActivate false places it switched off, for a sequence particle track or gameplay to start.
particle: Spawn a particle effect (Cascade or Niagara) from a preset name or a system asset.

lightRadius.description: Multiplier on each particle's light radius (the renderer RadiusScale, engine default 1). Left unchanged when omitted.

lightType.description: Dynamic light type: Point (the default, and what any other value gives), Spot, Directional or Rect, in any case; there is no sky light here.

location.description: World or relative location as [x, y, z].

materialPath.description: Canonical /Game material asset path for the renderer; its Niagara sprite or ribbon usage flag is set and the material saved, so the renderer never falls back to the default material.

meshPath.description: Canonical /Game static mesh for the mesh renderer; its materials get their Niagara mesh-particle usage flag set and saved, so the particles never fall back to the default material.

moduleKind.description:
Which add niagara module variant to run; omit for 'module'.
module: Add a module to a Niagara emitter, where its dependencies hold: before the first module that must run after it (a force before Solve Forces and Velocity), else at the end of the stack.
spawn_rate: Insert the SpawnRate module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
spawn_burst: Insert the SpawnBurst_Instantaneous module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
spawn_per_unit: Insert the SpawnPerUnit module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
initialize_particle: Insert the InitializeParticle module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
velocity: Insert a velocity module into the emitter's particle spawn stack, chosen by velocityMode: Linear (AddVelocity, the default), Cone (AddVelocityInCone) or FromPoint (AddVelocityFromPoint); another mode is INVALID_ARGUMENT. Its inputs keep their defaults; set them with set_parameter_value. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false; the reply gives moduleName.
acceleration: Insert the AccelerationForce module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
force: Insert the force module forceType names (Gravity by default; Drag, Wind, Curl, Vortex, PointAttraction) into the emitter's particle update stack, before Solve Forces and Velocity, with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<moduleName>.<Input>"). Another forceType is INVALID_ARGUMENT. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false; the reply gives moduleName as the stack named it.
color: Insert the Color module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
size: Insert the ScaleSpriteSize module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
collision: Insert the Collision module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
kill_particles: Insert the KillParticles module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
camera_offset: Insert the CameraOffset module with its default inputs; tune them with set_parameter_value (parameterName "<Module>.<Input>").
particle_state: Add a particle-state module.
sprite_renderer: Give the emitter a sprite renderer, or configure the one it has (rendererCreated false), drawing with materialPath (its Niagara sprite usage flag set and saved); without materialPath it keeps its material, the engine default on a new one. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false; the reply reads back materialPath and rendererPath.
mesh_renderer: Give the emitter a mesh renderer, or configure the one it has (rendererCreated false), drawing each particle as meshPath (required; it replaces the renderer's mesh list, and its materials get their Niagara mesh-particle flag). Without meshPath it is INVALID_ARGUMENT, since a mesh renderer with no mesh draws nothing. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false.
ribbon_renderer: Give the emitter a ribbon renderer (a strip joining its particles, for trails), or configure the one it has (rendererCreated false), drawing with materialPath (its Niagara ribbon usage flag set and saved); without it the material stays as it is. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false; the reply reads back materialPath.
light_renderer: Give the emitter a light renderer, a point light at each particle, or configure the one it has (rendererCreated false); lightRadius multiplies each particle's light radius (RadiusScale, engine default 1) and is read back. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false.
simulation_stage: Add an empty generic simulation stage named stageName to the emitter, running over stageIterationSource (Particles, the default, DataInterface or DirectSet on UE 5.2 and later; another name is INVALID_ARGUMENT). Stages run on GPU emitters. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false; the reply gives simulationStageCount.
event_generator: Insert the engine's event generator module for eventType (Location, the default, Death or Collision) into the emitter's particle update stack. The event it emits is named by that module, and the reply gives that name (eventName) for moduleKind=event_receiver on another emitter; an eventName given that differs is not applied and draws a warning. Another eventType is INVALID_ARGUMENT. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false.
event_receiver: Add an event handler to the emitter for the event eventName (the name moduleKind=event_generator reported): with spawnOnEvent true it spawns eventSpawnCount particles (default 1) per event, otherwise its script runs on every particle when the event arrives. Its handler script starts empty. The system recompiles and is saved unless save is false.

moduleName.description: Module (function call) name that owns inputName; alternative to targetNodeId.

moduleNames.description: Only these modules' moduleInputs and staticSwitches (Collision, SpawnRate), any case; a whole system's inputs run to 15 KB.

modulePath.description: Canonical /Niagara module script path to insert.

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

parameterType.description: Niagara parameter type (Float, Vector, Color or LinearColor, ...).

parameters.description: Several values written together and saved once, in place of parameterName and parameterValue: each {parameterName, parameterValue} names a user parameter, a module input or a module's static switch as get_niagara_info lists it (InitializeParticle.Lifetime, InitializeParticle.Ribbon Width Mode), and emitterName and save apply to every entry. With actorName (edit=set_parameter) each entry is a user parameter of that placed effect, in place of parameterName and value. The reply lists every entry (parameterName, applied, error); the call fails PARAMETER_BATCH_INCOMPLETE naming any that did not apply, and the others stay written.

path.description: Canonical /Game output path for the created asset.

preset.description: Particle preset name or canonical /Game particle asset path.

replaceExisting.description: Whether an existing dynamic input is replaced.

reset.description: Restart the effect from age 0 as it activates (default true); false resumes a deactivated one where it stopped.

rotation.description: Rotation as [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees.

save.description: Persist the asset to disk (default true); false leaves the change in memory only.

savePath.description: Canonical /Game directory for the created asset.

scale.description: Scale of the spawned system: one uniform number, or [x, y, z] (an {x, y, z} object is accepted). Default 1.

scriptType.description: Which script the graph edit works in: Spawn (default) or Update. With emitterName that is the particle spawn or particle update stack of that emitter; without it, the system spawn or update script.

shape.description: The shape, as shapeType names it; read when shapeType is absent or sphere.

shapeType.description: The shape to draw: sphere, box, circle, line, point, coordinate, cylinder, cone, capsule, arrow or plane, in any case (default sphere; another name is refused).

sourceBinding.description: The parameter to read: a user parameter of the same type (User.Tint) or an engine, system or emitter one (Emitter.Age).

sourceEmitterName.description: The emitter of sourceSystemPath to copy, by the name get_niagara_info lists.

sourceSystemPath.description: Niagara system to copy sourceEmitterName from, in place of emitterPath. The user parameters the emitter reads come along with their values when this system lacks them. An emitter that inherits from an emitter asset is refused (EMITTER_INHERITS): add that asset with emitterPath.

spawnOnEvent.description: Whether the receiver spawns particles on each event.

stageIterationSource.description: What the stage runs over: Particles (the default, each particle), DataInterface (each element of a grid or other data interface) or DirectSet (a count you set; UE 5.2 and later). Any other name is refused.

steps.description: Steps to run (default 1): the system ages steps x deltaTime seconds.

system.description: Niagara system path; alias normalized to systemPath.

systemName.description: Runtime Niagara system/component name on the target actor.

targetNodeId.description: Niagara graph node the dynamic input is attached to.

templateEmitterPath.description: Niagara emitter asset the authored system starts from; defaults to the engine template for the effect kind. Ignored when systemPath names an existing system.

thickness.description: Line thickness of the debug shape (default 2).

toNode.description: Destination node: its GUID, name or title.

toPin.description: Input pin name (or display name) on the destination node.

velocityMode.description: Velocity module: Linear (AddVelocity, the default), Cone (AddVelocityInCone) or FromPoint (AddVelocityFromPoint); any other name is refused.

tools.name: manage_gas
tools.description: Create Gameplay Abilities, Effects, Attribute Sets, and Gameplay Cues for ability systems.

abilityClass.description: GameplayAbility class path; accepted wherever abilityPath is.

abilityTags.description: Gameplay tags granted to this ability.

activationBlockedTags.description: Tags that block activation of this ability.

activationPolicy.description: Net execution policy: where the ability activates.

activationRequiredTags.description: Tags required to activate this ability.

applicationRequiredTags.description: Tags required to apply this effect.

baseValue.description: New base and current value of the attribute (required; an omitted one used to write 0).

blockAbilitiesWithTag.description: Tags of abilities blocked while this is active.

calculationClass.description: The GameplayEffectExecutionCalculation class: a Blueprint path (/Game/X/GEC, as create_execution_calculation returns, or /Game/X/GEC.GEC_C) or a native /Script/Module.Class.

cancelAbilitiesWithTag.description: Tags of abilities cancelled when this activates.

componentName.description: Ability System Component name. Adding: the new component (default AbilitySystemComponent). Configuring: which one (default the Blueprint's own).

cooldownEffectPath.description: Canonical /Game path to the cooldown Gameplay Effect.

costEffectPath.description: Canonical /Game path to the cost Gameplay Effect.

cueType.description: Static or Actor, in any case (default Static; any other value makes a Static one).

defaultValue.description: Starting base and current value of the new attribute (default 0).

duration.description: Duration in seconds for a HasDuration effect (ignored for Instant).

grantedTags.description: Tags granted while the effect is active.

immunityTags.description: Tags that make a target immune to this effect.

kind.description:
Which create gas asset variant to run.
gameplay_ability: Create a Gameplay Ability asset.
gameplay_effect: Create a Gameplay Effect Blueprint (name, in path) with its duration policy: durationType Instant (the default without duration), HasDuration (the default with duration, in seconds) or Infinite; period in seconds makes a non-Instant effect tick. An effect already at that path is left as it is (reusedExisting; set_effect_duration changes it). Saved.
attribute_set: Create an AttributeSet class/asset.
gameplay_cue_notify: Create a Gameplay Cue Notify Blueprint: Static (GameplayCueNotify_Static, nothing spawned, for one-shot cues) or Actor (GameplayCueNotify_Actor, spawned and kept while the cue is active, for looping ones), with cueTag set as its GameplayCueTag.
execution_calculation: Create a GameplayEffectExecutionCalculation blueprint for custom effect math.

magnitudeCalculationType.description: How the magnitude is given: ScalableFloat (a fixed value, the default) or SetByCaller (supplied by the effect spec under setByCallerTag).

modifierIndex.description: Zero-based index of the modifier to edit.

modifierOperation.description: Modifier operation applied to the attribute.

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

path.description: Canonical /Game output path for the created asset.

period.description: Period in seconds for a periodic non-Instant effect.

removalTags.description: Tags that cause this effect to be removed.

replicationMode.description: How gameplay effects replicate: Full (every effect to every client, for single player), Mixed (effects to the owning client only, cues and tags to all, for player characters) or Minimal (cues and tags only, for AI).

setByCallerTag.description: Gameplay tag keying a SetByCaller magnitude.

setting.description:
Which configure ability variant to run.
tags: Add gameplay tags to an ability Blueprint: abilityTags (its own asset tags), cancelAbilitiesWithTag and blockAbilitiesWithTag (abilities it cancels or blocks while active), activationRequiredTags and activationBlockedTags (tags its owner must have, or must not have, to activate). Tags are added, never replaced; each must be registered in the project (GAMEPLAY_TAG_NOT_REGISTERED before anything changes) and is read back from the compiled class before the ability is saved (ABILITY_TAGS_NOT_APPLIED otherwise).
cooldown: Set the Gameplay Effect an ability applies as its cooldown when it commits (cooldownEffectPath: a HasDuration GameplayEffect that grants a cooldown tag; the ability cannot activate again while its owner has that tag). Read back from the compiled class, then saved; the reply names the class it holds (cooldownEffectClass). An effect that does not load is ASSET_NOT_FOUND.
costs: Set the Gameplay Effect an ability applies as its cost when it commits (costEffectPath: a GameplayEffect Blueprint, usually Instant with a negative modifier on the spent attribute; the ability cannot activate while its owner cannot pay). Read back from the compiled class, then saved; the reply names the class it holds (costEffectClass). An effect that does not load is ASSET_NOT_FOUND.
activation_policy: Set where an ability activates: its net execution policy, LocalPredicted (the default: the client runs it at once and the server confirms), LocalOnly, ServerOnly or ServerInitiated. Another name is refused; the policy is read back from the compiled class, then saved.
instancing_policy: Set how an ability is instanced: InstancedPerActor (the default: one instance per actor, keeping its state between activations), InstancedPerExecution (a fresh instance each activation) or NonInstanced (runs on the class default object with no state; deprecated in newer engines). Another name is refused; read back from the compiled class, then saved (the reply gives instancingPolicy).
add_to_set: Add an ability class (abilityPath, a Blueprint, or abilityClass) to an existing ability set (setPath: a DataAsset, or DataAsset Blueprint, with an array of ability classes); one already there is reported (alreadyPresent), not doubled. Saved; a set that cannot be written is SAVE_FAILED, and a set with no array that takes the class is PROPERTY_NOT_FOUND, listing its arrays.

stackExpirationPolicy.description: What happens when a stack expires.

targetAttribute.description: Target attribute captured by the modifier.

tools.name: manage_geometry
tools.description: Create procedural meshes using Geometry Script: booleans, deformers, UVs, collision, and LOD generation. Each edit of a placed dynamic mesh is one undo step.

angle.description: Degrees to turn the profile about local Z, 1 to 360 (default 360), starting on local +X and turning toward +Y; less leaves an open wedge whose two cut faces are not closed.

aoDistance.description: How far an occluder can be, in cm (default 15% of the bounds diagonal); nearer geometry darkens R, farther geometry is ignored.

aoRays.description: Hemisphere rays per vertex for occlusion (default 32, clamped to 8-256); the bake cuts them on a very dense mesh to keep the call short, and the reply says how many it used.

arrayMode.description:
Which array mesh variant to run.
linear: Repeat a dynamic mesh in a row inside the same mesh: count copies in all, each one offset further from the last. The reply gives the triangleCount after the copies.
radial: Repeat a dynamic mesh round its local Z axis inside the same mesh: count copies in all, angle / count apart. The reply gives the triangleCount after the copies.

axis.description: Axis to deform along: X, Y or Z (default Z).

baseRadius.description: Cone base radius; defaults to radius.

blurIterations.description: Neighbour-averaging passes over R, G and B (default 1, 0 to 16); 0 keeps the masks per vertex and noisy.

booleanOp.description:
Which boolean mesh variant to run.
union: Union of two placed dynamic mesh actors: toolActor's volume joins targetActor's mesh, in place and in world space. keepTool (default true) keeps the tool actor, false deletes it once the union worked; a union that leaves nothing is EMPTY_RESULT with the target unchanged.
subtract: Cut toolActor's volume out of targetActor's dynamic mesh, in place and in world space (a hole, a doorway). A tool that does not cross the target's surface is NO_EFFECT and one that empties it EMPTY_RESULT, both leaving the target as it was and the tool in place to move; keepTool (default true) false deletes the tool once the cut worked.
intersection: Keep only where two placed dynamic mesh actors overlap: targetActor's mesh becomes the shared volume, in place and in world space. Meshes that do not overlap are EMPTY_RESULT with the target unchanged; keepTool (default true) false deletes toolActor once it worked.
trim: Trim a dynamic mesh actor by another one, trimActorName, kept in place: keepInside false (default) cuts away what lies inside it, true keeps only that part. Refused like a subtract or intersection when nothing would change or nothing would be left.
self_union: Resolve a dynamic mesh that overlaps itself (after an append or array): the overlapping shells are unioned into one surface, holes filled and flaps trimmed; trianglesBefore and trianglesAfter come back.

min.description: Corner with the smallest x, y and z, in the mesh's local space.

max.description: Corner with the largest x, y and z; larger than min on every axis.

materialId.description: Material id of every face of the box and its copies (default 0); a baked asset gets one slot per id.

materialIds.description: Material ids the copies take in turn (copy k takes entry k modulo the list length), counted along count, then rows, then layers: colour variety across a stack or a row. Replaces materialId.

open.description: Faces to leave out, by the direction they face: a face nobody sees (the bottom of a post on a floor, the faces two touching boxes share) costs triangles and can flicker.

count.description: Copies along offset, the box itself included (default 1).

offset.description: Step from one copy to the next, e.g. {x: 200} for one every 2 m.

rowOffset.description: Step from one row to the next.

layers.description: Layers of those rows (default 1), e.g. the tiers of a stack.

layerOffset.description: Step from one layer to the next.

repeat.description: Lay the box out count x rows x layers times, each copy moved by offset per step, rowOffset per row and layerOffset per layer. A step larger than the box leaves a gap between copies.

boxes.description: Boxes to append, at most 2500 once repeats are unrolled: each an axis-aligned box from min to max, its six faces wound outward and each face its own polygroup.

by.description: parts (default): one mesh per separate object, where connected pieces whose bounds touch or come within gap cm are one object (a crate's planks stay one crate); material: one per material slot.

cap.description: Close open ends: the tube ends of a loft, sweep or extrude along a spline, or for a revolve flat discs from the first and last profile points to the axis (revolve default true).

capMaterialId.description: Material id of the end caps and tip fans (default 0).

caps.description: Close a closed tube's first and last sections with a flat face each (default true), unless startPoint or endPoint closes that end.

oneOf.description: A point on the mirror plane in the mesh's local space, cm (default 0,0,0).
Ring: a point on the turning axis in the mesh's local space, cm (default 0,0,0); the copies turn about the mesh's local Z through it.

center.description: A point on the mirror plane in the mesh's local space, cm (default 0,0,0).

closed.description: Each section is a closed loop and the loft a closed tube (default true). false joins open polylines into a sheet (an awning, a curved panel), its faces turned by the order of the points; flip reverses them.

collision.description: Collision for the baked asset: box (default) is one box the size of the bounds, which pawns can stand on (on a converted-over asset too); complex uses the render triangles as simple collision too, exact but costly; none gives the asset no collision at all.

collisionOp.description:
Which configure mesh collision variant to run.
generate: Generate simple collision for a dynamic mesh.
generate_complex: Generate complex (convex decomposition) collision.
simplify: Simplify an existing collision hull.

count.description: Copies in all, the original included (1 to 100): count 3 is the original and two copies.
