Custom playback range end frame, EXCLUSIVE: must be strictly greater than startFrame. 0..1 renders exactly one frame; 0..0 renders nothing and is refused as INVALID_FRAME_RANGE.
New end of the section in display-rate frames, after its start.

endFrame.description: Custom playback range end frame, EXCLUSIVE: must be strictly greater than startFrame. 0..1 renders exactly one frame; 0..0 renders nothing and is refused as INVALID_FRAME_RANGE.

filePath.description: A local media file under the project's Content or Saved folder: an absolute path there, or Content/... or Saved/... (/Saved/... too). It must exist; file:// URLs, traversal and links are refused.

filePaths.description: Media file paths appended to the playlist.

oneOf.description: Focal length in mm.

Focal length in mm for a cine camera (default by shotSize: close 85, medium 50, wide 24; two subjects 35), kept within what its lens allows. A plain camera actor has no lens: its own field of view is used and focalLength is refused.

focalLength.description: Focal length in mm for a cine camera (default by shotSize: close 85, medium 50, wide 24; two subjects 35), kept within what its lens allows. A plain camera actor has no lens: its own field of view is used and focalLength is refused.

focusDistance.description: Manual focus distance alias in centimetres.

frameRate.description: Frame rate as fps or a rate string such as 24fps or 24000/1001.

frames.description: Remove the keys on each of these frames in one call, of every key type (transform, float, Visibility, particle). Without frame and frames every key on the track goes.

x.description: Left edge -1, centre 0, right edge 1; the third lines are at -0.333 and 0.333.

framing.description: Where each subject's centre should sit on screen, one {x, y} per subject in the order of subjects (default: one subject at {x: -0.333, y: 0}, two at {x: -0.333, y: 0} and {x: 0.333, y: 0}). Two subjects need points apart from each other.

gameModeOverride.description: The game mode the render plays. Unset, MRQ uses its cinematic game mode, which spawns no player pawn and no HUD: right for a cinematic, empty for gameplay. "level" plays the level's own game mode (its pawn, HUD and rules); a class path (/Game/X/BP_Mode or /Script/Module.Class) plays that one.

height.description: Output height in pixels (positive; paired with width).

includeTranslucentObjects.description: Whether the pass includes translucent objects.

info.description:
Which get properties variant to run; omit for 'properties'.
properties: Read the playback properties of a Level Sequence: frameRate (the display rate, a number), playbackStart and playbackEnd in display-rate frames, and lengthInFrames. An asset that is not a Level Sequence is INVALID_SEQUENCE.
bindings: List all bindings (possessables and spawnables) in a Level Sequence.
tracks: List every track of a Level Sequence: the sequence-wide tracks (the camera cut track included) and each binding's tracks. Each row gives trackName (the object name track actions take), trackType (its class), displayName (the label Sequencer shows, also accepted), isMasterTrack, for a bound track bindingName (Actor/Component for a component) and bindingGuid, sectionCount, muted (set_track_muted or solo turned it off), the animation clips a skeletal animation track plays (animations) and isCameraCut. Read only.
keys: Read the sections and keyframes already on a sequence track.
track_types: List all available MovieScene track types registered in the engine.
list: List Level Sequence assets under a content folder (recursively; the whole Game folder when path is omitted).
open: Open a Level Sequence (path) in the Sequencer editor; nothing in it changes. The reply gives sequencePath. A path that is not a Level Sequence is SEQUENCE_NOT_FOUND, and an editor that does not open EDITOR_NOT_OPEN.

interpolation.description: How the curve leaves this key: auto (default) a smooth curve through the keys, linear a steady rate to the next key (a bullet, a constant pan), constant a hold that jumps at the next key.

key.description: Metadata key to look up; the reply then carries found and value.

value.description: Key value, in the form value takes.

interpolation.description: How the curve leaves this key; default the interpolation of the call.

keys.description: Several keys on this property in one call, in place of frame and value: a whole curve, or a flash shown on one frame and hidden on the next. Each entry is {frame, value, interpolation}; they are written in order, so lookAt keys turn the short way from the entry before. Every frame is checked before any key is written.

kind.description:
Which create cinematic asset variant to run.
cine_camera_actor: Create a CineCameraActor in the level and bind it to the sequence.
master_sequence: Create the master level sequence of a cinematic: an empty sequence at frameRate (default 24 fps) with its playback range, saved; shots and sub-sequences are added to it afterwards.

label.description: Actor label alias for the camera or rig actor (alias of actorName).

lengthInFrames.description: Playback length in display-rate frames, counted from playbackStart (or the current start); playbackEnd wins when both are sent.

levelNames.description: Level names toggled by the visibility track.

loadDefaultMapOnStop.description: Whether to load the default map on stop.

lookAt.description: An actor the camera faces the whole way (the middle of what it draws); left out, the camera faces the way it is going.

loopMode.description: Sequencer loop mode for the preview: once or loop.

looping.description: Whether media playback loops (alias of loop).

manualFocusDistance.description: Manual focus distance in centimetres (read before focusDistance).

materialIndex.description: Material slot index on the component.

materialPath.description: Material asset path for a material render pass.

maxShotSeconds.description: Longest shot, in seconds (default 8; at least minShotSeconds).

minShotSeconds.description: Shortest shot, in seconds (default 1.5; at least segmentSeconds).

name.description: Name for the new sequence or asset.

newName.description: New name for the sequence asset.

onlyJob.description: Whether to queue only this job.

overscanPercentage.description: Extra image rendered past the frame edges, as a fraction of the frame (0.1 is 10%); it also turns the setting's overscan override on where the engine has one.

particleKey.description: The key at startFrame: trigger fires the system once, the key for a one-shot burst; activate keeps it running, so a one-shot that finishes starts again until the section ends; deactivate stops it. Default from activate.

path.description: Canonical /Game path of the master sequence that owns the shot track.

platformSources.description: Per-platform media source asset paths keyed by platform name.

playOnOpen.description: Whether the media player plays on open (alias of autoPlay).

playRate.description: The speed of an animation section (2 is twice as fast). Without endFrame the section keeps playing the same frames, so it gets shorter or longer by the same factor, as in Sequencer.

playlistIndex.description: Zero-based index into the media playlist.

precacheFile.description: Whether the file media source precaches on open.

prioritizeActors.description: Whether to prioritize actor replication during recording.

property.description: Property to animate, by name (Transform, Intensity...); required, or send it as propertyName (refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT when neither is sent).

propertyName.description: Property name to animate (alias of property).

propertyType.description: Property value type hint (alias of type).

recordInto.description: Record into the sequence named by sequencePath instead of a new take based on it (default false).

recordParentHierarchy.description: Also record the actors the source actor is attached under, so its motion keeps its parents.

recordType.description: How an actor source records the actor: possessable (onto the actor in the level), spawnable (the take spawns its own copy) or projectDefault (the Take Recorder project setting). Anything else is INVALID_ARGUMENT.

recordingSequencePath.description: Level Sequence the take is set up from: recorded as a new take based on it, or into it with recordInto true; the same as sequencePath. One that is not a Level Sequence is INVALID_SEQUENCE.

renderAllCameras.description: Render every camera of the sequence instead of the camera cut; refused with NOT_SUPPORTED_ON_ENGINE where the engine has no such option.

renderJobName.description: Render job name: names a new job, or selects an existing job (alternative to jobId).

renderPass.description: Render pass identifier: beauty (final, lit), depth, motion_vector, normal, object_id, custom_stencil (with materialPath), or ui (the game viewport's UMG layer: HUD and menus; widget and ui_renderer also work).

items.description: Render pass identifier, as renderPass takes.

renderTimeoutMs.description: How long the render may run before it is cancelled, in milliseconds (default 300000). More than the plugin setting MaxMovieRenderTimeoutMs (3600000, one hour, by default) is refused with RESOURCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. options.timeoutMs is the gateway deadline for the call and never reaches the render.

replayName.description: Default replay name for recordings that do not name one.

resolution.description: Output resolution in WIDTHxHEIGHT format, such as 1920x1080.

rotation.description: Camera rotation as {pitch, yaw, roll} (x/y/z are accepted as aliases).

rowIndex.description: Sequencer row index for the created section.

save.description: Whether to save the sequence asset after the mutation.

oneOf.description: Seek time in seconds (alias of timeSeconds).
How long the flight takes (0.5-600; default its length at 300 cm a second, at least 1).

seconds.description: How long the flight takes (0.5-600; default its length at 300 cm a second, at least 1).

oneOf.description: Index of the shot section to configure.
Which section of the track, in the order info=keys lists them (default 0).

sectionIndex.description: Index of the shot section to configure.

sectionName.description: Shot section display name to configure (alternative to sectionIndex).

segmentSeconds.description: How finely the range is judged, in seconds (default 0.5): cuts fall on these steps.

sequenceOp.description:
Which create variant to run; omit for 'create'.
create: Create a Level Sequence asset and save it: name in the folder path names (default /Game), or path alone naming the sequence itself (/Game/Cinematics/SEQ_Shot). A Level Sequence already there is kept and answered with alreadyExists true; another asset there is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS, and a path outside the writable content roots SEQUENCE_PATH_NOT_WRITABLE. The new sequence is empty, with no bindings or camera, at the project's default display rate (30 fps out of the box) and 24000 ticks per second.
duplicate: Copy a Level Sequence to destinationPath (a folder; one not starting with / is under the source folder) as newName, and save the copy. A destination already taken is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS, a source that is not a Level Sequence INVALID_SEQUENCE, a destination outside the writable content roots SEQUENCE_PATH_NOT_WRITABLE. The reply gives duplicatedPath and saved; the copy keeps the original's bindings, which still point at the same level actors.
rename: Rename a Level Sequence: newName keeps its folder, a path starting with / moves it there. The engine saves the renamed sequence and leaves a redirector at the old path when other assets reference it. A name already taken is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS, a source that is not a Level Sequence INVALID_SEQUENCE, a path outside the writable content roots SEQUENCE_PATH_NOT_WRITABLE. The reply gives oldPath and sequencePath.

sequenceProperty.description:
Which set properties variant to run; omit for 'properties'.
properties: Set the display frame rate of a Level Sequence (frameRate, such as 24 or 29.97) and its playback range in display-rate frames: playbackStart, and playbackEnd or lengthInFrames (end = start + length; playbackEnd wins). Send at least one; one undo step, and the sequence is left unsaved. The reply reads the values back; a negative frame or an unreadable rate is INVALID_ARGUMENT, another asset type INVALID_SEQUENCE.
display_rate: Set the display frame rate of a Level Sequence (frameRate: 24, 29.97, "30fps", "30000/1001"), the rate its timeline counts frames in; keys stay at the same times. An unreadable rate is INVALID_ARGUMENT; the reply reads the rate back. One undo step; the sequence is left unsaved.
tick_resolution: Set the tick resolution of a Level Sequence, the time grid keys and sections are stored on (resolution: whole ticks per second such as 24000, the default, or 60000; a ratio N/D is N ticks every D seconds), moving every key, section and range onto the new grid as the Sequencer does so nothing shifts in time. Anything else, zero included, is INVALID_ARGUMENT, and so is a resolution coarser than the display rate, which could not hold every frame. The reply gives tickResolution and previousTickResolution, and warns when the display rate does not fall on whole ticks. One undo step; the sequence is left unsaved.
playback_speed: Set the play rate of a Level Sequence (speed, above 0; 1 is normal, 0.5 half speed) on every level sequence actor in the editor level that plays it, which is the rate it runs at in game and Play In Editor, and on the Sequencer preview when the sequence is open there (a preview setting that is not saved). The actors change in one undo step and the level is left unsaved. The reply lists the actors (levelSequenceActors) and sequencerUpdated. With neither an actor nor an open Sequencer it is PLAYBACK_TARGET_NOT_FOUND; speed 0 or below is INVALID_ARGUMENT.
view_range: Set the view range of a Level Sequence, the part of the timeline the Sequencer window shows: start and end in seconds, end after start (INVALID_ARGUMENT otherwise). Display only: playback and keys are untouched.
work_range: Set the work range of a Level Sequence, the stretch of timeline the Sequencer shows and edits within: start and end in seconds, end after start (INVALID_ARGUMENT otherwise). An end past the playback range extends playback to it (playbackExtended), so keys out there play; the reply gives the range in seconds and in display-rate frames.

setting.description:
Which configure cinematic variant to run.
camera: Set the lens of a CineCameraActor (actorName): currentFocalLength or focalLength (mm), currentAperture or aperture (f-stop), sensorWidth and sensorHeight (mm), manualFocusDistance or focusDistance (cm), each also accepted inside a lens, filmback or focus object. The camera clamps them to its lens limits and the reply reads back what it kept (values). One undo step; a call with nothing to set, or an actor with no CineCameraComponent, is refused.
rig_crane: Set cranePitch and craneYaw (degrees) and craneArmLength (cm) on a CameraRig_Crane named actorName, placing one at the world origin when actorName names none (spawned true). One undo step; a call with no setting is refused, and an actor of another class is RIG_CLASS_MISMATCH.
rig_rail: Set positionOnRail (0 to 1, where the camera mount sits along the rail spline) on a CameraRig_Rail named actorName, placing one at the world origin when actorName names none (spawned true). One undo step; a call with no setting is refused, and an actor of another class is RIG_CLASS_MISMATCH.
shot: Configure shot settings (display name, range) for a cinematic shot.

oneOf.description: Nested MRQ settings.

spatialSampleCount.description: Spatial sample count per render sample pass.

temporalSampleCount.description: Temporal sample count per render sample pass.

antiAliasingMethod.description: Anti-aliasing method name, such as TSAA or FXAA.

oneOf.description: Nested output settings.

shotName.description: Name for the new sequence or asset.

shotSize.description: One subject: how much of the frame its box spans, the larger of its height share and its width share (close 90%, medium 55%, the default, wide 25%); it also picks the default focal length. Two subjects are sized by their framing points, so it only picks the lens.

shutterTiming.description: When the shutter opens: FrameOpen at the frame (no blur reaching back across a cut), FrameCenter (the default) half a frame before it, FrameClose a whole frame before it.

soundPath.description: Audio track only: /Game path of the SoundWave, SoundCue or MetaSound the section plays. Without end the section is as long as the sound (one second for a looping one).

sourceClasses.description: Take Recorder source classes to add besides actors, each listed in the plugin setting TakeRecorderSourceClassAllowlist (by default /Script/TakeRecorderSources.TakeRecorderCameraCutSource and TakeRecorderLevelVisibilitySource); another class is INVALID_SOURCE_CLASS.

sourcePaths.description: Media source asset paths for the playlist.

sourceType.description: Media source type: file or platform (network streams are refused).

spatialSampleCount.description: Sample count per render sample pass.

spawnable.description: Add a spawnable camera owned by the sequence instead of placing a camera actor in the level (default false).

startFrame.description: Custom playback range start frame (paired with endFrame).

startTime.description: Sequence time in seconds. play starts there; pause jumps the playhead there and holds that frame, so the viewport and screenshots show the scene at that moment. A time past the end of the playback range is refused: frame N at 24 fps is N / 24 seconds.

oneOf.description: The one or two actors to frame, by exact name. Each is framed by the box of what it draws: its centre goes to its framing point, and its size sets the distance.
The actors the cut serves (1-4), most important first: the first must be seen at every moment (NO_CUT otherwise), and the line between the first two is the one cuts should not cross.

subjects.description: The actors the cut serves (1-4), most important first: the first must be seen at every moment (NO_CUT otherwise), and the line between the first two is the one cuts should not cross.

takePresetPath.description: Take Preset whose template sequence seeds a new take; cannot be combined with a sequence path or recordInto (INVALID_ARGUMENT), and one that does not load is TAKE_PRESET_NOT_FOUND.

takeSequencePath.description: Level Sequence the take is set up from, the same as sequencePath.

targetActor.description: Actor receiving the media sound component (alias of actorName).

temporalSampleCount.description: Sample count per render sample pass.

through.description: The points the camera passes, in order, in cm (2-16). Each must stand at least clearanceCm from geometry (a point beside a wall or near the floor is POINT_IN_SOLID).

time.description: Seek time in seconds (alias of timeSeconds).

trackKind.description:
Which add cinematic track variant to run.
camera_cut: Add a camera cut track to a cinematic sequence.
camera_shake: Add a camera shake track to a cinematic sequence.
transform: Add a transform track to animate actor transforms during cinematic.
property: Add a property track to animate a specific property on a bound actor.
skeletal_animation: Add a skeletal animation track to play animations on a skeletal mesh. A clip whose skeleton the mesh cannot play is refused with SKELETON_MISMATCH instead of silently showing the rest pose. Overlap the clips before and after it and give easeInFrames/easeOutFrames to crossfade between them instead of cutting in one frame.
material_parameter: Add a material parameter collection track to animate material parameters.
particle: Add a particle track to trigger particle systems during cinematic: trigger fires a one-shot burst (a hit, a spark) once, activate keeps a system running for the section.
event: Add an event track to trigger events at specific frames.
fade: Add a fade track for cinematic fade-in/fade-out transitions.
level_visibility: Add a level visibility track to control level streaming during cinematic.
shot: Add a cinematic shot track to a master sequence.
subsequence: Add a sub-sequence to a master sequence shot track.

trackName.description: Display name for the new track; track actions find it by this name. A track type that takes no name keeps its own, which the reply reads back.

trackType.description: Track type: "Audio" (music or sound, then add_section with soundPath), "Transform", or a MovieScene track class name such as MovieSceneEventTrack.

tracks.description: Recorded properties to turn on or off, by the names the actor source lists (such as Transform), matched without case.

useCurrentLevel.description: Whether to render against the currently loaded level.

oneOf.description: Key value at startFrame: a number for a scalar parameter, or an {r, g, b, a} object for a color parameter.

Keyframe value. For property "Transform" pass a composed object with any subset of {location:{x,y,z}, rotation:{pitch,yaw,roll}, scale:{x,y,z}}; each component supplied must carry all of its finite axes; a new Transform track starts from the current transform of the actor, so the parts a key leaves out keep their values. Add lookAt:{x,y,z} beside location to aim the key at that point (a camera at its subject): pitch and yaw are worked out, roll comes from rotation.roll or 0, and the yaw turns the short way from the key before, so an orbit of aimed keys never spins round. For "Location"/"Rotation"/"Scale" pass that component object alone. Visibility takes true or false; other properties take their own scalar value, so no type is declared here.
Value written under key.

value.description: Key value at startFrame: a number for a scalar parameter, or an {r, g, b, a} object for a color parameter.

visibility.description: Level visibility state: Visible or Hidden.

width.description: Output width in pixels (positive; paired with height).

tools.name: manage_tools
tools.description: Dynamic MCP tool management. List canonical tools, view category counts, and enable/disable tools or categories at runtime.

taskId.description: The task.taskId the still-running answer gave. Only the last 32 such calls of this server or editor session are kept.

tools.description: Tool names to enable or disable.

tools.name: system_control
tools.description: Control the project runtime: profiling, benchmarks, scalability/LOD/Nanite settings, CVars, console commands, Python scripts, UBT, tests, logs, and widgets.

actors.description: Labels of the actors to merge, at least 2; every one must be in the level.

archiveDirectory.description: Archive directory package_project wrote (default <Project>/Packaged). Must be inside the project.

args.description: Each parameter's value by name: a number, text, true/false, a list or an object.

build.description: Compile the game target first (default true).

category.description: A section by friendly name instead of section: general, maps, packaging, rendering, input, physics, collision, audio, engine, navigation.

categoryName.description: A registered category name, case ignored (letters, digits, underscore, hyphen only).

cellSize.description: Cell size of the first runtime grid, in cm.

channels.description: Trace channels (validated: letters, digits, underscore, comma, space, hyphen).

classLocation.description: public (default): header in Public, .cpp in Private; private: both in Private. A module without those folders takes both files in its own folder.

className.description: The class name without its prefix: MyActor makes AMyActor (an Actor parent), MyThing makes UMyThing (an Object parent). Letters, digits and _.

code.description: Python code to execute inline (1 MB max).

command.description: Alternate CVar name field (parsed as name + value).

connectionType.description: Trace connection type; network is restricted to loopback.

control.description:
Which profile performance variant to run.
start: Start recording every stat group to a .uestats file under Saved/Profiling (stat startfile), for Unreal Insights or the Session Frontend to open; no MCP action reads it. duration stops it by itself after that many seconds, else it runs until control=stop. To find what makes a frame slow, inspect get_stats with stats frame answers directly.
stop: Stop the stats file capture control=start began (stat stopfile); the file stays under Saved/Profiling.
benchmark: Measure the editor as it runs now, over duration seconds (default 10), sampling every frame: frames, averageFps, and with type cpu or all (the default) averageFrameMs, worstFrameMs, bestFrameMs, gameThreadMs and renderThreadMs, with gpu or all gpuMs. A minimized or unfocused editor is throttled and measures slow: focus it, or run during Play to measure the game. A call longer than the client allows answers as a task to poll.
memory_report: Generate an engine memory report, optionally detailed.
show_stats: Show or hide a stat HUD overlay (e.g. Unit, GPU) in the active editor viewport; the call sets the state rather than toggling it.

dataValidation.description: Also run Data Validation on every asset that loads (default false): an asset row gains dataValidation (valid, invalid or notValidated, the last when no validator checks that kind of asset) with its errors and warnings, a folder row the count of each verdict and issues (up to 20 assets with errors or warnings). An invalid asset makes its row invalid.

oneOf.description: As run_script: milliseconds after which no further call starts; default 20000.
Milliseconds after which no further call starts; default 20000, at most 25000 (a client gives up on a call at 30 s). Past it the script stops (SCRIPT_DEADLINE) and rolls back.

deadlineMs.description: As run_script: milliseconds after which no further call starts; default 20000.

deleteSlot.description: true deletes the slot instead; properties are then ignored.

oneOf.description: The capabilities the script calls that ask for consent, by id or alias (control_actor.delete, asset.delete); this run's one elevated consent covers exactly these.
The destructive capabilities the script calls, as run_script takes them.

destructive.description: The capabilities the script calls that ask for consent, by id or alias (control_actor.delete, asset.delete); this run's one elevated consent covers exactly these.

duration.description: Seconds after which the capture stops by itself (default: runs until stop_profiling).

enableBatching.description: Same as enabled; enabled wins when both are given.

enableInstancing.description: Dynamic instancing of compatible draws (r.MeshDrawCommands.DynamicInstancing), default true.

enabledOnly.description: Return only plugins currently enabled for this project.

executableName.description: Name the packaged game takes instead of the project name (no .exe): the Win64 launcher becomes <name>.exe, and the game binaries and an Android package are named after it too. It is the game target built; a project with C++ code gets one of that name (Source/<name>.Target.cs, a copy of its own game target) when it has none. Letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.

extension.description: Only files with this extension, e.g. png or json (a leading dot is ignored, case-insensitive).

file.description: Path to a .py file to execute.

filename.description: File name of the PNG (.png is added; a folder part is dropped). Default Screenshot_<unix time>.

filter.description: Case-insensitive plain text (not a regex) a line must contain; separate alternatives with | to match any of them (LoadMap|Bringing World).

forceLOD.description: LOD index every static mesh draws (0 is the most detailed); -1 returns to distance-based LOD.

forceRecompile.description: Recompile every shader, overriding mode (default false); slow on a large project.

hardwareRayTracing.description: Support hardware ray tracing (applies after an editor restart).

includeMetadata.description: true: echo metadata back in the reply (default false).

info.description:
Which get trace status variant to run; omit for 'status'.
status: Query the current trace session status.
analyze: Read a captured trace file's metadata: whether it exists, its size, extension, .utrace flag and modified time.

jobId.description: The jobId package_project or launch_build returned. Omit to list the jobIds this editor session knows.

keepFile.description: false: hand the image back without leaving a file in Saved/Screenshots (refused with returnBase64 false, which would leave no output at all). Default true. Files already written are listed by list_output_files and removed by delete_output_file.

kind.description:
Which run build variant to run.
tests: Run automation tests in the editor, one after another, and answer with each one's result: passed or not, its duration, and the errors and warnings it reported.
ubt: Run UnrealBuildTool for a target/platform/configuration, spawning UBT locally with a manage_pipeline bridge fallback.

launchViewer.description: Open the Unreal Insights application on the trace: default true for control=launch_viewer (start_unreal_insights), false for the other variants.

limit.description: How many files to return (default 100, max 500).

lines.description: How many of the newest matching lines to return, oldest first (default 100, max 1000).

lodBias.description: Texture mip bias, -15 to 15 (r.MipMapLODBias); positive is blurrier, 0 the default.

map.description: Level to open in place of the game's default map: a path (/Game/Maps/L_Main) or a name (L_Main). It must be one of the packaged maps; package_status warns when the game never loaded it.

maps.description: Maps to cook. Pass these when a map is reached by NAME at runtime (OpenLevel) rather than by reference, or the cooker will not find it.

materialUsage.description: Also list the material usage flags the assets' meshes need and their materials lack (default false): a Nanite static mesh's slots, a skeletal mesh's, and a Blueprint's mesh components (Nanite, instanced, spline or skeletal), as materialUsage [{material, usage, property, unsaved, component, asset}] (a folder: at most 40, with materialUsageCount). The editor sets such a flag only while it draws the mesh outside play, so a mesh that only appears in play draws the default material there and in a cooked game; set property true on the material (inspect set_property) to fix one. unsaved true: the editor set the flag (drawing a preview or loading a mesh sets it) but it is not on disk yet; save that material (control_editor save_all with assetPaths). On UE 5.8 a material instance holds its own flags, so material can name the instance. A missing flag makes its row invalid.

maxFPS.description: Maximum frames per second; 0 for no cap.

oneOf.description: As run_script: calls the recipe may make; default 200.
Calls the script may make; default 200. Past it the script stops (SCRIPT_BUDGET) and rolls back.

maxSteps.description: As run_script: calls the recipe may make; default 200.

maxTests.description: Run at most this many of the matching tests, in the order the editor lists them (default 50, at most 200); matched says how many there were.

megaLights.description: Use MegaLights by default (UE 5.5 and later; listed under unavailable on older engines).

meshDistanceFields.description: Generate mesh distance fields, which software Lumen traces (applies after an editor restart).

metadata.description: An object of your own, such as a label or a step number, returned under metadata when includeMetadata is true; the capture itself never reads it.

minVerbosity.description: Least severe level to include (default log): error returns errors only, warning adds warnings, verbose returns everything. Editor source only; refused with the other sources.

mode.description: What to capture: editor_viewport (default, the level viewport), game_viewport (the running game frame without its UMG widgets) or full_editor_window (the editor window as displayed, game UI and asset editors included).

moduleName.description: The project module that gets the files; default the module named after the project, else its first runtime module. A wrong name lists the modules.

name.description: CVar name (alternatively cvar, key, or command).

offset.description: How many of the newest matching files to skip (default 0); pass the previous reply's nextOffset to read the next page.

outputPath.description: The folder for a packageName that is a name, or with no packageName the merged asset's /Game path.

overwrite.description: Replace a recipe of the same name (default false).

packageName.description: The merged asset: a /Game path, or a name placed in the outputPath folder (default /Game/MergedActors); the mesh is named SM_<name>.

paramNames.description: The parameter names (at most 16), each bound by run_recipe's args before the script runs.

parentClass.description: The C++ class to derive from, by name or path (Actor, Character, Pawn, ActorComponent, SceneComponent, Object, BlueprintFunctionLibrary, /Script/Engine.GameModeBase), or None for a plain C++ class. A Blueprint class is refused: derive from its C++ parent.

parentName.description: Panel to add the child under (get_widget_info lists the panels); omitted, the root panel. A name that is not a panel fails with PARENT_NOT_FOUND.

path.description: Another single asset or folder path; validated alongside assetPath when both are given.

oneOf.description: Asset paths to validate.
Several project-relative file paths to delete in one call; each gets its own entry in results. Takes precedence over path.

pluginName.description: Plugin name exactly as reported by list_plugins (the .uplugin name, not the friendly name).

pluginState.description:
Which enable plugin variant to run; omit for 'enable'.
enable: Enable a plugin for this project by writing it into the .uproject, or limit it to some build targets (targets ["Editor"] keeps an editor-only plugin out of a packaged game). A plugin on only because another plugin needs it is written into the project file. A plugin the editor has not loaded yet needs a restart, so the response reports restartRequired.
disable: Disable a plugin for this project by removing it from the .uproject. Assets that depend on it fail to load after the restart, so confirm dependents first.

poolSize.description: Streaming pool size in megabytes, at least 1, or -1 for the engine default.

profile.description: performance (Low), balanced (High, the default) or quality (Epic).

properties.description: Saved properties to set, by name, each value as list_save_games shows it ({"BestScore": 0}). All are checked before the slot is written. A slot being created may leave them out: it is written with its class defaults.

query.description: Words every listed recipe's name or summary holds.

recursive.description: For a folder path, include its subfolders (default true).

remove.description: Delete the recipe named instead of saving one (script is then not needed); RECIPE_NOT_FOUND when there is none.

replaceSourceActors.description: Place the merged mesh in the level and remove the source actors, in one undo step (default false).

resolution.description: Maximum WxH for the PNG (e.g. "1280x720"), aspect ratio kept, never upscaled. Without it an image returned inline fits 1600x900.

returnBase64.description: Return the PNG inline as an image (default true); a capture also saves a file unless keepFile is false. With no resolution, an inline image is downscaled to fit 1600x900. false returns only the saved path and metadata, at the full viewport size.

root.description: Search only this output folder (default all four).

runsBack.description: With source previous: how many editor runs back to read (default 1, max 20). After a crash and one more restart, the crashed run is 2.

saveGameClass.description: SaveGame subclass to create the slot from when it does not exist yet, such as /Game/Core/BP_Save.BP_Save_C (SaveGame itself is abstract); an existing slot keeps its own class.

scale.description: Percent of the window resolution per axis (100 is full resolution); 0 for the engine default.

script.description: The script, in run_script's language; it reads each of paramNames as a variable.

seconds.description: How long the game runs before it is closed (default 20, 5-120). Quitting or crashing sooner fails the run.

section.description: Settings section: a class path such as /Script/EngineSettings.GameMapsSettings, or its class name (GameMapsSettings).

setting.description:
Which configure display variant to run.
resolution: Set the screen resolution via the r.SetRes console command.
fullscreen: Toggle fullscreen mode via r.SetRes or r.FullScreenMode console command.
quality: Set an engine scalability quality CVar (sg.*Quality) for a category and level.
cvar: Set a console variable value, derived from name/cvar/key/command plus value.
fps: Toggle the FPS HUD overlay via the stat fps console command.
profile: Toggle a profiling stat display (CPU, GPU, memory, render/game thread) via console command.

shadows.description: Shadow map method: virtual shadow maps or classic shadow maps.

slotName.description: Slot to change, as list_save_games lists it: its file name without .sav.

snapshotPath.description: Snapshot .utrace file name, resolved inside Saved/Profiling (default a generated name).

soundPath.description: Sound asset path (default the editor CompileSuccess cue).

source.description: editor (default): the editor log. build: the UnrealBuildTool log of the last compile, where the compiler errors behind "Live coding failed" go. livecoding: the Live Coding console log (patching and linking). previous: the log of the editor's previous run, e.g. why an editor that went away exited. Only filter and lines apply to build, livecoding and previous.

startTime.description: Seconds into the sound to start playing from (default 0).

streamingDistance.description: Loading range of the first runtime grid, in cm: cells this close to a streaming source load.

subfolder.description: Folder under the module's Public (or Private) folder, such as Gameplay/Pickups; default none. A module without Public and Private folders refuses one: its own folder is no include path, so the class would not compile there.

summary.description: What the recipe does, in a sentence: search and list_recipes match its words.

targets.description: Build targets the plugin is enabled for, every other build leaving it out: ["Editor"] keeps it in the editor and out of a packaged game. An empty list lifts the limit.

timeoutSeconds.description: Stop a test still running after this many seconds and count it failed (default 60, at most 600).

traceFile.description: File mode: .utrace file name, resolved inside Saved/Profiling (default a generated McpInsights_<time>.utrace).

type.description: What to report: cpu (frame and thread times), gpu (GPU frame time) or all (default); another value is refused.

userIndex.description: User index the game saves under (default 0).

widgetId.description: Only "notification" (the default); any other value is refused.

widgetOp.description:
Which create widget variant to run; omit for 'create'.
create: Create a widget asset via the manage_widget_authoring bridge action.
add_child: Add a child widget component to a parent widget via the manage_widget_authoring bridge action.
show: Show an editor toast notification with a message; it cannot put a widget Blueprint on screen.

widgetPath.description: Full widget asset path such as /Game/UI/WBP_Menu; supplies name and savePath when they are omitted.

widgetType.description: Parent class: UserWidget (default) or another UserWidget subclass by name or path; anything else is refused.

window.description: With mode full_editor_window, which window to capture: a list index (2, or "2") or a case-insensitive substring of its title ("WBP_HubUI"). Omit for the main editor frame; responses list the open windows under windows[].

windowed.description: Show a 1280x720 window instead of rendering offscreen (default false: no window, no focus taken).
